data.title: Proximity Sensor Replacement
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro is a smartphone that has a lot of ambient sensors, such as an accelerometer, a gyroscopic sensor, and a proximity sensor. The proximity sensor is probably the most used in your iPhone. This sensor is used for turning your phone’s screen off when it is placed near your face during a phone call. So that it may conserve battery or avoid unnecessary touch inputs by your face when talking. It may also be used for features like “Raise and Wake” and other minimal yet handy features.

However, you may face problems with the proximity sensor of your iPhone 11 Pro over time. Some issues of the iPhone 11 Pro proximity sensor reported by users of the iPhone 11 Pro in the users' community are

  • The proximity sensor is not/is too sensitive. And turning the phone screen on and off during calls
  • The phone display doesn’t turn off during a phone call.
  • The phone display doesn’t turn on automatically as it should after the phone call ends.

These are the most common issues found in the iPhone 11 Pro proximity sensor. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes you may try that may solve issues regarding your proximity sensor if they are very minor. Apple recommends:

  • Try removing your screen protector, which may block the proximity sensors from working properly.
  • Restart your iPhone.
  • Update your iOS.

If you have already tried the above-mentioned fixes and none of the fixes work for you, you might need to get your phone checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing iPhones. We have service centers situated in locations around Dhaka, Bangladesh. data.description:
The new iPhone 16e comes with a lightning port which is one of the most important parts of the smartphone. However, after using the phone for a long time or by an accident; your charging dock of the phone may get faulty or damaged, and you might need to get it replaced.

The most common issues of the iPhone 16e charging dock are:

The battery charges very slowly

iPhone 16e not charging beyond 80%

Charging Not available or Liquid has been detected in the charging port error

The charging dock can’t be connected to a USB supported device through the lightning cable

If your phone has any one of these issues or something not mentioned in the list of the common issues. You will still like to check out these DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may solve the problem regarding the charging dock in your iPhone 16e.

Make sure you don’t have any debris or dirt on your charging dock. This may prevent charging

Make sure your power outlet isn’t faulty

If your phone is wet, wait until it is dry to charge your phone

Make sure you do not have the “optimized battery charging” option checked on your iPhone 16e. if you do have it make sure to disable it to charge your phone past 80%

Disable optimized Charging in here: Settings > Battery > Battery Health.

Note: This option is only available on iOS 13 or later updates.

If none of the fixes cut it for you, you may need to get your phone looked at by professionals. data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu.

This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

  • This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:
  • The iPhone has taken in some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)
  • Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss
  • A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity
  • It is rare; however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 11 pro

(Press volume up (+) and then quickly press volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 11 pro power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software. (If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, you may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work, for you. You might have an issue that needs the touch of a professional iPhone technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in fixing iPhones. ifixit bd is a prominent iPhone servicing center that is located in 4 locations around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

We offer service benefits for Apple logo issues for your iPhone 11 pro. Not only will we provide the best available service for you, but you can also avail yourself.

  • Free Diagnostics to see what's wrong with your iPhone
  • Quick service in applicable repair services
  • 30 days service warranty on applicable repairs

We understand how important your iPhone is to you, so ensure top notch quality we try to provide your servicing needs with original apple parts and accessories. We do not compromise with our quality.

data.title: Power Issue
data.description:
This correlation between the power button and the battery is unavoidable for the perfect operation of the iPhone. The iPhone has been designed to maintain it. However, many users have complained about issues regarding issues in their power supply and other power-related errors in their iPhones. These power issues include:

The phone does not turn on

The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked-out phone. Therefore you can not determine the problem

iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.

iPhone doesn’t charge. It is stuck on the battery percentage you left it to charge on.

Can’t use the iPhone without keeping it on a constant power supply (eg: Connected to a wall adapter or power bank etc.

These frustrating problems are however the most common issues found on iPhone 14 Pro. There are some widely renowned DIY (Do It Yourself) fixes available on the internet which may help with the issue on your device. Such as...

Force restart your iPhone ( Press Volume up (+) and quickly press volume down (-) and then quickly press the power button to complete the restart process)

Check your Lightning cable and adapter to see if they are functioning properly

Check if there is any debris on the iPhone 14 Pro charging porthole

Limit background processes by stopping background app refresh

Try charging for 20 minutes while keeping your phone switched off

Sometimes excessive battery drain can happen due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version

If none of these methods work to resolve the issue on your smartphone, you might need to get it checked by professional technicians.iFixit bd is an iPhone servicing center located around 4 different service points around Dhaka, Bangladesh. We provide the best iPhone servicing support in Bangladesh.

data.description:
It is quite frustrating when you see there’s no network bar/ Wi-Fi signal strong enough near you. We use our phones mostly to stay connected with others most of the time, and problems like that keep us from staying connected. You may face a similar kind of problem with your iPhone 14 Pro Max. This usually happens after a faulty or incomplete update where you might see this: There’s no network bar available at the top of the display. Restarting or reinstalling the SIM card doesn’t help. There is always “Searching” shown on the network bar. There is no Cellular connection available for your phone. You can’t turn on, discover, or connect to available wireless Hotspot networks available near you through your iPhone 14 Pro Max.

You can’t connect to your Bluetooth devices like Apple Watch, Bluetooth headphones, and stereo speakers through your phone. It appears that you cannot connect to anything wireless through your iPhone 14 Pro Max. If you are facing this issue go to Settings > General > About and see if you can find information regarding IMEI, Bluetooth location, Modem Firmware, etc. If there is nothing there then you are having an issue with the modem firmware

There are no DIY (Do It Yourself) fixes available for this issue. You are going to be needing to take your iPhone 14 Pro Max to an expert repair technician to resolve the “No modem firmware” issue. data.description:
The new iPhone 12 mini has a beautiful battery that is optimized for using it for a reasonable amount of time. However, most of the users have complained the iPhone 12 mini charges very slowly in comparison to other smartphones on the market with almost the same range. The Apple company, recommends that you use an Apple 18-W USB Type-C charging brick if you face a slow charging issue. Which is the default charger with iPhone 12 mini. Apple claims this charging brick can shoot your charging time up to 50% in 30 minutes only!

However, even with an 18-W charger, some users face issues while charging their iPhone 12 mini. The most common issues are as follows:

The iPhone 12 mini charges slowly or not at all

The iPhone is not charging beyond 80 %

An alert that shows that the accessory you are using to charge the iPhone is not certified or supported

These are the most reported issues for an iPhone 12 mini with faulty charging. You may try some home fixes that may resolve the issues.

Try changing the wall adapter or cable

Check if there is no debris or dirt in both the charging dock and the charging adapter

Make sure the USB is connected firmly on both ends

Check the charging adapter or the lightning cable for visible signs of damage. Example: Bent pin, loose cable, etc.

if you have iOS 14 or above make sure you uncheck the “optimized battery charging” option to make sure it charges beyond 80 %.

To disable it go to: Settings > Battery > Battery Health > Optimized Battery Charging

Make sure you have no damage in your charging dock if unsupported device warning shows.

If none of the fixes seem to work for resolving your iPhone 11 pro charging issues. You may need to get it looked at by professionals. data.title: Proximity Sensor Replacement
data.description:
The proximity sensor is probably the most used on your iPhone. This sensor is used for turning your phone’s screen off when it is placed near your face during a phone call. So that it may conserve battery or avoid unnecessary touch inputs by your face when talking. It may also be used for features like “Raise and Wake” and other minimal yet handy features.

However, you may face problems with the proximity sensor of your iPhone 16 over time. Some issues with the iPhone 16 proximity sensor reported by users of the iPhone 16 in the users' community are:

  • The proximity sensor is not working/ too sensitive. And turning the phone screen on and off during calls
  • The phone display doesn’t turn off during a phone call
  • The phone display doesn’t turn on automatically as it should after the phone call ends

These are the most common issues found in the iPhone 16 proximity sensor. There are some DIY (do it yourself) fixes you may try which may solve issues regarding your proximity sensor if they are very minor. Apple recommends:

  • Update your iOS
  • Restart your iPhone
  • Try removing your screen protector, which may block the proximity sensors' proper working
  • If you have already tried the above-mentioned fixes and none of the fixes work for you, you might need to get your phone checked by a professional technician.

data.description:
The new iPhone 12 Pro Max comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way

Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts

If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all

data.description:
The new iPhone 11 pro max offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu.

  • This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.
  • This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:
  • The iPhone has taken in some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)
  • Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss
  • A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity
  • It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up


These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 11 pro max

(Press volume up (+) and then quickly press volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 11 pro max power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

data.title: Mic Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 13 Mini offers a set of microphones to ensure your iPhone makes the best out of the audio inputs it receives. The iPhone offers the users a mono speaker and microphone to ensure the best listening experience for their users. However, it is often reported by iPhone 13 Mini users that, they are getting trouble regarding the microphones in their phones. The most common issues reported in Apple’s user community forum and other blogs are:

Low or unclear voice sound in voice calls/ voice memos.

Low or unclear voice in Facetime, skype, or video recording.

Muffled or cracked sound while recording/calling using the mic.

Siri doesn’t work/ can’t hear me/ can’t pick up commands.

The iPhone 13 Mini has at least 3 different microphones in different places for phone for different purposes.

The bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls

One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri

The one in the back of your in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video.

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any of the one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

Make sure if you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes.

Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there.

Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works

If the mic works in voice memo make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone 13 Mini go to: Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone.

If none of the fixes work for you, you may need it to be looked at by professional technicians. data.description:
The new iPhone 13 Pro Max has a new wireless firmware that can support up to 7GHz of wireless bandwidth speed. This gives the users unmatched speed in comparison to most of the smartphones in the market. However, there have been issues regarding the Wi-Fi of the iPhone 13 Pro Max. Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone 13  Pro Max

Wi-Fi stays connected but there is no internet on the receiver

Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/ non-metered connections on Wi-Fi

iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi

These Wi-Fi issues found on iPhone 13 Pro Max are pretty common issues found on other wireless supported devices too! There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issue has been resolved

Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again

Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection

Restore the default network connection

(Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > * Enter Passcode * > Confirm)

Update your iOS to the latest version available

If none of the solutions mentioned above work to resolve your Wi-Fi issue on your iPhone 13 Pro Max, you may need to get it checked by a professional technician. data.description:
The iPhone 13 Mini offers the users a new iOS version (iOS 13 upgradable to iOS 14) and updates it forward. Users need to update iOS regularly to maintain the stable and smooth operation of the iPhone. However, sometimes a user may face some unforeseen problems. Like the Boot loop in this instance, where the phone starts and shows the Apple logo. Then goes black and again shows only the apple logo on the screen, the phone can show nothing beyond that.

This issue happens mostly when there is a failed or interrupted software update happens on your phone. Also, other issues may cause your phone to boot loop such as:

Hardware Damage

Physical Damage (Dropping the phone from your hand, etc.)

Battery connector may have gotten loose or have gone bad

Improper or failed update that is missing necessary files to get the phone started

If you think one of the above issues is causing the boot looping error on your phone, you may just try these fixes listed below and see if they work to resolve your issue.

Force Restart Your iPhone 13 Mini

(press the volume up button (+) then release the button. And then quickly press and release the volume down (-) and then hold the power button again until your screen turns black and shows the apple logo)

Check if your iPhone is fully charged or is charging properly.

Connect your iPhone to your computer and try restoring or updating the software through the iTunes application.

If your phone still doesn’t recover from boot looing after trying these fixes, something may have gone wrong which can only be fixed by a professional iPhone technician. data.title: Network Problem
data.description:
The iPhone 7 comes with upgraded network connectivity than the previous iPhone models and supports 4G network connectivity. Despite these technological advancements from the previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone 7’s network connectivity. Such as loss in the network, prompt disconnections, inability to find or locate the network.

The most common issues however are often discussed upon Apple’s user forum and the most common problems found regarding network in iPhone 7 are:

  • iPhone 7 gets down to 0 network bars randomly
  • Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G.
  • Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company.
  • Network never reaches the full level.

These common issues however can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 7. To resolve these Apple recommends its iPhone 7 users some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

  • Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache.
  • Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. (requires a restart of the device)
  • Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.
  • To set up go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network

then:

  • Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier 
  • Insert Username (provided by your carrier)
  • Insert Password (provided by your carrier)
  • Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.
  • Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.
  • Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)
  • Restart your iPhone
  • Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to get checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving your network issues in your iPhone 7. ifixit bd has 4 service points which are located in points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Screen cracking more easily due to the ultra-thin chassis

USB-C on the iPhone Air is the single port for both charging and data. Daily cable insertion on an ultra-thin device puts more mechanical stress on the port mounting point than on thicker iPhones. Intermittent charging and loose connectors are early signs of port wear. iPhone Air charging issues

The iPhone XS is a pretty sturdy phone considering gorilla glass in both the front and back. So, if you, somehow, have managed to get your back part (housing) damaged. Damages to the housing may include...

  • Deformation of the housing
  • Housing breaking into pieces
  • Visible scratches and dents
  • Loosening of the adhesive that holds the housing

Any sort of damage or deformation on the back housing of the iPhone XS indicates that it might lead to an internal issue in the future. Also, a damaged back housing may harm your inner parts, like the battery, display, and other peripherals of your iPhone. An iPhone XS is IP68 rated, which means it is water- and dustproof. However, it can’t protect your phone from dust and water with damaged housing. And in that sense, the housing of the iPhone XS serves more purpose than just visual aesthetics.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone SE 2020 is not a standard IP68 rated, dust and water-resistant phone. Which means it can not resist dust and water coming in up to it. However, it can resist certain levels of water. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

  • If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:
  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY
  • If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.
  • If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers.

data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues, however, have some home remedies that may work for your iPhone. These fixed attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.

Make sure you are facing the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID, instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

data.description:

Turn off background iCloud/iTunes sync to save battery by a considerable amount

When not in use turn off WiFi/Cellular Data/Location/Bluetooth service in your iPhone

Turn on optimized battery charging to save your battery life and protect it from draining

Adjust your brightness settings in iPhone 12 to auto-brightness

Turn off Background app refresh

From here: Settings > general > Background app refresh

Try running it on low power mode

from here: Settings > Battery > Low power mode ON

Turn off “reduce motion” to turn off aesthetic animations in your phone to save battery life might help

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage. If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY
  • If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.

If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers. data.title: Network Problem
data.description:
The iPhone Se 2022 comes with upgraded network connectivity compared to previous iPhone models and supports 5G network connectivity. Despite technological advancements from previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone Se 2022 network connectivity. Such as loss of the network, prompt disconnections, and inability to find or locate the network.

The most common issues, however, are often discussed on Apple’s user forum and the most common problems found regarding networks in iPhone Se 2022 are:

iPhone Se 2022 gets down to 0 network bars randomly

Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G

Network never reaches the full level

Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company

These common issues, however, can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone Se 2022. To resolve this, Apple recommends its iPhone Se 2022 users some DIY (do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache

Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. -requires a restart of the device

Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.

To set it up, go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network.

then:

Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier

Insert Username (provided by your carrier)

Insert Password (provided by your carrier)

Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.

Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.

Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)

Restart your iPhone

Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to be checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving your network issues with your iPhone Se 2022. ifixit bd has 4 service points which are located in points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Power Issue
data.description:
This correlation between the power button and the battery is unavoidable for the perfect operation of the iPhone. The iPhone has been designed to maintain it. However, many users have complained about issues regarding issues in their power supply and other power-related errors in their iPhones.

Phone does not turn on

The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked-out phone. Therefore you can not determine the problem

iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.

iPhone doesn’t charge. It is stuck on the battery percentage you left it to charge on.

Can’t use the iPhone without keeping it on a constant power supply (eg: Connected to a wall adapter or power bank etc.

These frustrating problems are however the most common issues found on iPhone 13 . There are some widely renowned DIY (Do It Yourself) fixes available on the internet which may help with the issue on your device. Such as...

Force restart your iPhone ( Press Volume up (+) and quickly press volume down (-) and then quickly press the power button to complete the restart process)

Check your Lightning cable and adapter to see if they are functioning properly

Check if there is any debris on the iPhone 13 charging porthole

Limit background processes by stopping background app refresh

Try charging for 20 minutes while keeping your phone switched off

Sometimes excessive battery drain can happen due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version

If none of these methods work to resolve the issue on your smartphone, you might need to get it checked by professional technicians. ifixit bd is an iPhone servicing center located around 4 different service points around Dhaka, Bangladesh. data.title: Taptic Engine Issue
data.description:
The Taptic Engine in an iPhone Xs is responsible for providing haptic feedback, such as vibrations for notifications and the "click" sensation for the home button (on supported models). You might need to replace the Taptic Engine in your iPhone if you experience any of the following issues:

Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:

  • If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.
  • The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.
  • The Taptic Engine produces grinding or buzzing noises that were not present before.
  • Error messages or diagnostics indicate an issue with the Taptic Engine.

Possible Causes of Failure:

  • Physical Damage: Dropping the phone or exposing it to water can damage internal components.
  • Software Bugs: Sometimes, a software issue may mimic hardware failure. Perform a factory reset or update the iPhone before deciding on hardware repair.
  • Wear and Tear: Over time, mechanical components can degrade and stop working properly.

iPhone 12 Pro gets down to 0 network bars randomly

Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G

Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company

Network never reaches the full level

These common issues however can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 12 Pro. To resolve these Apple recommends its iPhone 12 Pro users some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache

Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. (requires a restart of the device)

Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.

To set up go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network

then:

Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier

Insert Username (provided by your carrier)

Insert Password (provided by your carrier)

Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.

Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.

Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)

Restart your iPhone

Soft reset your iPhone

data.title: Temperature High Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 13 Mini comes with a generally better and more efficient better processor and battery than the iPhone X series. However, users have said that the phone tends to get hotter than the previous iPhones Apple has released. The new iPhone 13 Mini comes with a special thermal compound in the back area of the phone which helps to omit heat faster and more efficiently than previous iPhones. It may make your iPhone seem a lot hotter than the previous iPhones.

However, that doesn’t make the iPhone 13 mini so warm that the users find it difficult to hold it down with their hands. This is a clear indication of overheating in the iPhone 13 mini. Some similar cases of overheating include:

Phone gets way too hot while charging and takes a long time to be fully charged

The phone gets hot and the battery drains drastically

You might see a notification that will say “Temperature high”

The iPhone gets warm in standby mode for no apparent reason whatsoever

(Note: if your phone gets too hot while transferring data for the first time from a previous iPhone, chances are it’s a one-time issue and will not happen again.)

These are some of the most discussed problems in Apple’s user threads and community. However, there are some DIY (Do it Yourself) fixes that you may try which may help you to resolve your overheating issues.

Disable background app refresh.

Disable background app refresh from here: Settings > General > Background App Refresh

Turn off Bluetooth / Location services to reduce processes running in the background

Most of the users have reported that they are getting the heating issue in the latest iOS version, In that case

try updating your iOS to later versions to check if it works for your phone.

If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get it looked at by professional technicians who specialize in resolving iPhone 13 mini heating issues. What are the common iPhone 13 Pro Max problems we fix?

Battery capacity dropping after years of daily use

The iPhone 13 Pro Max battery was one of the largest ever fitted to an iPhone at launch — but after 4+ years of charge cycles, capacity has degraded significantly for most users. Unexpected shutdowns, short on-time, and slow performance throttling are all signs of a battery that needs replacing. This is the single most common repair we perform on this model. iPhone 13 Pro Max battery replacement

Cracked ProMotion OLED display

The 6.7-inch 120Hz ProMotion OLED is the centrepiece of this phone. OLED damage — dead pixel columns, green lines, touch dead zones — removes the display experience that defines the 13 Pro Max. We replace the full assembly and verify ProMotion refresh rate and Face ID sensor alignment after every repair. iPhone 13 Pro Max screen replacement

Triple camera malfunction — blur, LiDAR failure, or lens switching

The three-lens system — wide, ultrawide, telephoto — plus LiDAR scanner is a complex optical and electronic assembly. Drops that impact the raised camera island, OIS mechanical damage, and flex cable wear all cause blur, autofocus failure, and LiDAR-dependent AR errors. We diagnose each module independently. iPhone 13 Pro Max camera repair

Lightning port charging intermittently

Four years of daily cable use packs lint into the Lightning port. Intermittent charging, cables that only work at certain angles, and complete charging failure are all common. We clean during every free diagnosis — flex cable replacement only when the cable is confirmed physically damaged. iPhone 13 Pro Max charging issues

Battery completely depleted — replacement is essential

A 10–12 year old lithium-ion cell holds almost no practical charge. iPhone 6 Plus batteries in service today require immediate replacement for any continued use — this is not a question of "when" but "now." iPhone 6 Plus battery replacement

Cracked 5.5-inch LCD screen

The 5.5-inch Retina HD LCD display shows standard LCD damage after cracks — white backlight spots, touch dead zones, and dark bleed patches. Full display assembly replacement restores complete function. iPhone 6 Plus screen replacement

Touch Disease — flickering grey bar and unresponsive touch

The iPhone 6 Plus has a known board-level fault called Touch Disease. This is not a screen fault — it is a logic board fault requiring micro-soldering re-work to fix. iFixit BD's board-level lab addresses Touch Disease directly. iPhone 6 Plus Touch Disease repair

Touch ID home button not working

Mechanical failure, touch sensor degradation, and broken pairing from prior repairs all cause Touch ID failure. iFixit BD restores Touch ID function where the board-level pairing is intact. iPhone 6 Plus home button / Touch ID repair

Lightning port completely worn after 10 years

A decade of daily cable connections has worn the Lightning port pins past usability. Port cleaning alone cannot restore function at this age — flex cable replacement is required. iPhone 6 Plus charging issues

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service restores your damaged handset to full working order through diagnostics, component replacement, and function testing. The service covers screen repair, battery replacement, charging port repair, back glass replacement, camera repair, Face ID repair, speaker and microphone repair, water damage repair, logic board repair, and software fault repair.

Repair costs sit in three tiers. Entry-level jobs like a charging port cleanup cost the least, mid-level jobs like a battery replacement land in the middle, and premium jobs like an OLED display swap cost the most. Screen replacement pricing follows the same three tiers.

Turnaround times vary by repair type. A battery swap wraps up same day, while logic board and water damage work takes longer because part availability drives the schedule.

You pick the replacement part grade before work starts. New genuine parts, used genuine parts, OEM-grade parts, and certified after-market parts each carry a different price and a different effect on parts and service history reporting. Every repair ships with a parts and labor warranty.

Booking takes six steps, starting with a free diagnostic and ending when you collect a function-tested device. Walk in or reserve your slot ahead — booking ahead locks in the part you need.

What is an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service is a technical service that diagnoses faults in an Apple iPhone 16 Pro Max, replaces the failed component, and verifies device function before handover. The service addresses display faults, power faults, camera faults, audio faults, liquid damage, and board-level faults. Every repair starts with a free diagnostic check that identifies the failed component before you approve any cost. Each completed repair passes a function test that confirms the repaired component and the surrounding systems operate correctly.

The iPhone 16 Pro Max repairs covered by this service are listed below.

  • iPhone 16 Pro Max screen repair — Replaces the cracked or unresponsive 6.9-inch LTPO OLED display assembly and calibrates True Tone, brightness, and touch response after fitting.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max battery replacement — Installs a new battery when battery health drops below 80 percent, then calibrates the cell so battery health reporting reads accurately.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max charging port repair — Restores the USB-C connector when the device charges intermittently, rejects accessories, or stops recognizing a cable.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max back glass replacement — Replaces the cracked rear glass panel and reseals the housing so the device retains its water resistance rating.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max camera repair — Replaces the rear camera module, front camera assembly, LiDAR sensor, or camera lens when images blur, shake, or fail to focus.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max facial recognition repair — Restores the TrueDepth camera and dot projector so Face ID authenticates, unlocks the device, and authorizes Apple Pay.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max speaker repair — Replaces the loudspeaker or earpiece when call audio distorts, media playback crackles, or one channel goes silent.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max microphone repair — Replaces the microphone assembly when callers hear you faintly, voice memos record silence, or Siri stops responding.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max water damage repair — Removes corrosion from the board with ultrasonic cleaning, replaces oxidized components, and restores the affected circuits.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max logic board repair — Repairs the failed integrated circuit at chip level when the device shows a boot loop, no power, or no display output.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max software fault repair — Recovers iOS when the device sticks on the Apple logo, restarts repeatedly, or fails a firmware update.

How much does an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair cost?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair costs between BDT 2,500 and BDT 55,000, depending on the failed component and the replacement part grade you select. The component determines the base cost, and the part grade adjusts it. You receive a written quotation after the free diagnostic, and that figure holds through the repair.

Entry-level repairs cost between BDT 2,500 and BDT 6,000. This tier covers charging port cleaning, speaker replacement, microphone replacement, button repair, and software fault recovery. These repairs use inexpensive components and finish quickly.

Mid-level repairs cost between BDT 7,000 and BDT 18,000. This tier covers battery replacement, charging port replacement, rear camera replacement, front camera replacement, and back glass replacement. These repairs use moderately priced modules and require housing disassembly.

Premium repairs cost between BDT 20,000 and BDT 55,000. This tier covers OLED display replacement, Face ID and TrueDepth camera repair, water damage restoration, and logic board repair. Display assemblies and board-level work carry the highest component and labor cost on the iPhone 16 Pro Max.

You confirm the exact figure for your device during the free diagnostic, since the same symptom sometimes traces to different components.

How much does an iPhone 16 Pro Max screen replacement cost?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max screen replacement costs between BDT 18,000 and BDT 52,000, depending on the display grade you select. The 6.9-inch LTPO OLED panel is the most expensive single component in the device, which places every screen replacement in the upper cost range.

An entry-level screen replacement costs between BDT 18,000 and BDT 24,000. This tier uses a certified after-market OLED assembly that restores display output and touch response at the lowest cost.

A mid-level screen replacement costs between BDT 26,000 and BDT 38,000. This tier uses an OEM-grade or used genuine display that matches original color accuracy and supports the ProMotion refresh rate.

A premium screen replacement costs between BDT 40,000 and BDT 52,000. This tier uses a new genuine Apple display that preserves True Tone, adaptive color temperature, Always-On display behavior, and clean parts and service history reporting.

You keep Face ID after any of these three grades, because the technician transfers the original TrueDepth assembly to the new display.

Which replacement parts are used for an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair?

The replacement part grades used for an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair are listed below.

  • New genuine manufacturer parts — Factory-new Apple components that deliver original performance and clean parts and service history reporting.
  • Used genuine manufacturer parts — Tested Apple components harvested from donor devices, offering genuine performance at reduced cost.
  • Original equipment manufacturer grade parts — Components built to Apple's specification by the same suppliers, matching original tolerances and materials.
  • Certified after-market parts — Independently manufactured components that pass quality certification and carry the same repair warranty.

You confirm the part grade in writing before the repair begins, so the quoted price and the fitted component always match. Genuine parts preserve adaptive color temperature, True Tone calibration, and accurate battery health reporting in Settings.

How long does an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair take?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair takes 30 minutes to 5 working days. Component replacements finish within the same day, while board-level work extends across several days. Turnaround depends on part availability more than on repair difficulty, so a stocked display fits faster than a special-order camera module. Logic board repair and water damage repair take longer than component replacement, because both require diagnosis at circuit level, ultrasonic cleaning, micro-soldering, and staged testing between each step.

Repair typeTypical turnaround timeSame-day availabilityScreen replacement45 to 90 minutesYesBattery replacement30 to 60 minutesYesCharging port repair60 to 120 minutesYesSpeaker or microphone repair45 to 90 minutesYesCamera repair60 to 120 minutesYesBack glass replacement2 to 4 hoursYesFace ID repair3 to 6 hoursYesSoftware fault repair1 to 3 hoursYesWater damage repair2 to 4 working daysNoLogic board repair2 to 5 working daysNo

You receive a turnaround estimate in writing alongside your quotation, and the service desk updates you when a repair moves between stages. Verify current figures against your own service records before publishing, since part supply changes turnaround ranges over time.

Does an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair include a warranty?

Yes, an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair includes a warranty. Every repair carries parts and labor coverage that runs from the collection date. The warranty covers component failure and workmanship faults on the repaired part. Coverage applies to the specific component replaced during the repair, and the service desk records the covered part and the coverage period on your invoice at handover.

How do you book an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service?

You book an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service by describing the fault, requesting a free diagnostic, approving the written quotation, and confirming a collection time. Our service center operates in Dhaka and covers customers across Bangladesh, including Gulshan, Banani, Dhanmondi, Uttara, Mirpur, and Mohakhali. Walk-in service runs during business hours, and booking ahead reserves the specific part your repair requires. You back up the device to iCloud or a computer before handover, since board-level and water damage repairs sometimes affect stored data.

The steps to book an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service are outlined below.

  1. Describe the fault and request a free diagnostic — Report the symptom by phone, message, or in person, and the technician runs Apple Diagnostics to identify the failed component.

  6. Collect the device after function testing — Inspect the repaired component, verify the function test results, and receive your warranty invoice at handover.

Your iPhone 16 Pro Max deserves a repair that holds up. Book your free diagnostic today and get a written price before anyone opens your device.

What are the common iPhone 12 Mini problems we fix?

Battery — the most critical fault on this model

The iPhone 12 Mini has a very small battery relative to its screen size and chip demands. Battery life was limited even at full health — and after 5+ years of degradation, most 12 Mini batteries are significantly below useful capacity. Battery replacement is urgent and transformative on this device. iPhone 12 Mini battery replacement

Cracked compact OLED screen

The 5.4-inch Super Retina XDR OLED panel is beautiful but fragile. Small phones are often used without cases — more drops, more cracked screens. OLED damage requires full assembly replacement to resolve. iPhone 12 Mini screen replacement

MagSafe back glass cracked

The glass back enables MagSafe and wireless charging. Rear drops crack it and impair charger alignment. iFixit BD replaces back glass as a standalone repair. iPhone 12 Mini back glass repair

Main camera blur or OIS failure

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water. However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • Never charge your phone until you have made sure it is completely dry.

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth. If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers. data.title: Network Problem
data.description:
The iPhone 8 Plus comes with upgraded network connectivity than the previous iPhone models and supports 4G network connectivity. Despite these technological advancements from the previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone 8 plus’s network connectivity. Such as loss in the network, prompt disconnections, inability to find or locate the network.

The most common issues however are often discussed upon Apple’s user forum and the most common problems found regarding networks in iPhone 8 plus are:

  • iPhone 8 plus gets down to 0 network bars randomly
  • Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G.
  • Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company.
  • Network never reaches the full level.


These common issues however can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 8 plus. To resolve these Apple recommends its iPhone 8 plus users some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

  • Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache.
  • Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. (requires a restart of the device)
  • Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.
  • To set up go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network

then:

  • Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier
  • Insert Username (provided by your carrier)
  • Insert Password (provided by your carrier)
  • Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.
  • Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.
  • Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)
  • Restart your iPhone
  • Soft reset your iPhone


If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to get checked by a professional technician. data.title: Touch Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 13 offers a haptic touch system instead of a 3D touch system that was available in the previous versions of the iPhones. The new haptic touch does not require assessing the strength of users like it needed to in the 3D touch system. Instead, it measures the area of your fingertips to decide the strength and length of the touch input provided by the user. This haptic touch is also a way to ensure your touch works for a long time. However, you might just face an issue anytime soon on your iPhone 13 regarding your phone’s touch.

The most common issues faced by users that are reported in the iPhone 13 user community forum are as follows:

Very sensitive screen/screen response intermittently (means responses without the user having to input or auto touch)

Touch doesn’t respond after dropping from hand. (Everything else seems to be working fine)

Touch screen in your iPhone does not respond at all

Delayed Touch issue

There are some fixes you might try to see if any of them work for your phone. They are listed below:

Make sure your touch screen protector doesn’t interfere with the proper operation

Make sure there’s no internal/external damage (cracking or shattering glass)

Disconnect your USB-lightning port to check if it works

If your phone is above normal temperature, wait for it to cool down and then try again

Restart your device

If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get your iPhone checked by professional technicians. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving issues regarding touch on your iPhone 13. ifixit bd is located in 4 different service points. which are in convenient locations for you around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Touch Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 14 Plus offers a haptic touch system instead of a 3D touch system that was available in the previous versions of the iPhones. The new haptic touch does not require assessing the strength of users like it needed to in the 3D touch system. Instead, it measures the area of your fingertips to decide the strength and length of the touch input provided by the user. This haptic touch is also a way to ensure your touch works for a long time. However, you might just face an issue anytime soon on your iPhone 14 Plus regarding your phone’s touch.

The most common issues faced by users that are reported in the iPhone 14 Plus user community forum are as follows:

Delayed Touch issue

Touch screen in your iPhone does not respond at all

Touch doesn’t respond after dropping from hand. (Everything else seems to be working fine)

Very sensitive screen/screen response intermittently (means responses without the user having to input or auto touch)

There are some fixes you might try to see if any of them work for your phone. They are listed below:

Make sure your touchscreen protector doesn’t interfere with the proper operation

Make sure there’s no internal/external damage (cracking or shattering glass)

Disconnect your USB-lightning port to check if it works

If your phone is above normal temperature, wait for it to cool down and then try again

Restart your device

If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get your iPhone checked by professional technicians. Here at iFixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving issues regarding touch on your iPhone 14 Plus. iFixit bd is located in 4 different service points. which are in convenient locations for you around Dhaka, Bangladesh.   • The battery of the iPhone 11 pro runs out after installing an app/ update of an app

These are the most common problems regarding battery-draining found on the internet. Your issues may be one of them or not listed! However, we recommend trying some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may resolve your issue.

  • Don’t overcharge/ Frequently charge your iPhone 11 pro. It may reduce battery health
  • Turn on optimized battery charging to save your battery life and protect it from draining
  • Adjust your brightness settings in iPhone 11 pro to auto-brightness
  • Turn off Background app refresh
  • From here: Settings > general > Background app refresh
  • Try running it on low power mode
  • from here: Settings > Battery > Low power mode ON
  • Turn off “reduce motion” to turn off aesthetic animations in your phone to save battery life might help
  • Turn it off from here: Settings > General > Accessibility > Reduce Motion

If none of the aforementioned procedures work to resolve your battery draining issues, it may need to be looked at by a professional technician to get them resolved. Apple has introduced an exclusive feature of Touch ID since the iPhone 5s. It is a fingerprint sensor that lets users of the iPhone 8 plus unlock their iPhone without having to put in a passcode every time they do so. However, like all the other technical difficulties you may face in your iPhone; your fingerprint/touch-id may cause an error in its operation. The most common issues faced regarding touch ID are:

  • You are asked to enter the passcode to unlock the phone by default instead of Touch ID
  • You can not avail of Apple Payment by touch-ID.
  • Can’t Register Touch ID to set up your fingerprint.
  • Touch ID is grayed or dimmed out.

Apple recommends some fixes you may try in your home which may fix the issue if it is due to a software glitch. Those fixes are:

  • Make sure your hands are clean and dry. Different sorts of moisturizers may affect the workability of your iPhone. (Such as Oil, lotion, sweat, or water)
  • Make sure your iPhone touch ID is clean and wipe it down with a lint-free cloth.
  • Make sure you put your entire finger on the home button to make the sensor work.
  • Make sure your screen protector or case is not getting in the way of touch ID
  • Update your iOS

Also, make sure that Touch ID does not work if you have...

  • Restarted your phone
  • You haven’t unlocked your device in 48 hours
  • 5 failed attempts to unlock the phone through touch ID.

data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 12 Pro comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

  • The face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

  • These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way

Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

  • If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts

If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all

If your iPhone 12 Pro Face ID problems can’t be categorized and sorted by the above-mentioned issues and fixes, you may just need to take it to an extremely diligent iPhone technician to deal with Face ID issues. repair_info.image_alt_text: iPhone 13 Pro Max Face ID Issue

data.description:
The new iPhone 13 Pro Max comes with a distinct feature called Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues, however, have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fixed attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.

Make sure you are facing the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID, instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked with face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts

If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all

If your iPhone 13 Pro Max Face ID problems can’t be categorized and sorted by the above-mentioned issues and fixes, you may just need to take it to an extremely diligent iPhone technician to deal with Face ID issues. data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone XR is a standard IP68-rated, dust- and water-resistant phone. This means it can resist dust and water coming in up to a certain level. However, it is not completely immune to water getting inside the iPhone and damaging it. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the SIM tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the SIM tray by putting the ejector pin into the SIM tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the SIM tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the SIM tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver, then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red, you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

  • If you have dropped your phone in the water, here are some basic things you should do:
  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth.
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY.
  • If anything spills on your phone (like oil, etc.), just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.

If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your battery or charging port or give you muffled speakers. data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

The iPhone has taken in some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

The update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss.

A third-party app may have access to vital permissions which can disrupt iPhones' productivity.

It is rare; however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up.

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 11

(Press volume up (+) and then quickly press volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 11 power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, you may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work, for you. You might have an issue that needs the touch of a professional iPhone technician. data.title: Taptic Engine Replace
data.description:
The Taptic Engine in an iPhone 8 is responsible for providing haptic feedback, such as vibrations for notifications and the "click" sensation for the home button (on supported models). You might need to replace the Taptic Engine in your iPhone if you experience any of the following issues:

  • Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:
  • If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.
  • The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.
  • The Taptic Engine produces grinding or buzzing noises that were not present before.
  • Error messages or diagnostics indicate an issue with the Taptic Engine.

Possible Causes of Failure:

  • Physical Damage: Dropping the phone or exposing it to water can damage internal components.
  • Software Bugs: Sometimes, a software issue may mimic hardware failure. Perform a factory reset or update the iPhone before deciding on hardware repair.
  • Wear and Tear: Over time, mechanical components can degrade and stop working properly.

data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone. Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues, however, have some home remedies that may work for your iPhone. These fixed attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.

Make sure you are facing the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID, instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked with face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts

If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all

data.title: Charge Draining Issue
data.description:
The battery is optimized perfectly for the phone. However, it may be due to some manufacturer error or something about some faulty app optimization, you may not get the smoothest output from your iPhone 13 battery. Most users have reported that the iPhone’s battery starts draining after the system has updated to iOS 14 Several other issues may also cause battery drain issues. These issues include:

  • The battery of the iPhone 13 runs out too quickly after the update
  • The battery of the iPhone 13 battery runs out after installing app/ update of app
  • The battery of the iPhone drains quickly after turning on the optimized charging mode
  • iPhone Battery drains after phone heats up too quickly

These are the most common problems regarding battery-draining found on the internet. Your issue may be one of the ones listed! However, we recommend trying some DIY (do it yourself) fixes that may resolve your issue.

  • Turn off background iCloud/iTunes sync to save battery by a considerable amount
  • When not in use, turn off WiFi/Cellular Data/Location/Bluetooth service on your iPhone
  • Don’t overcharge/ Frequently charge your iPhone 13 It may reduce battery health
  • Turn on optimized battery charging to save your battery life and protect it from draining
  • Adjust the brightness settings on your iPhone 13 to auto-brightness
  • Turn off Background app refresh. From here: Settings > general > Background app refresh
  • Try running it on low power mode from here: Settings > Battery > Low power mode ON.
  • Turn off “reduce motion” to turn off esthetic animations in your phone to save battery life might help.
  • Turn it off from here: Settings > General > Accessibility > Reduce Motion

If none of the aforementioned procedures work to resolve your battery draining issues, they may need to be looked at by a professional technician to get them resolved. data.title: Proximity Sensor Replacement
data.description:
The new iPhone 13 mini is a smartphone that has a lot of ambient sensors such as an accelerometer, a gyroscopic sensor, and a proximity sensor. The proximity sensor is probably the most used on your iPhone. This sensor is used for turning your phone’s screen off when it is placed near your face during a phone call. So that it may conserve battery or avoid unnecessary touch inputs by your face when talking. It may also be used for features like “Raise and Wake” and other minimal yet handy features.

However, you may face problems with the proximity sensor of your iPhone 13 Mini over time. Some issues with the iPhone 13 mini proximity sensor reported by users of the iPhone 13 mini in the users' community are:

The proximity sensor is not working/ too sensitive. And turning the phone screen on and off during calls

The phone display doesn’t turn off during a phone call

The phone display doesn’t turn on automatically as it should after the phone call ends

These are the most common issues found in the iPhone 13 mini proximity sensor. There are some DIY (do it yourself) fixes you may try which may solve issues regarding your proximity sensor if they are very minor. Apple recommends:

Try removing your screen protector, which may block the proximity sensors' proper working

Restart your iPhone

Update your iOS

If you have already tried the above-mentioned fixes and none of the fixes work for you, you might need to get your phone checked by a professional technician.

data.description:
The new iPhone 12 offers one of the best displays consisting of a Super AMOLED retina display and a significantly high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both the back and front. However, not all damage in display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone 12 have reported a sudden black screen without any prior damage history. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 12 is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs.

But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

The Phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus) 

The phone has calls, notifications but doesn’t show anything on display

iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone. (Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen) 

Connect the lightning cable, charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone

UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issue. It might be risky for any layman person. 

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving No light on display issues on your iPhone 12. The Taptic Engine in an iPhone Xs is responsible for providing haptic feedback, such as vibrations for notifications and the "click" sensation for the home button (on supported models). You might need to replace the Taptic Engine in your iPhone if you experience any of the following issues:

Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:

  • If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.
  • The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.
  • The Taptic Engine produces grinding or buzzing noises that were not present before.
  • Error messages or diagnostics indicate an issue with the Taptic Engine.

Possible Causes of Failure:

  • Physical Damage: Dropping the phone or exposing it to water can damage internal components.
  • Software Bugs: Sometimes, a software issue may mimic hardware failure. Perform a factory reset or update the iPhone before deciding on hardware repair.
  • Wear and Tear: Over time, mechanical components can degrade and stop working properly.

Battery in critical condition after 7+ years

The iPhone Xs Max's dual camera system powers Portrait Mode. Telephoto lens failure from a drop, OIS wear, and flex cable damage degrade Portrait Mode and zoom quality. [→ iPhone Xs Max camera repair]

Lightning port worn after 7 years of daily use
