iPhone Air original battery

This is a genuine Apple battery for the iPhone Air (iPhone Air) — the original 3,149 mAh lithium-ion cell with Apple's factory battery management system, not an aftermarket copy. In Apple's thinnest iPhone, battery choice matters more than in any other model: the cell is engineered to exact thickness tolerances, and the phone's efficiency-tuned hardware depends on the factory power management to deliver all-day endurance from a compact capacity. Every unit is capacity-tested before sale.

iPhone Air battery technology and specifications

Capacity: 3,149 mAh — compact by flagship standards, but paired with the Air's efficiency-focused C1X modem and A19 Pro silicon, it delivers genuinely all-day use on a healthy cell. That balance only holds with a genuine cell delivering true rated capacity; copy cells with overstated capacity fall visibly short in this model.

Engineered thinness: The Air's cell is built to strict thickness tolerances for the ultra-thin housing. Aftermarket cells that deviate even slightly can press against internal components or the display — a genuine cell is the only guaranteed safe fit.

Power management: Apple's factory battery management circuitry governs charging curves, thermal limits, and Battery Health reporting accuracy — the components copy batteries compromise on.

Charging behavior: Restores the factory charging profile including MagSafe wireless charging. Apple also offers a MagSafe Battery accessory designed around the Air's charging system; genuine internal cells maintain full compatibility with it.

Safety: Genuine Apple cells meet Apple's thermal and overcharge standards — in the thinnest iPhone ever made, this is not the component to economize on.

Why a genuine battery matters?

Degradation shows up as faster drain, slowdowns under load, and a battery service message. A genuine replacement resolves all three as designed: full rated capacity, restored performance, correct Battery Health reporting.

What is the iPhone Air original battery price in Bangladesh?

The original iPhone Air battery costs Tk 12,000 at iFixit BD, including capacity testing before sale and an 18-month warranty. In Apple's thinnest iPhone, the genuine cell is a safety decision as much as a performance one — the housing leaves no tolerance for copy cells that deviate in thickness or run hot, which is why we do not recommend economizing on this part for this model.

Condition, Warranty, and Ordering

Capacity-tested before sale, priced at Tk 12,000, an 18-month warranty. Order on WhatsApp, call 01613338800, or visit any iFixit BD branch.

With 18+ years of experience, 500,000+ devices repaired, and 70+ expert technicians across 4 dedicated branches in Dhaka, iFixit BD repairs every iPhone Air fault. What are the common iPhone Air problems we fix?

Screen cracking more easily due to the ultra-thin chassis

The iPhone Air's extreme thinness means less material between the display glass and the surface it hits on impact. Drops that would survive on a standard iPhone are more likely to crack the Air screen. We see this model frequently — OLED panel replacement and full display assembly replacement are the most common repairs. iPhone Air screen replacement

Battery draining quickly in a slim form factor

Apple fitted a smaller physical battery to achieve the iPhone Air's ultra-thin profile. Heavy users notice this — on-screen time is visibly shorter than on the standard iPhone air. When capacity drops further through normal degradation, the battery becomes noticeably insufficient for a full day. Same-day battery replacement restores performance. iPhone Air battery replacement

Frame bending from pressure or bag compression

An extremely thin aluminium-titanium chassis is more susceptible to frame flex from sitting on it, carrying it in a full bag, or dropping it on a flat surface. A bent frame creates a gap at the display seal, allows moisture ingress, and can damage internal flex cables. iFixit BD's frame repair and housing replacement service addresses this before it causes further internal damage. iPhone Air housing repair

USB-C port damage from frequent use

USB-C on the iPhone Air is the single port for both charging and data. Daily cable insertion on an ultra-thin device puts more mechanical stress on the port mounting point than on thicker iPhones. Intermittent charging and loose connectors are early signs of port wear. iPhone Air charging issues

Camera module misalignment after drop

The iPhone Air features a single large rear camera. A drop that impacts the thin rear chassis can shift the camera module or crack the lens. Blurry images, autofocus hunting, and app instability are the visible symptoms. iPhone Air camera repair

data.title: Charge Draining Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone comes with a powerful battery. The battery is optimized perfectly for the phone. However, it may be for some manufacturer error or something about some faulty apps optimization, you may not get the smoothest output from your iPhone 7 plus battery. Most users have reported that the iPhone’s battery starts draining after the system has updated. Several other issues may cause battery drain issues also. These issues include:

  • The battery of the iPhone 7 plus runs out too quickly after the update
  • The battery of the iPhone 7 plus runs out after installing an app/ update of an app.
  • The iPhone Battery drains after the phone heats up too quickly.

These are the most common problems regarding battery-draining found on the internet. Your issues may be one of them or not listed! However, we recommend trying some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may resolve your issue.

  • Turn off background iCloud/itunes sync to save battery by a considerable amount.
  • When not in use turn off WiFi/Cellular Data/Location/Bluetooth service in your iPhone
  • Don’t overcharge/ Frequently charge your iPhone 7 plus. It may reduce battery health.
  • Adjust your brightness settings in iPhone 7 plus to auto-brightness.
  • Turn off Background app refresh
  • From here: Settings > general > Background app refresh

Try running it on low power mode

  • from here: Settings > Battery > Low power mode ON
  • Turn off “reduce motion” to turn off aesthetic animations in your phone to save battery life might help
  • Turn it off from here: Settings > General > Accessibility > Reduce Motion

If none of the aforementioned procedures work to resolve your battery draining issues, it may need to be looked at by a professional technician to get them resolved. data.title: Power Issue
data.description:
To maintain the sleek and uniform design, Apple provided a power button at the side of the device. This correlation between the power button and the Battery is unavoidable for the perfect operation of the iPhone. The iPhone has been designed to maintain it. However, many users have complained about issues regarding issues in their power supply and other power-related errors in their iPhones.

These power issues include:

  • The Phone does not turn on
  • The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked-out phone. Therefore you can not determine the problem.
  • iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.
  • iPhone doesn’t charge. It is stuck on the battery percentage you left it to charge on.
  • Can’t use the iPhone without keeping it on a constant power supply (eg: Connected to a wall adapter or power bank etc,)

These frustrating problems are however the most common issues found on iPhone X. There are some widely renowned DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available on the internet which may help the issue on your device. Such as

  • Force restarting your iPhone ( Press Volume up (+) and quickly press volume down (-) and then quickly press the power button to complete the restart process)
  • Check Your Lightning cable and adapter and see if they are functioning properly.
  • Check if there is any debris on the iPhone X charging porthole.
  • Limit background processes by stopping the background app refresh.
  • Try charging for 20 minutes while keeping your phone switched off.
  • Sometimes excessive battery drain can be happening due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version.

If none of these methods work to resolve the issues on your smartphone, you might need to get it checked by professional technicians. repair_info.name: No Light On Display Issue
repair_info.image_alt_text: iPhone Se 2022 No Light On Display Issue

data.description:
The new iPhone Se 2022 offers one of the best displays of high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both the back and the front. However, not all damage to the display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone Se 2022 have reported a sudden black screen with no prior damage history. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone Se 2022 is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone is running okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. The phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

The phone's display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus) 

The phone has calls and notifications but doesn’t show anything on display

iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone. (Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen) 

Connect the lightning cable and charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone

UNCONVENTIONAL: Press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect to any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended, however, it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issues. It might be risky for any layman. 

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving no light-on-display issues on your iPhone Se 2022. We are a service center that operates based on 4 different and convenient points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Cleaning Service
data.description:
The new iPhone SE 2022 is an IP68-rated dust and water-resistant phone. However, once you have opened your iPhone once for repair or any replacement of parts. The rating becomes null and void and your phone loses its IP68 rating. If your iPhone doesn’t have that IP68 rating, it means it can easily catch dirt or any form of debris from outside. Because it does not have that dust-resistant substance and machine-formed compact bonding like when it came from the company.

If you have dirt, dust, or debris on your iPhone, it may get in the way of your phone's functionality, for example:

data.description:
The new iPhone XS MAX offers a haptic touch system instead of a 3D touch system that was available in the previous versions of the iPhones. The new haptic touch does not require assessing the strength of users like it needed to in the 3D touch system. Instead, it measures the area of your fingertips to decide the strength and length of the touch input provided by the user. This haptic touch is also a way to ensure your touch works for a long time. However, you just might face an issue anytime soon on your iPhone XS MAX regarding your phone’s touch.

The most common issues faced by the users that are reported in the iPhone XS MAX users community forum are as follows:

  • Too sensitive screen/screen response intermittently (means responses without the user having to input or auto touch)
  • Touchscreen in your iPhone does not respond at all
  • Delayed Touch issue
  • Touch doesn’t respond after dropping from hand. (Everything else seems to work fine)

There are some fixes you might try to see if any of them work for your phone. Those are the following listed below:

  • Make sure your touch screen protector doesn’t interfere with proper operation.
  • Make sure there’s no internal/external damage (cracking or shattering glass)
  • Disconnect your USB-lightning port to check if it works.
  • If your phone is above normal temperature wait for it to cool down and then try again.
  • Restart your device.

If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get your iPhone checked by professional technicians. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving issues regarding touch on your iPhone XS MAX. ifixit bd is located in 4 different service points. data.description:
The new iPhone 15 Pro comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

The face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way

Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts

If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all. If your iPhone 15 Pro Face ID problems can’t be categorized and sorted by the above-mentioned issues and fixes, you may just need to take it to an extremely diligent iPhone technician to deal with Face ID issues. data.description:

If the top or bottom speaker of your iPhone 13 Pro is not working, you should check something before reaching any conclusions. Check if:

Make sure the ringer switch is on in sound mode

iPhone 6s repair service in Dhaka, Bangladesh

With 18+ years of experience, 500,000+ devices repaired, and 70+ expert technicians across 4 dedicated branches in Dhaka, iFixit BD repairs every iPhone 6s fault. The iPhone 6s brought 3D Touch, a 12MP camera with 4K video, and Touch ID second generation to the standard 4.7-inch design in 2015. We repair cracked screens, dead batteries, Lightning port damage, Touch ID failure, and board-level issues. Screen replacement starts from ৳2,000, battery from ৳1,000, every repair with a free written diagnosis.

What are the common iPhone 6s problems we fix?

Battery completely failed — must be replaced before anything else

The iPhone 6s battery is 10+ years old. At this age, cells are effectively depleted — the phone shuts down at 50%, charges slowly, and runs hot. Battery replacement is mandatory before any other repair is considered. iPhone 6s battery replacement

Cracked LCD screen

The 4.7-inch Retina HD LCD display cracks on drops and shows LCD damage — white backlight spots, dark bleed from cracks, touch dead zones. Full display assembly replacement restores complete function. iPhone 6s screen replacement

3D Touch not responding or inconsistent

The 3D Touch pressure layer on the 6s screen degrades over time. Inconsistent pressure detection, 3D Touch features failing to trigger, or complete 3D Touch failure are all repaired through display assembly replacement. iPhone 6s 3D Touch repair

Touch ID slow or not recognising fingerprints

The second-generation Touch ID sensor is more precise but still wears with age. Fingerprint failure, very slow response, and home button clicking without Touch ID response are all common on 10-year-old units. iPhone 6s Touch ID repair

Lightning port pin wear causing charging failure

Ten years of daily cable use wears the Lightning port pins past the point where cleaning helps. Port flex cable replacement is typically necessary at this device age. iPhone 6s charging issues

How does our repair process work?

Step 1 — Free diagnosis. Bring your iPhone 6s to any iFixit BD branch. Fault identified, written quote at no cost.

data.title: Audio Issue
data.description:
The iPhone 12 Pro is one of the best phones in the market, considering its audio output quality. It has a dual stereo speaker with noise cancellation and spatial audio features. It has two speaker grills in the bottom part of the phone. It should be kept in mind that, the left speaker grill is not a speaker but instead it is there to catch audio inputs for your voice calls and Siri. The audio-only comes out of the right speaker grill and it is not a faulty feature. The two speakers of the iPhone 12 Pro are located on the top and the bottom of the phone. The top speaker also serves its purpose as an ear speaker when in calls.

However, some users have reported a lot of different audio issues. The most common audio issues faced by iPhone 12 Pro users are:

No sound in audio playback

No sound in voice calls

Distorted sound/Low sound on the speakers

Headphones not working

Audio not working or audio levels low after an update.

Phone stuck in Headphone mode

Ringer Switch not working/ Audio level increases or decreases automatically/ Physical audio level buttons not working.

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “Do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. Those are:

Checking the ringer switch to see if it is on the sound mode

Restarting Your Phone

Disabling your Bluetooth in the iPhone 12 Pro

Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode

Check sound notification settings and try turning noise cancellation off.

Try using headphones and check if the sounds come okay in headphones.

Try removing any protective cases

Clean the speaker grills for dirt and debris

if none of the fixes works for your phone you need to get it checked by professional technicians who specialize in repairing iPhones. In ifixit bd, we have experienced technicians who specialize in repairing iPhone 12 Pro. Our service points are located at locations in Dhaka, Bangladesh. We also offer quick service for your ease of access and on top of that, a 30-days warranty on applicable services you receive from ifixit bd.

data.description:
Other issues like high ping or latency have often been reported by the users of the phone. The most common reported iPhone 6s Wi-Fi issues are...

Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone 6s.

Wi-Fi stays connected but there is no internet on the receiver.

Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/ non-metered connections on Wi-Fi.

High Latency/Ping on Wi-Fi connections

iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi

iPhone can’t discover your Wi-Fi connection.

These Wi-Fi issues found on iPhone 6s are pretty common issues found on other wireless supported devices too! And does not necessarily indicate that there is something specifically wrong with your iPhone 6s wireless hardware. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issues have been resolved.

Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again.

Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection.

Cracked LCD screen

The 4.7-inch Retina HD LCD display cracks on drops and shows LCD damage — white backlight spots, dark bleed from cracks, touch dead zones. Full display assembly replacement restores complete function. iPhone 6s screen replacement

Touch ID slow or not recognising fingerprints

The second-generation Touch ID sensor is more precise but still wears with age. Fingerprint failure, very slow response, and home button clicking without Touch ID response are all common on 10-year-old units. iPhone 6s Touch ID repair

Lightning port pin wear causing charging failure

Ten years of daily cable use wears the Lightning port pins past the point where cleaning helps. Port flex cable replacement is typically necessary at this device age. iPhone 6s charging issues

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service restores your damaged handset to full working order through diagnostics, component replacement, and function testing. The service covers screen repair, battery replacement, charging port repair, back glass replacement, camera repair, Face ID repair, speaker and microphone repair, water damage repair, logic board repair, and software fault repair.

Repair costs sit in three tiers. Entry-level jobs like a charging port cleanup cost the least, mid-level jobs like a battery replacement land in the middle, and premium jobs like an OLED display swap cost the most. Screen replacement pricing follows the same three tiers.

Turnaround times vary by repair type. A battery swap wraps up same day, while logic board and water damage work takes longer because part availability drives the schedule.

You pick the replacement part grade before work starts. New genuine parts, used genuine parts, OEM-grade parts, and certified after-market parts each carry a different price and a different effect on parts and service history reporting. Every repair ships with a parts and labor warranty.

Booking takes six steps, starting with a free diagnostic and ending when you collect a function-tested device. Walk in or reserve your slot ahead — booking ahead locks in the part you need.

What is an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service is a technical service that diagnoses faults in an Apple iPhone 16 Pro Max, replaces the failed component, and verifies device function before handover. The service addresses display faults, power faults, camera faults, audio faults, liquid damage, and board-level faults. Every repair starts with a free diagnostic check that identifies the failed component before you approve any cost. Each completed repair passes a function test that confirms the repaired component and the surrounding systems operate correctly.

The iPhone 16 Pro Max repairs covered by this service are listed below.

  • iPhone 16 Pro Max screen repair — Replaces the cracked or unresponsive 6.9-inch LTPO OLED display assembly and calibrates True Tone, brightness, and touch response after fitting.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max battery replacement — Installs a new battery when battery health drops below 80 percent, then calibrates the cell so battery health reporting reads accurately.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max charging port repair — Restores the USB-C connector when the device charges intermittently, rejects accessories, or stops recognizing a cable.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max back glass replacement — Replaces the cracked rear glass panel and reseals the housing so the device retains its water resistance rating.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max camera repair — Replaces the rear camera module, front camera assembly, LiDAR sensor, or camera lens when images blur, shake, or fail to focus.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max facial recognition repair — Restores the TrueDepth camera and dot projector so Face ID authenticates, unlocks the device, and authorizes Apple Pay.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max speaker repair — Replaces the loudspeaker or earpiece when call audio distorts, media playback crackles, or one channel goes silent.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max microphone repair — Replaces the microphone assembly when callers hear you faintly, voice memos record silence, or Siri stops responding.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max water damage repair — Removes corrosion from the board with ultrasonic cleaning, replaces oxidized components, and restores the affected circuits.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max logic board repair — Repairs the failed integrated circuit at chip level when the device shows a boot loop, no power, or no display output.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max software fault repair — Recovers iOS when the device sticks on the Apple logo, restarts repeatedly, or fails a firmware update.

How much does an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair cost?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair costs between BDT 2,500 and BDT 55,000, depending on the failed component and the replacement part grade you select. The component determines the base cost, and the part grade adjusts it. You receive a written quotation after the free diagnostic, and that figure holds through the repair.

Entry-level repairs cost between BDT 2,500 and BDT 6,000. This tier covers charging port cleaning, speaker replacement, microphone replacement, button repair, and software fault recovery. These repairs use inexpensive components and finish quickly.

Mid-level repairs cost between BDT 7,000 and BDT 18,000. This tier covers battery replacement, charging port replacement, rear camera replacement, front camera replacement, and back glass replacement. These repairs use moderately priced modules and require housing disassembly.

Premium repairs cost between BDT 20,000 and BDT 55,000. This tier covers OLED display replacement, Face ID and TrueDepth camera repair, water damage restoration, and logic board repair. Display assemblies and board-level work carry the highest component and labor cost on the iPhone 16 Pro Max.

You confirm the exact figure for your device during the free diagnostic, since the same symptom sometimes traces to different components.

How much does an iPhone 16 Pro Max screen replacement cost?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max screen replacement costs between BDT 18,000 and BDT 52,000, depending on the display grade you select. The 6.9-inch LTPO OLED panel is the most expensive single component in the device, which places every screen replacement in the upper cost range.

An entry-level screen replacement costs between BDT 18,000 and BDT 24,000. This tier uses a certified after-market OLED assembly that restores display output and touch response at the lowest cost.

A mid-level screen replacement costs between BDT 26,000 and BDT 38,000. This tier uses an OEM-grade or used genuine display that matches original color accuracy and supports the ProMotion refresh rate.

A premium screen replacement costs between BDT 40,000 and BDT 52,000. This tier uses a new genuine Apple display that preserves True Tone, adaptive color temperature, Always-On display behavior, and clean parts and service history reporting.

You keep Face ID after any of these three grades, because the technician transfers the original TrueDepth assembly to the new display.

Which replacement parts are used for an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair?

The replacement part grades used for an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair are listed below.

  • New genuine manufacturer parts — Factory-new Apple components that deliver original performance and clean parts and service history reporting.
  • Used genuine manufacturer parts — Tested Apple components harvested from donor devices, offering genuine performance at reduced cost.
  • Original equipment manufacturer grade parts — Components built to Apple's specification by the same suppliers, matching original tolerances and materials.
  • Certified after-market parts — Independently manufactured components that pass quality certification and carry the same repair warranty.

You confirm the part grade in writing before the repair begins, so the quoted price and the fitted component always match. Genuine parts preserve adaptive color temperature, True Tone calibration, and accurate battery health reporting in Settings.

How long does an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair take?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair takes 30 minutes to 5 working days. Component replacements finish within the same day, while board-level work extends across several days. Turnaround depends on part availability more than on repair difficulty, so a stocked display fits faster than a special-order camera module. Logic board repair and water damage repair take longer than component replacement, because both require diagnosis at circuit level, ultrasonic cleaning, micro-soldering, and staged testing between each step.

The turnaround time for each iPhone 16 Pro Max repair type is shown below.

Repair typeTypical turnaround timeSame-day availabilityScreen replacement45 to 90 minutesYesBattery replacement30 to 60 minutesYesCharging port repair60 to 120 minutesYesSpeaker or microphone repair45 to 90 minutesYesCamera repair60 to 120 minutesYesBack glass replacement2 to 4 hoursYesFace ID repair3 to 6 hoursYesSoftware fault repair1 to 3 hoursYesWater damage repair2 to 4 working daysNoLogic board repair2 to 5 working daysNo

You receive a turnaround estimate in writing alongside your quotation, and the service desk updates you when a repair moves between stages. Verify current figures against your own service records before publishing, since part supply changes turnaround ranges over time.

Does an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair include a warranty?

Yes, an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair includes a warranty. Every repair carries parts and labor coverage that runs from the collection date. The warranty covers component failure and workmanship faults on the repaired part. Coverage applies to the specific component replaced during the repair, and the service desk records the covered part and the coverage period on your invoice at handover.

How do you book an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service?

You book an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service by describing the fault, requesting a free diagnostic, approving the written quotation, and confirming a collection time. The process moves from fault description to device collection in six steps, and each step produces a written record you keep. Our service center operates in Dhaka and covers customers across Bangladesh, including Gulshan, Banani, Dhanmondi, Uttara, Mirpur, and Mohakhali. Walk-in service runs during business hours, and booking ahead reserves the specific part your repair requires. You back up the device to iCloud or a computer before handover, since board-level and water damage repairs sometimes affect stored data.

The steps to book an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service are outlined below.

  1. Describe the fault and request a free diagnostic — Report the symptom by phone, message, or in person, and the technician runs Apple Diagnostics to identify the failed component.
  2. Receive a written quotation and turnaround estimate — Review the itemized cost and completion time before you approve any work on your device.
  3. Confirm the replacement part grade — Select new genuine, used genuine, OEM-grade, or certified after-market parts, and the service desk records your choice in writing.
  4. Book a time slot or walk in — Reserve a slot to secure your part in advance, or bring the device directly during business hours for stocked repairs.
  5. Back up the device before handover — Sync your data to iCloud or a computer, and note your Apple ID credentials for post-repair activation.
  6. Collect the device after function testing — Inspect the repaired component, verify the function test results, and receive your warranty invoice at handover.

Your iPhone 16 Pro Max deserves a repair that holds up. Book your free diagnostic today and get a written price before anyone opens your device.

This correlation between the power button and the Battery is unavoidable for the perfect operation of the iPhone. The iPhone has been designed to maintain it. However, many users have complained about issues regarding issues in their power supply and other power-related errors in their iPhones.

These power issues include:

The Phone does not turn on

The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked out phone. Therefore you can not determine the problem.

iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.

iPhone doesn’t charge. It is stuck on the battery percentage you left it to charge on.

Can’t use the iPhone without keeping it on a constant power supply (eg: Connected to a wall adapter or power bank etc,)

These frustrating problems are however the most common issues found on iPhone XS MAX. There are some widely renowned DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available on the internet which may help the issue on your device. Such as

Force restarting your iPhone ( Press Volume up (+) and quickly press volume down (-) and then quickly press the power button to complete restart process)

Check Your Lightning cable and adapter and see if they are functioning properly.

Check if there is any debris on the iPhone XS MAX charging porthole.

Limit background processes by stopping the background app refresh.

Try charging 20 minutes while keeping your phone switched off.

Sometimes excessive battery drain can be happening due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version.

data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 13 offers its users better optimization and balance in software than previous iPhone models. However, no matter how hard they try, there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning.The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it gets stuck on the boot menu. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

This Stuck on the Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

The iPhone has caused some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

Update disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss

A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity

It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up

These issues, however, can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps to see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 13

(Press the volume up (+) and then quickly press the volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 13 power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS app to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work for you. You might have an issue that requires the touch of a professional iPhone technician. So, visit your nearest ifixit bd service point to avail the best iPhone servicing available to you for your iPhone 13 “Stuck on apple logo” issue or any other iPhone issue for that matter.

data.title: Temperature High Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone XR comes with a generally better and more efficient processor and battery than the iPhone X series. Although the users have said that the phone tends to get hotter than the previous iPhones Apple has released,. The new iPhone XR comes with a special thermal compound in the back area of the phone, which helps to omit heat faster and more efficiently than the previous iPhones. It may make your iPhone seem a lot hotter than the previous iPhones.

However, that doesn’t make the iPhone XR so warm that the users find it difficult to hold it down with their hands. This is a clear indication of overheating in the iPhone XR. Some similar cases of overheating include...

  • The phone gets way too hot while charging and takes a long time to be fully charged.
  • The phone gets hot, and the battery drains drastically.
  • You might see a notification that will say “Temperature high.”
  • The iPhone gets warm on standby mode for no apparent reason whatsoever.

(Note: if your phone gets too hot while transferring data for the first time from a previous iPhone, chances are it’s a one-time issue and will not happen again.)

These are some of the most discussed problems in Apple’s user threads and community. However, there are some DIY (do it yourself) fixes that you may try that may help you to resolve your overheating issues.

  • Disable background app refresh.
  • Disable background app refresh from here: Settings > General > Background App Refresh
  • Turn off Bluetooth/location services to reduce processes running in the background.
  • Most of the users have reported they get the heating issue in the latest iOS version. In that case,
  • Try updating your iOS to later versions to check if it works for your phone.

If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get it looked at by professional technicians who specialize in resolving iPhone XR heating issues. data.description:
The new iPhone 13 Pro offers one of the best displays of high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both back and the front. However, not all damage to the display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone 13 Pro have reported a sudden black screen with no prior damage history. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 13 Pro is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone is running okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. The phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

The phone's display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus) 

The phone has calls and notifications but doesn’t show anything on display

iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone. (Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen) 

Connect the lightning cable and charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone

UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect to any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended, however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issues. It might be risky for any layman. 

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving no light on display issues on your iPhone 13 Pro. We are a service center that operates based on 4 different and convenient points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.description:
The new iPhone 13 has 3 physical buttons and 1 switch to ensure maximum accessibility to its users. The buttons and the switches are:

Volume Up (+) button

Ringer Switch

Power Button

Newer iPhone models have discontinued the Home button, which used to serve both the purpose of a home button and a fingerprint sensor. Apple has discontinued Home Buttons since the iPhone X models and has continued on the same policy till now. The iPhone 13 has no home buttons. Instead, it has a Face ID or face unlock feature. Now with time, the buttons on your iPhone 13 may face wear and tear and may cease to function properly.

The most common issues faced regarding the buttons of smartphones are...

The Sound doesn’t increase/decrease when I press the volume up or down key

data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone SE 2020 offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu.

This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

  • This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:
  • The iPhone has taken in some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)
  • Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss.
  • A third-party app may have access to vital permissions which can disrupt iPhones' productivity.
  • It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up.

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

  • Force Restart your iPhone SE 2020
  • Update your iOS Software.
  • (If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)
  • Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from iStore.
  • Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work, for you. You might have an issue that needs the touch of a professional iPhone technician. Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issues have been resolved

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone 12 mini is a standard IP68 rated, dust and water-resistant phone. This means it can resist dust and water coming in up to a certain level. However, it is not completely immune to water getting inside the iPhone and damaging it. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole.

Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth

You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there

NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth

If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers.

data.title: Audio Issue
data.description:
The iPhone 12 Pro is one of the best phones in the market, considering its audio output quality. It has a dual stereo speaker with noise cancellation and spatial audio features. It has two speaker grills in the bottom part of the phone. It should be kept in mind that, the left speaker grill is not a speaker but instead it is there to catch audio inputs for your voice calls and Siri. The audio-only comes out of the right speaker grill and it is not a faulty feature. The two speakers of the iPhone 12 Pro are located on the top and the bottom of the phone. The top speaker also serves its purpose as an ear speaker when in calls. However, some users have reported a lot of different audio issues.

The most common audio issues faced by iPhone 12 Pro users are:

No sound in audio playback

No sound in voice calls

Distorted sound/Low sound on the speakers

Headphones not working

Audio not working or audio levels low after an update.

Phone stuck in Headphone mode

Ringer Switch not working/ Audio level increases or decreases automatically/ Physical audio level buttons not working.

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “Do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. Those are:

Checking the ringer switch to see if it is on the sound mode

Restarting Your Phone

Disabling your Bluetooth in the iPhone 12 Pro

Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode

Check sound notification settings and try turning noise cancellation off.

Try using headphones and check if the sounds come okay in headphones.

Try removing any protective cases

Clean the speaker grills for dirt and debris

data.description:
The new iPhone 14 Pro Max comes with a distinct feature called Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided by the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me to the Passcode and not Face ID.

These common issues, however, have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fixed attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.

Make sure you are facing the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing your face and the camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID, instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked with face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts

If at Face ID is set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all

data.description:
The new iPhone 7 Plus offers one of the best displays consisting of a retina display and a significantly high DPI. Not all damage in display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone 7 have reported a sudden black screen without any prior damage history. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 7 is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

  • The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:
  • The Phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen.
  • The phone has calls, notifications but doesn’t show anything on display
  • iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display.

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

  • Force Restart your iPhone.
  • Connect the lightning cable, charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone.
  • UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issue.

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. data.description:
The new iPhone 11 offers one of the best displays consisting of a Liquid Retina IPS LCD display and a significantly high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both the back and front. However, not all damage in display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone 11 have reported a sudden black screen without any prior damage history. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 11 is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs.

But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

  • The Phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus)
  • The phone has calls, notifications but doesn’t show anything on display
  • iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display.
  • This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.
  • Force Restart your iPhone.

(Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen)

  • Connect the lightning cable, charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone.
  • UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issue. It might be risky for any layman person.

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving No light on display issues on your iPhone 11. We are a service center that operates based on 4 different and convenient points around Dhaka, Bangladesh. We offer the best service options you can avail of anywhere regarding your iPhone in Dhaka, Bangladesh. We provide:

data.title: Mic Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro offers a set of microphones to ensure your iPhone makes the best out of the audio inputs it receives. The iPhone offers the users a dual speaker and microphone to ensure the best listening experience for their users. However, it is often reported by iPhone 11 pro users that, they are getting trouble regarding the microphones in their phones. The most common issues reported in Apple’s user community forum and other blogs are:

  • Low or unclear voice sound in voice calls/ voice memos
  • Low or unclear voice in Facetime, skype, or video recording
  • Muffled or cracked sound while recording/calling using the mic
  • Siri doesn’t work/ can’t hear me/ can’t pick up commands

The iPhone 11 pro has at least 3 different microphones in different places for the phone for different purposes.

  • The bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls
  • One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri
  • The one in the back of your in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video.

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any of the one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY(Do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

Make sure if you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes

Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there

Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works

If the mic works in voice memo make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone 11 pro

go to Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone.

If none of the fixes work for you, you may need it to be looked at by professional technicians. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving issues in your iPhone 11 pro.

  • Most of the users have reported they only get heating in older iOS, try updating your iOS to later versions to check if it works for your phone.

The Taptic Engine in an iPhone Xs is responsible for providing haptic feedback, such as vibrations for notifications and the "click" sensation for the home button (on supported models). You might need to replace the Taptic Engine in your iPhone if you experience any of the following issues:

Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:

  • If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.
  • The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.
  • The Taptic Engine produces grinding or buzzing noises that were not present before.
  • Error messages or diagnostics indicate an issue with the Taptic Engine.

Possible Causes of Failure:

  • Physical Damage: Dropping the phone or exposing it to water can damage internal components.
  • Software Bugs: Sometimes, a software issue may mimic hardware failure. Perform a factory reset or update the iPhone before deciding on hardware repair.
  • Wear and Tear: Over time, mechanical components can degrade and stop working properly.

data.title: Network Problem
data.description:
The iPhone XS comes with upgraded network connectivity compared to the previous iPhone models and supports 5G network connectivity. Despite these technological advancements from the previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone XS’s network connectivity. Such as loss in the network, prompt disconnections, and inability to find or locate the network. The most common issues, however, are often discussed on Apple’s user forum, and the most common problems found regarding network in iPhone XS are:

  • iPhone XS gets down to 0 network bars randomly.
  • Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G.
  • Cannot access metered/cellular internet connection through the carrier or the SIM company.
  • Network never reaches the full level.

These common issues, however, can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone XS. To resolve these, Apple recommends its iPhone XS users some DIY (do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

  • Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache.
  • Remove your SIM card and reinstall it again. (requires a restart of the device)
  • Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.
  • To set up, go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network.

then:

  • Insert the APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier.
  • Insert username (provided by your carrier).
  • Insert Password (provided by your carrier)
  • Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.
  • Make sure your data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.
  • Install the carrier update for your iPhone (check in Settings > General > About).
  • Restart your iPhone.
  • Soft reset your iPhone.

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need to get your phone checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving your network issues in your iPhone XS. ifixit bd has 4 service points, which are located in points around Dhaka, Bangladesh. MacBook M1 display replacement in Bangladesh

MacBook M1 display replacement is the process of removing a broken screen from a MacBook Air M1 or MacBook Pro M1 and fitting a new Retina display in its place. The repair covers screen damage, dead pixels, backlight failure, and display lines. In Bangladesh, display assembly repair costs range from 35,500 BDT to 45,000 BDT depending on the model and screen type. ifixit BD and other certified service centers in Dhaka complete this repair in 2 to 4 hours. Most centers give a service warranty of 3 months to 1 year after the repair is done.

What is MacBook M1 display replacement?

MacBook M1 display replacement is the repair process of taking out the damaged Retina display from a MacBook Air M1 or MacBook Pro M1 and putting in a working replacement screen. The MacBook M1 screen is not just a plain glass panel — the display assembly includes the screen, the backlight, the front glass, and the connecting cable, all joined together as one unit. When one part of this assembly breaks, the whole screen unit needs to be replaced.
The 4 main types of screen damage that require MacBook M1 display replacement are as follows: a cracked or broken screen from a drop or impact, dead pixels that show as fixed dark or bright spots on the screen, backlight failure that makes the screen very dim or fully dark, and display lines or color patches caused by a damaged screen cable or screen module.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water. However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth

You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.

NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth. If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers. data.description:
The iPhone 11 is one of the best phones in the market, considering its audio output quality. It has a dual stereo speaker with noise cancellation and spatial audio features. It has two speaker grills in the bottom part of the phone. It should be kept in mind that, the left speaker grill is not a speaker but instead it is there to catch audio inputs for your voice calls and Siri. The audio-only comes out of the right speaker grill and it is not a faulty feature. The two speakers of the iPhone 11 are located on the top and the bottom of the phone. The top speaker also serves its purpose as an ear speaker when in calls.

However, some users have reported a lot of different audio issues. The most common audio issues faced by iPhone 11 users are:

  • No sound in audio playback
  • No sound in voice calls
  • Distorted sound/Low sound on the speakers
  • Headphones not working
  • Audio not working or audio levels low after an update.
  • Phone stuck in Headphone mode
  • Ringer Switch not working/ Audio level increases or decreases automatically/ Physical audio level buttons not working.

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “Do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. Those are:

  • Checking the ringer switch to see if it is on the sound mode
  • Restarting Your Phone
  • Disabling your Bluetooth in the iPhone 11
  • Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode
  • Check sound notification settings and try turning noise cancellation off.
  • Try using headphones and check if the sounds come okay in headphones.

data.description:
The new iPhone XS MAX comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature...

  • Face not recognized
  • Face ID is not available at the moment
  • Move the camera a bit lower/higher
  • Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID.

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

  • Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock.

Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

  • if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.
  • Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region.
  • Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy.
  • Update your iOS to the latest version.

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

  • User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone.
  • The user may have just restarted the device.
  • The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours.
  • The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days.
  • The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours.
  • The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space.
  • If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts.
  • If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all.

data.description:
The new iPhone 12 mini offers one of the best displays consisting of a Super AMOLED retina display and a significantly high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both back and front. However, not all damage in display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone 12 mini have reported a sudden black screen without any prior damage history. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 12 mini is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

The Phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus) 

The phone has calls, notifications but doesn’t show anything on display

iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone. (Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen) 

Connect the lightning cable, charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone

UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issue. It might be risky for any layman person. 

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving No light on display issues on your iPhone 12 mini. data.description:
The new iPhone SE 2020 has a new wireless firmware which can support a high range of wireless bandwidth speed. This gives the users unmatched speed in comparison to most of the smartphones in the market. However, there have been issues regarding the Wi-Fi of the iPhone SE 2020. And frankly, some users have taken issue with the phone saying that the phone disconnects from the wireless network frequently and without any warning.

Other issues like high ping or latency have often been reported by the users of the phone. The most common reported iPhone SE 2020 Wi-Fi issues are...

  • Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone SE(2).
  • Wi-Fi stays connected but there is no internet on the receiver.
  • Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/ non-metered connections on Wi-Fi.
  • High Latency/Ping on Wi-Fi connections
  • iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi
  • iPhone can’t discover your Wi-Fi connection.

These Wi-Fi issues found on iPhone SE(2) are pretty common issues found on other wireless supported devices too! And does not necessarily indicate that there is something specifically wrong with your iPhone SE(2)’s wireless hardware. There are some DIY(Do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issues have been resolved.

Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again.

Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection.

Restore the default network connection

( Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > * Enter Passcode * > Confirm)

Update your iOS to the latest version available.

If none of the solutions mentioned above works to resolve your Wi-Fi issues on your iPhone SE(2), you may need to get it checked by a professional technician. product_data.description:
iPhone 17e Original Battery

This is a genuine Apple battery for the iPhone 17e — the original 4,005 mAh lithium-ion cell with Apple's factory battery management system, not an aftermarket copy cell. A genuine battery restores the phone's original battery life, charging behavior, and safety characteristics. Every unit is capacity-tested before sale and comes with an 18-month warranty.

Battery Technology and Specifications

Capacity: 4,005 mAh — the largest battery Apple has fitted in this size class, rated by Apple for up to 26 hours of video playback on a healthy cell. Copy cells routinely overstate printed capacity while delivering measurably less; a genuine cell delivers its rated capacity.

Power management: The assembly includes Apple's factory battery management circuitry, which governs charging curves, thermal limits, and the accuracy of the Battery Health reporting in iOS. This is the component copy batteries cut corners on, and it is the difference between a battery that degrades predictably and one that fails or swells.

Charging behavior: Restores the iPhone 17e's factory charging profile — up to 50% charge in around 30 minutes with a 20W or higher USB-C adapter, plus full MagSafe (up to 15W) and Qi2 wireless charging compatibility. Aftermarket cells frequently charge slower and run hotter under MagSafe.

Safety: Genuine Apple cells meet Apple's thermal and overcharge protection standards. Swollen and overheating batteries in the repair market are overwhelmingly low-grade copy cells; a genuine cell is the single most important safety component you can choose for a battery replacement.

Why a Genuine Battery Matters

When an iPhone battery degrades, most owners notice three things: the percentage drains faster, the phone slows down under peak load, and iOS eventually shows a battery service message. Replacing with a genuine cell resolves all three the way Apple designed: full rated capacity returns, peak performance capability is restored, and the battery reports its health correctly to iOS.

Compatibility

This battery fits the iPhone 17e only. Battery dimensions, connectors, and management firmware differ between iPhone models, so batteries are never cross-compatible. If you are unsure of your model, check Settings → General → About.

Condition, Warranty, and Ordering

Each battery is tested for capacity and health before sale, priced at, and backed by an 18-month warranty. Order on WhatsApp, call 01613338800, or visit any iFixit BD branch in Dhaka.

data.description:
Sometimes when you update your iPhone, or when you try to run your phone you may see some sort of black screen with some sort of Error with a number on your iPhone’s screen out of nowhere. These messages with errors and numbers can be seen while booting up the phone or trying to upgrade the ipsw files from iTunes from a pc. These are Error Codes that indicate to the service technicians that a specific part of the iPhone is malfunctioning. These codes are used by professional repair technicians of iPhones to make their jobs easy. They do not need to diagnose the entire iPhone when they see the code. Therefore saves both the customer’s and the tech expert’s time and other resources.

Some of the common error codes seen in the iPhones are as follows:

ERROR(9): This code shows when you are trying to upgrade your iOS through PC on iTunes, but the iTunes app shows an Error code-9. It is a relatable problem with iTunes error codes – 4013, 4014, and 4005.

Apple recommends:

To check if your iPhone is updated

To check if the lightning cable works. (Error code 4013,4014 and 4015 usually indicate this issue)

If the update still fails try updating from another pc.

Error 1015: This is an issue if you have a jailbroken device (iOS) and apple detects it.

Error 69: This is a common issue found in iPhone X and later devices. This issue suggests that there might be some sort of hardware error on your phone, which is repairable, to say the least.

Aside from these errors, there are a lot of errors that can occur on your iPhone. These are all listed on Apple’s error solution info pages with possible DIY (Do it yourself) solutions.

The whole error code list: https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT201444

However, not all problems can be fixed only by DIY fixes. Some errors might require some handy work around the inner parts of the phone which should be done by a professional iPhone technician. That is where ifixit bd comes in, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving errors in iPhone SE(2) or any other iPhone devices. ifixit bd is a prominent Apple gadget servicing center based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. We have service points in 4 different locations. We specialize in iPhone repairs and replacements of parts.

The new iPhone XR is a smartphone that has a lot of ambient sensors, such as an accelerometer, a gyroscopic sensor, and a proximity sensor.   • Removing any protective cases for your phone. Especially metallic or magnetic cases, which may hamper the proper functioning of your phone’s camera
  • Try Switching between camera lenses in the settings

data.description:
The new iPhone 8 plus has a new wireless firmware that can support a high range of wireless bandwidth speed. This gives the users unmatched speed in comparison to most of the smartphones in the market. However, there have been issues regarding the Wi-Fi of the iPhone 8 plus. And frankly, some users have taken issue with the phone saying that the phone disconnects from the wireless network frequently and without any warning.

Other issues like high ping or latency have often been reported by the users of the phone. The most common reported iPhone 8 plus Wi-Fi issues are...

  • Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone 8 plus.
  • Wi-Fi stays connected but there is no internet on the receiver.
  • Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/ non-metered connections on Wi-Fi.
  • High Latency/Ping on Wi-Fi connections
  • iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi
  • iPhone can’t discover your Wi-Fi connection.

These Wi-Fi issues found on iPhone 8 plus are pretty common issues found on other wireless supported devices too! And does not necessarily indicate that there is something specifically wrong with your iPhone 8 plus’s wireless hardware. There are some DIY(Do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case,

  • Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issues have been resolved.
  • Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again.
  • Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection.
  • Restore the default network connection (Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > * Enter Passcode * > Confirm)
  • Update your iOS to the latest version available.

If none of the solutions mentioned above works to resolve your Wi-Fi issues on your iPhone 8 plus, you may need to get it checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and professional technicians who specialize in repairing iPhone 8 plus Wi-Fi and its related issues. ifixt bd has 4 service points located in prominent locations around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Touch Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 12 Pro Max offers a haptic touch system instead of a 3D touch system that was available in the previous versions of the iPhones. The new haptic touch does not require assessing the strength of users like it is needed in the 3D touch system. Instead, it measures the area of your fingertips to decide the strength and length of the touch input provided by the user.

This haptic touch is also a way to ensure your touch works for a long time. However, you just might face an issue anytime soon on your iPhone 12 Pro Max regarding your phone’s touch.

The most common issues faced by the users that are reported in the iPhone 12 Pro Max users community forum are as follows:

Too sensitive screen/screen response intermittently (means responses without the user having to input or auto touch)

Touchscreen in your iPhone does not respond at all

Delayed Touch issue

Touch doesn’t respond after dropping from hand. (Everything else seems to work fine)

There are some fixes you might try to see if any of them work for your phone. Those are the following listed below:

Make sure your touch screen protector doesn’t interfere with the proper operation

Make sure there’s no internal/external damage (cracking or shattering glass)

Disconnecting your USB-lightning port to check if it works

If your phone is above normal temperature wait for it to cool down and then try again

Restart your device

If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get your iPhone checked by professional technicians. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving issues regarding touch on your iPhone 12 Pro Max. ifixit bd is located in 4 different service points. data.description:
The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 8 plus is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

  • The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:
  • The Phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen.
  • The phone has calls, notifications but doesn’t show anything on display
  • iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display.

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone.

Connect the lightning cable, charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone.

UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issue.

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues.
