data.title: Power Issue
data.description:
This correlation between the power button and the battery is unavoidable for the perfect operation of the iPhone. The iPhone has been designed to maintain it. However, many users have complained about issues regarding issues in their power supply and other power-related errors in their iPhones.

These power issues include:

  • Phone does not turn on
  • The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked-out phone. Therefore you can not determine the problem
  • iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.
  • iPhone doesn’t charge. It is stuck on the battery percentage you left it to charge on.
  • Can’t use the iPhone without keeping it on a constant power supply (eg: Connected to a wall adapter or power bank etc.

These frustrating problems are however the most common issues found on iPhone Xs . There are some widely renowned DIY (Do It Yourself) fixes available on the internet which may help with the issue on your device. Such as...

  • Force restart your iPhone ( Press Volume up (+) and quickly press volume down (-) and then quickly press the power button to complete the restart process)
  • Check your Lightning cable and adapter to see if they are functioning properly
  • Check if there is any debris on the iPhone Xs charging porthole
  • Limit background processes by stopping background app refresh
  • Try charging for 20 minutes while keeping your phone switched off

Sometimes excessive battery drain can happen due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service restores your damaged handset to full working order through diagnostics, component replacement, and function testing. The service covers screen repair, battery replacement, charging port repair, back glass replacement, camera repair, Face ID repair, speaker and microphone repair, water damage repair, logic board repair, and software fault repair.

Repair costs sit in three tiers. Entry-level jobs like a charging port cleanup cost the least, mid-level jobs like a battery replacement land in the middle, and premium jobs like an OLED display swap cost the most. Screen replacement pricing follows the same three tiers.

Turnaround times vary by repair type. A battery swap wraps up same day, while logic board and water damage work takes longer because part availability drives the schedule.

You pick the replacement part grade before work starts. New genuine parts, used genuine parts, OEM-grade parts, and certified after-market parts each carry a different price and a different effect on parts and service history reporting. Every repair ships with a parts and labor warranty.

Booking takes six steps, starting with a free diagnostic and ending when you collect a function-tested device. Walk in or reserve your slot ahead — booking ahead locks in the part you need.

What is an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service is a technical service that diagnoses faults in an Apple iPhone 16 Pro Max, replaces the failed component, and verifies device function before handover. The service addresses display faults, power faults, camera faults, audio faults, liquid damage, and board-level faults. Every repair starts with a free diagnostic check that identifies the failed component before you approve any cost. Each completed repair passes a function test that confirms the repaired component and the surrounding systems operate correctly.

The iPhone 16 Pro Max repairs covered by this service are listed below.

  • iPhone 16 Pro Max screen repair — Replaces the cracked or unresponsive 6.9-inch LTPO OLED display assembly and calibrates True Tone, brightness, and touch response after fitting.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max battery replacement — Installs a new battery when battery health drops below 80 percent, then calibrates the cell so battery health reporting reads accurately.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max charging port repair — Restores the USB-C connector when the device charges intermittently, rejects accessories, or stops recognizing a cable.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max back glass replacement — Replaces the cracked rear glass panel and reseals the housing so the device retains its water resistance rating.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max camera repair — Replaces the rear camera module, front camera assembly, LiDAR sensor, or camera lens when images blur, shake, or fail to focus.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max facial recognition repair — Restores the TrueDepth camera and dot projector so Face ID authenticates, unlocks the device, and authorizes Apple Pay.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max speaker repair — Replaces the loudspeaker or earpiece when call audio distorts, media playback crackles, or one channel goes silent.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max microphone repair — Replaces the microphone assembly when callers hear you faintly, voice memos record silence, or Siri stops responding.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max water damage repair — Removes corrosion from the board with ultrasonic cleaning, replaces oxidized components, and restores the affected circuits.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max logic board repair — Repairs the failed integrated circuit at chip level when the device shows a boot loop, no power, or no display output.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max software fault repair — Recovers iOS when the device sticks on the Apple logo, restarts repeatedly, or fails a firmware update.

How much does an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair cost?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair costs between BDT 2,500 and BDT 55,000, depending on the failed component and the replacement part grade you select. The component determines the base cost, and the part grade adjusts it. You receive a written quotation after the free diagnostic, and that figure holds through the repair.

Entry-level repairs cost between BDT 2,500 and BDT 6,000. This tier covers charging port cleaning, speaker replacement, microphone replacement, button repair, and software fault recovery. These repairs use inexpensive components and finish quickly.

Mid-level repairs cost between BDT 7,000 and BDT 18,000. This tier covers battery replacement, charging port replacement, rear camera replacement, front camera replacement, and back glass replacement. These repairs use moderately priced modules and require housing disassembly.

Premium repairs cost between BDT 20,000 and BDT 55,000. This tier covers OLED display replacement, Face ID and TrueDepth camera repair, water damage restoration, and logic board repair. Display assemblies and board-level work carry the highest component and labor cost on the iPhone 16 Pro Max.

You confirm the exact figure for your device during the free diagnostic, since the same symptom sometimes traces to different components.

How much does an iPhone 16 Pro Max screen replacement cost?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max screen replacement costs between BDT 18,000 and BDT 52,000, depending on the display grade you select. The 6.9-inch LTPO OLED panel is the most expensive single component in the device, which places every screen replacement in the upper cost range.

An entry-level screen replacement costs between BDT 18,000 and BDT 24,000. This tier uses a certified after-market OLED assembly that restores display output and touch response at the lowest cost.

A mid-level screen replacement costs between BDT 26,000 and BDT 38,000. This tier uses an OEM-grade or used genuine display that matches original color accuracy and supports the ProMotion refresh rate.

A premium screen replacement costs between BDT 40,000 and BDT 52,000. This tier uses a new genuine Apple display that preserves True Tone, adaptive color temperature, Always-On display behavior, and clean parts and service history reporting.

You keep Face ID after any of these three grades, because the technician transfers the original TrueDepth assembly to the new display.

Which replacement parts are used for an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair?

The replacement part grades used for an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair are listed below.

  • New genuine manufacturer parts — Factory-new Apple components that deliver original performance and clean parts and service history reporting.
  • Used genuine manufacturer parts — Tested Apple components harvested from donor devices, offering genuine performance at reduced cost.
  • Original equipment manufacturer grade parts — Components built to Apple's specification by the same suppliers, matching original tolerances and materials.
  • Certified after-market parts — Independently manufactured components that pass quality certification and carry the same repair warranty.

You confirm the part grade in writing before the repair begins, so the quoted price and the fitted component always match. Genuine parts preserve adaptive color temperature, True Tone calibration, and accurate battery health reporting in Settings.

How long does an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair take?

data.description:
Apple revolutionized the entire line of iPhones with the iPhone 12 series. The iPhone 12 Pro Max offers a triple camera setup with Dual-LED dual-tone flash. Which easily makes iPhone 12 Pro Max the best in its business. Even with such an amazing camera, it has been found that some users have found some issues regarding the camera.

The most common issues regarding the rear camera of iPhone 12 Pro Max found in the apple support forum and internet are:

Black Display when the camera turns on/ nothing shows in the camera

LED Flash is not working

Photos seem too noisy/ grainy

Camera or the iPhone freezes while zooming in

Camera freezes/ shows black screen after an iOS update

Blurry, unclear photos

Out of Sync flash. This is a problem where a user wants to take a photo with the flash, but the flash gets triggered after the photo has been taken

  • These are the most common issues that are often reported by users in Apple service centers and user forums. However, they are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available that works as a remedy for these issues. If you are facing any of the above-mentioned problems, try doing.

Removing any protective cases for your phone. Especially metallic or magnetic cases, which may hamper the proper functioning of your phone’s camera

Try Restarting your phone

Try Cleaning your lenses with a microfiber cloth. Be careful not to scratch it

If your camera flash isn’t working, try turning on flash from the control center and see if it works

Try disabling Voiceover settings for your iPhone. From Settings > General > Accessibility > Turn off voiceover

Try Switching between camera lenses in settings

data.title: Boot Loop
data.description:
The iPhone 12 Mini offers the users a new iOS version (iOS 13 upgradable to iOS 14) and updates it forward. Users need to update iOS regularly to maintain the stable and smooth operation of the iPhone. However, sometimes a user may face some unforeseen problems. Like the Boot loop in this instance, where the phone starts and shows the Apple logo. Then goes black and again shows only the apple logo on the screen, the phone can show nothing beyond that.

This issue happens mostly when there is a failed or interrupted software update happens on your phone. Also, other issues may cause your phone to boot loop such as:

Physical Damage (Dropping the phone from your hand, etc.)

Battery connector may have gotten loose or have gone bad.

Hardware Damage.

Improper or failed update that is missing necessary files to get the phone started.

If you think one of the above issues is causing the boot looping error on your phone, you may just try these fixes listed below and see if they work to resolve your issue.

Force Restart Your iPhone 12 Mini

(press the volume up button (+) then release the button. And then quickly press and release the volume down (-) and then hold the power button again until your screen turns black and shows the apple logo)

Check if your iPhone is fully charged or is charging properly.

Connect your iPhone to your computer and try restoring or updating the software through the iTunes application.

If your phone still doesn’t recover from boot looing after trying these fixes, something may have gone wrong which can only be fixed by a professional iPhone technician. iPhone 16e Repair Service in Bangladesh

An iPhone 16e repair service restores your handset to full working order through diagnostics, part replacement, and function testing. The service covers screen repair, battery replacement, charging port repair, back glass replacement, camera repair, Face ID repair, speaker and microphone repair, water damage repair, and motherboard repair.

Repair costs in Bangladesh sit in three tiers. Entry-level jobs like a speaker swap cost the least, mid-level jobs like a battery replacement land in the middle, and premium jobs like an original display replacement cost the most.

Most repairs finish the same day. Motherboard and water damage work runs longer because it needs board-level diagnosis.

What does our iPhone 16e repair service cover?

An iPhone 16e repair service is a technical service that diagnoses faults in an Apple iPhone 16e, replaces the failed part, and verifies device function before handover. The service addresses display faults, power faults, camera faults, audio faults, liquid damage, and board-level faults on the A18 chip platform. Every repair starts with a free diagnostic check that identifies the failed component before you approve any cost. Each completed repair passes a function test that confirms the repaired part and the surrounding systems operate correctly.

The iPhone 16e repairs covered by this service are listed below.

  • iPhone 16e screen repair — Replaces the cracked or unresponsive 6.1-inch OLED display assembly and calibrates brightness, color, and touch response after fitting.
  • iPhone 16e battery replacement — Installs a new battery when battery health drops below 80 percent, then calibrates the cell so battery health reporting reads accurately.
  • iPhone 16e charging port repair — Restores the USB-C connector when the device charges intermittently, rejects accessories, or stops recognizing a cable.
  • iPhone 16e back glass replacement — Replaces the cracked matte back glass and reseals the aluminium frame so the device retains its water resistance rating.
  • iPhone 16e camera repair — Replaces the single rear camera module or the front camera assembly when images blur, shake, or fail to focus.
  • iPhone 16e facial recognition repair — Restores the TrueDepth camera and dot projector so Face ID authenticates, unlocks the device, and authorizes Apple Pay.
  • iPhone 16e speaker repair — Replaces the loudspeaker or earpiece when call audio distorts, media playback crackles, or one channel goes silent.
  • iPhone 16e microphone repair — Replaces the microphone assembly when callers hear you faintly, voice memos record silence, or Siri stops responding.
  • iPhone 16e water damage repair — Removes corrosion from the board with ultrasonic cleaning, replaces oxidized components, and restores the affected circuits.
  • iPhone 16e motherboard repair — Repairs the failed integrated circuit at chip level when the device shows a boot loop, no power, or no display output.

How much does an iPhone 16e repair cost?

An iPhone 16e repair costs between BDT 1,500 and BDT 32,000, depending on the failed part and the grade you select. The failed component sets the base cost, and the part grade adjusts it. You receive a written quotation after the free diagnostic, and that figure holds through the repair.

Entry-level repairs cost between BDT 1,500 and BDT 4,500. This tier covers speaker replacement, microphone replacement, charging port cleaning, action button repair, and software fault recovery. These repairs use low-cost components and finish within a single visit.

Mid-level repairs cost between BDT 5,000 and BDT 14,000. This tier covers battery replacement, charging port replacement, rear camera replacement, front camera replacement, and back glass replacement. These repairs use moderately priced modules and require housing disassembly.

Premium repairs cost between BDT 15,000 and BDT 32,000. This tier covers original display replacement, Face ID and TrueDepth camera repair, water damage restoration, and motherboard repair. Original display assemblies and board-level work carry the highest part and labor cost on the iPhone 16e.

You confirm the exact figure for your device during the free diagnostic, since the same symptom sometimes traces to different components.

How much does an iPhone 16e screen replacement cost in Bangladesh?

An iPhone 16e screen replacement costs between BDT 6,500 and BDT 26,000 in Bangladesh, depending on the display grade you select. The display assembly is the most expensive single part in the device, and the local market supplies five grades at five price points. A display assembly charge covers fitting and calibration and appears as a separate line on your quotation.

An entry-level screen replacement costs between BDT 6,500 and BDT 11,000. This tier uses a copy display or a high quality after-market hard display that restores picture and touch at the lowest cost.

A mid-level screen replacement costs between BDT 12,000 and BDT 18,000. This tier uses a high quality after-market soft display or an OEM-grade display, both of which reproduce OLED contrast and match original touch sensitivity.

A premium screen replacement costs between BDT 19,000 and BDT 26,000. This tier uses an original display pulled from a genuine device, which preserves factory color accuracy, brightness range, and True Tone behavior.

You keep Face ID after any of these five grades, because the technician transfers the original TrueDepth assembly to the new display.

The display grades available for an iPhone 16e repair are listed below.

  • Original display pulled from a genuine device — Factory Apple panel with original color accuracy, peak brightness, and True Tone support.
  • Original equipment manufacturer grade display — Panel built to Apple specification by the same supply chain, matching original tolerances.
  • High quality after-market display, soft variant — Flexible OLED panel with strong contrast, deep blacks, and accurate touch response.
  • High quality after-market display, hard variant — Rigid OLED panel offering durable construction and reliable daily performance at moderate cost.
  • Copy display — Budget replacement panel that restores picture output and touch function at the lowest price point.

You confirm the display grade in writing before the repair begins, so the quoted price and the fitted panel always match. A display assembly charge is added separately to the part price and covers fitting, sealing, and calibration. The warranty period differs by display grade, with original and OEM-grade panels carrying the longest coverage. Adaptive color temperature data transfers from your original display where the feature remains active after the swap.

An iPhone 16e repair takes 30 minutes to 5 working days. Component replacements finish within the same day, while board-level work extends across several days. Turnaround depends on display grade availability in the local market, so a stocked after-market panel fits faster than a special-order original display. data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the SIM tray by putting the ejector pin into the SIM tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the SIM tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water. However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water, here are some basic things you should do:

Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth.

You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.

Never charge your phone untill you have made sure it is completely dry

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.

If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers. Battery draining fast or shutting down suddenly

Home button not working or Touch ID failing

The physical home button on the iPhone 6 is a mechanical component that wears down over time — it can become stiff, stop clicking, or stop registering presses entirely. What are the common iPhone 6 Plus problems we fix?

Battery completely depleted — replacement is essential

A 10–12 year old lithium-ion cell holds almost no practical charge. iPhone 6 Plus batteries in service today require immediate replacement for any continued use — this is not a question of "when" but "now." iPhone 6 Plus battery replacement

Cracked 5.5-inch LCD screen

The 5.5-inch Retina HD LCD display shows standard LCD damage after cracks — white backlight spots, touch dead zones, and dark bleed patches. Full display assembly replacement restores complete function. iPhone 6 Plus screen replacement

Touch Disease — flickering grey bar and unresponsive touch

The iPhone 6 Plus has a known board-level fault called Touch Disease. A design weakness in the touch IC solder joints on the logic board causes a flickering grey bar to appear at the top of the screen, followed by complete touch failure. This is not a screen fault — it is a logic board fault requiring micro-soldering re-work to fix. iFixit BD's board-level lab addresses Touch Disease directly. iPhone 6 Plus Touch Disease repair

Touch ID home button not working

The physical home button and Touch ID sensor wear after 10+ years of use. Mechanical failure, touch sensor degradation, and broken pairing from prior repairs all cause Touch ID failure. iFixit BD restores Touch ID function where the board-level pairing is intact. iPhone 6 Plus home button / Touch ID repair

Lightning port completely worn after 10 years

A decade of daily cable connections has worn the Lightning port pins past usability. Port cleaning alone cannot restore function at this age — flex cable replacement is required. iPhone 6 Plus charging issues

What is an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service is a technical service that diagnoses faults in an Apple iPhone 16 Pro Max, replaces the failed component, and verifies device function before handover. The service addresses display faults, power faults, camera faults, audio faults, liquid damage, and board-level faults.   • iPhone 16 Pro Max screen repair — Replaces the cracked or unresponsive 6.9-inch LTPO OLED display assembly and calibrates True Tone, brightness, and touch response after fitting.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max battery replacement — Installs a new battery when battery health drops below 80 percent, then calibrates the cell so battery health reporting reads accurately.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max charging port repair — Restores the USB-C connector when the device charges intermittently, rejects accessories, or stops recognizing a cable.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max back glass replacement — Replaces the cracked rear glass panel and reseals the housing so the device retains its water resistance rating.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max camera repair — Replaces the rear camera module, front camera assembly, LiDAR sensor, or camera lens when images blur, shake, or fail to focus.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max facial recognition repair — Restores the TrueDepth camera and dot projector so Face ID authenticates, unlocks the device, and authorizes Apple Pay.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max speaker repair — Replaces the loudspeaker or earpiece when call audio distorts, media playback crackles, or one channel goes silent.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max microphone repair — Replaces the microphone assembly when callers hear you faintly, voice memos record silence, or Siri stops responding.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max water damage repair — Removes corrosion from the board with ultrasonic cleaning, replaces oxidized components, and restores the affected circuits.

Limit background processes by stopping background app refresh

Try charging for 20 minutes while keeping your phone switched off

Sometimes excessive battery drain can happen due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version

iPhone 14 Pro Max repair service in Dhaka, Bangladesh

With 18+ years of experience, 500,000+ devices repaired, and 70+ expert technicians across 4 dedicated branches in Dhaka, iFixit BD repairs every iPhone 14 Pro Max fault. Apple's 2022 Pro flagship introduced Dynamic Island for the first time, alongside a 6.7-inch ProMotion OLED display, A16 Bionic chip, 48MP main camera, and Always-On Display. We repair cracked ProMotion screens, dead batteries, Lightning port damage, camera faults, and board-level issues using A-grade and Original parts. Screen replacement starts from ৳10,000, battery from ৳2,500, every repair with a free written diagnosis.

What are the common iPhone 14 Pro Max problems we fix?

Battery capacity declining — Always-On Display drains it faster

The Always-On Display on the iPhone 14 Pro Max runs the screen at a low refresh rate continuously — a useful feature that adds constant background battery drain. Combined with natural cell degradation over two years of use, battery replacement is the most common repair we see on this model. iPhone 14 Pro Max battery replacement

Cracked ProMotion OLED with Always-On Display failure

The 6.7-inch ProMotion panel supports always-on functionality via a low-power LTPO state. A screen crack or OLED damage that disables the always-on feature in addition to normal display function is common after a significant drop. We replace the full assembly and verify ProMotion and always-on operation after every repair. iPhone 14 Pro Max screen replacement

Dynamic Island area damage causing Face ID failure

The Dynamic Island replaced the notch on the iPhone 14 Pro Max — and houses the TrueDepth sensor cluster. A drop to the front top edge of the phone can damage the sensors around the island cutout, disabling Face ID. iPhone 14 Pro Max Dynamic Island / Face ID repair

48MP main camera blur or focus issues

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro is a standard IP68-rated, dust- and water-resistant phone. This means it can resist dust and water coming in up to a certain level. However, it is not completely immune to water getting inside the iPhone and damaging it. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the SIM tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the SIM tray by putting the ejector pin into the SIM tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the SIM tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the SIM tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver, then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red, you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage. If you have dropped your phone in the water, here are some basic things you should do:

  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth.
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY.
  • If anything spills on your phone (like oil, etc.), just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.
  • If water has gotten into your phone , it may damage your battery or charging port or give you muffled speakers.

Here at ifixit bd, we have professional and dedicated technicians who specialize in fixing the problems in your iPhones. ifixit bd is located in service points across Dhaka, Bangladesh. We at ifixit bd offer our customers quick repair service for their ease of access.

iPhone 17 Pro Original Display

This is a genuine Apple Super Retina XDR OLED display assembly for the iPhone 17 Pro, pulled from an original device — not an aftermarket or copy screen. The assembly includes the complete factory display stack: the LTPO OLED panel, the integrated touch layer, and the Ceramic Shield 2 front glass with Apple's anti-reflective coating. Every unit is function-tested before sale and comes with an 18-month warranty against display defects.

Display Technology and Specifications: iPhone 17 Pro

The iPhone 17 Pro uses one of the most advanced smartphone panels Apple has shipped, and because this unit is pulled from a genuine device, every specification below is the factory specification — nothing is downgraded or approximated.

Panel: 6.3-inch Super Retina XDR OLED with LTPO technology and a resolution of 2622×1206 pixels at 460 pixels per inch. Text renders sharp at any viewing distance, and the OLED panel delivers a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio with true blacks, since individual pixels switch off completely.

ProMotion adaptive refresh: The LTPO panel dynamically scales its refresh rate from 1Hz up to 120Hz. Scrolling, gaming, and animations run at up to 120Hz for full smoothness, while the panel drops to 1Hz for static content — which is also what enables the Always-On display without significant battery drain. Aftermarket panels are typically fixed at 60Hz and cannot support Always-On; this one behaves exactly like the factory screen because it is one.

Brightness: 1,000 nits typical maximum, 1,600 nits peak for HDR content, and 3,000 nits peak outdoor brightness — the highest outdoor brightness Apple has shipped on an iPhone. Combined with the factory anti-reflective coating, the display stays fully readable in direct Dhaka sunlight, where lower-grade panels wash out.

Color and calibration: Full P3 wide color gamut with Apple's factory color calibration, True Tone ambient color adjustment, and HDR support including Dolby Vision. Colors and skin tones display exactly as Apple tuned them.

Front glass: Ceramic Shield 2 with approximately 3× the scratch resistance of the original Ceramic Shield, plus the anti-reflective, fingerprint-resistant coating. Copy screens use standard glass that scratches and glares noticeably more.

Integrated components: The assembly retains the factory touch digitizer with full 120Hz touch sampling responsiveness, Haptic Touch support, the ambient light sensing window, and the Dynamic Island cutout with correct tolerances for the TrueDepth system.

How It Compares With OEM and Copy Panels

The technical gap between display grades is measurable, not cosmetic. OEM/aftermarket "original quality" panels are built in third-party factories on lower-grade OLED substrates: they typically run at a fixed 60Hz instead of adaptive 1–120Hz, lose True Tone and Always-On support, reach noticeably lower peak brightness, and draw more power because they lack LTPO's variable refresh. Copy panels (Incell/TFT) drop further — LCD or budget OLED technology with no ProMotion, no True Tone, washed-out color reproduction, weaker touch sampling, and lifespans that often fall under a year. The pulled original panel is the only grade that preserves the complete iPhone 17 Pro display specification: LTPO adaptive refresh, 3,000-nit outdoor brightness, factory color calibration, and Ceramic Shield 2 protection.

data.title: Network Problem
data.description:
The iPhone 13 Pro Max comes with upgraded network connectivity compared to previous iPhone models and supports 5G network connectivity. Despite technological advancements from previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone 13 Pro Max network connectivity. Such as loss of the network, prompt disconnections, inability to find or locate the network.

The most common issues, however, are often discussed upon Apple’s user forum and the most common problems found regarding networks in iPhone 13 Pro Max are:

iPhone 13 Pro Max gets down to 0 network bars randomly

Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G

Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company

Network never reaches the full level

These common issues, however, can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 13 Pro Max. To resolve this, Apple recommends its iPhone 13 Pro Max users some DIY (do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache

Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. -requires a restart of the device

Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.

To set it up, go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network.

then:

Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier

Insert Username (provided by your carrier)

Insert Password (provided by your carrier)

Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.

Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.

Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)

Restart your iPhone

Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to be checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving your network issues with your iPhone 13 Pro Max. ifixit bd has 4 service points which are located in points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 12 Pro comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

The face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way

Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts

If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all

If your iPhone 12 Pro Face ID problems can’t be categorized and sorted by the above-mentioned issues and fixes, you may just need to take it to an extremely diligent iPhone technician to deal with Face ID issues.

The battery of the iPhone 14 runs out too quickly after the update

The battery of the iPhone 14 runs out after installing an app/ update an app

The iPhone Battery drains after the phone heats up too quickly

These are the most common problems regarding battery draining found on the internet. Your issues may be one of them or not listed! However, we recommend trying some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may resolve your issue.

The new iPhone 13 Pro has a new wireless firmware that can support up to 7GHz of wireless bandwidth speed. This gives the users unmatched speed in comparison to most of the smartphones in the market. Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone 13  Pro

Wi-Fi stays connected but there is no internet on the receiver

Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/ non-metered connections on Wi-Fi

High Latency/Ping on Wi-Fi connections

iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi

iPhone can’t discover your Wi-Fi connection

These Wi-Fi issues found on iPhone 13 Pro are pretty common issues found on other wireless supported devices too! It also does not necessarily indicate that there is anything specifically wrong with your iPhone 13 Pro wireless hardware. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issue has been resolved

Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again

Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection

Restore the default network connection

(Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > * Enter Passcode * > Confirm)

Update your iOS to the latest version available

If none of the solutions mentioned above work to resolve your Wi-Fi issue on your iPhone 13 Pro, you may need to get it checked by a professional technician. Make sure the ringer switch is on in the sound mode

data.description:
The new iPhone 14 offers a set of microphones to ensure your iPhone makes the best out of the audio inputs it receives. The iPhone offers the users a dual speaker and microphone to ensure the best listening experience for their users.

However, it is often reported by iPhone 14 users that, they are getting trouble regarding the microphones in their phones. The most common issues reported in Apple’s user community forum and other blogs are:

Low or unclear voice sound in voice calls/ voice memos

Low or unclear voice in Facetime, skype, or video recording

Muffled or cracked sound while recording/calling using the mic

Siri doesn’t work/ can’t hear me/ can’t pick up commands

The iPhone 14 has at least 3 different microphones in different places for the phone for different purposes

At the bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls

One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri

The one in the back of your in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any of the one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

Make sure if you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes

Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there

Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works

If the mic works in voice memo make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone 14 go to: Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone.

If none of the fixes work for you, you may need it to be looked at by professional technicians. iPhone 16 Plus Original Battery

This is a genuine Apple battery for the iPhone 16 Plus — the original 4,674 mAh lithium-ion cell with Apple's factory battery management system, not an aftermarket copy. The 16 Plus is the endurance champion of the standard 16 lineup, rated for up to 27 hours of video playback, and a genuine replacement restores that full capability.

Battery technology and specifications

Capacity: 4,674 mAh — a 6.6% increase over the 15 Plus, and the largest cell in the non-Pro 16 lineup. Paired with the efficient A18 chip, this is what makes the 16 Plus famous for stretching into a second day of light use.

Power management: Apple's factory battery management circuitry governs charging curves, thermal limits, and Battery Health reporting accuracy.

Charging behavior: Restores the factory profile — up to 50% in around 30 minutes with a 20W or higher USB-C adapter, plus MagSafe wireless charging at up to 25W and Qi2 at 15W.

Adhesive system: The 16 Plus uses Apple's electrically-releasing battery adhesive, which makes professional replacement cleaner and safer with the right equipment — which our technicians use.

Why a genuine battery matters?

A degraded battery shows up as faster drain, slowdowns under peak load, and a battery service message. A genuine replacement resolves all three as Apple designed. Since iOS 18.1, iOS can report Battery Health for replacement batteries after Apple's Repair Assistant is run following installation.

Compatibility

Fits the iPhone 16 Plus only. Not cross-compatible with any other model.

The original iPhone 16 Plus battery costs Tk 5500 at iFixit BD, including capacity testing before sale and an 18-month warranty. The 16 Plus's standout endurance depends on its genuine 4,674 mAh cell — copy cells at lower prices consistently fall short of rated capacity, which defeats the reason people buy this model. Thermal design: The iPhone 17 Pro pairs its battery with a vapor chamber cooling system; a genuine cell operates within the thermal envelope that system was designed around. Copy cells running hotter under load undermine both endurance and the phone's sustained performance.

A degraded battery means faster percentage drain, slowdowns under peak load, and eventually a battery service message. A genuine replacement resolves all three as Apple designed: full rated capacity, restored peak performance capability, and correct Battery Health reporting.

data.title: Power Issue
data.description:
To maintain the sleek and uniform design, Apple provided a power button at the side of the device. This correlation between the power button and the battery is unavoidable for the perfect operation of the iPhone. The iPhone has been designed to maintain it. However, many users have complained about issues regarding issues in their power supply and other power-related errors in their iPhone.

These power issues include:

  • The phone does not turn on.
  • The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked-out phone. Therefore, you cannot determine the problem.
  • iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.
  • The iPhone doesn’t charge. It is stuck on the battery percentage you left it to charge on.
  • Can’t use the iPhone without keeping it on a constant power supply (e.g., connected to a wall adapter or power bank, etc.).

These frustrating problems are, however, the most common issues found on the iPhone XR. There are some widely renowned DIY (do it yourself) fixes available on the internet that may help the issue on your device. Such as

  • Force restart your iPhone (press volume up (+) and quickly press volume down, (-) and then quickly press the power button to complete the restart process).
  • Check your Lightning cable and adapter and see if they are functioning properly.
  • Check if there is any debris on the iPhone XR charging porthole.
  • Limit background processes by stopping the background app refresh.
  • Try charging for 20 minutes while keeping your phone switched off.

Sometimes excessive battery drain can be happening due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version. If none of these methods work to resolve the issues on your smartphone, you might need to get it checked by professional technicians. data.title: Error Solution
data.description:
Sometimes when you update your iPhone, or when you try to run your phone you may see some sort of black screen with some sort of Error with a number on your iPhone’s screen out of nowhere. These messages with errors and numbers can be seen while booting up the phone or trying to upgrade the ipsw files from iTunes from a pc. These are Error Codes that indicate to the service technicians that a specific part of the iPhone is malfunctioning. These codes are used by professional repair technicians of iPhones to make their jobs easy. They do not need to diagnose the entire iPhone when they see the code. Therefore saves both the customer’s and the tech expert’s time and other resources.

Some of the common error codes seen in the iPhones are as follows:

ERROR(9): This code shows when you are trying to upgrade your iOS through PC on iTunes, but the iTunes app shows an Error code-9. It is a relatable problem with iTunes error codes – 4013, 4014, and 4005.

Apple recommends:

  • To check if your iPhone is updated
  • To check if the lightning cable works. (Error code 4013,4014 and 4015 usually indicate this issue)
  • If the update still fails try updating from another pc
  • Error 1015: This is an issue if you have a jailbroken device (iOS) and apple detects it
  • Error 69: This is a common issue found in iPhone X and later devices. This issue suggests that there might be some sort of hardware error on your phone, which is repairable, to say the least.

Aside from these errors, there are a lot of errors that can occur on your iPhone. These are all listed on Apple’s error solution info pages with possible DIY (Do it yourself) solutions.

The whole error code list: https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT201444

However, not all problems can be fixed only by DIY fixes. Some errors might require some handy work around the inner parts of the phone which should be done by a professional iPhone technician. data.title: Error Solution
data.description:
Sometimes when you update your iPhone, or when you try to run your phone you may see some sort of black screen with some sort of Error with a number on your iPhone’s screen out of nowhere. These messages with errors and numbers can be seen while booting up the phone or trying to upgrade the IPSW files from iTunes from a PC. These are Error Codes that indicate to the service technicians that a specific part of the iPhone is malfunctioning. These codes are used by professional repair technicians of iPhones to make their jobs easy. They do not need to diagnose the entire iPhone when they see the code. Therefore saves both the customer’s and the tech expert’s time and other resources.

Some of the common error codes seen on iPhones are as follows:

ERROR(9): This code shows when you are trying to upgrade your iOS through PC on iTunes, but the iTunes app shows an Error code-9. It is a relatable problem with iTunes error codes – 4013, 4014, and 4005.

Apple recommends:

To check if your iPhone is updated

If the update still fails try updating it from another pc

To check if the lightning cable works. (Error code 4013,4014 and 4015 usually indicate this issue)

Error 1015: This is an issue if you have a jailbroken device (iOS) and apple detects it.

Error 69: This is a common issue found in iPhone X and later devices. This issue suggests that there might be some sort of hardware error on your phone, which is repairable, to say the least.

Aside from these errors, there are a lot of errors that can occur on your iPhone. These are all listed on Apple’s error solution info page with possible DIY (Do it yourself) solutions. However, not all problems can be fixed only by DIY fixes. Some errors might require some handy work around the inner parts of the phone which should be done by a professional iPhone technician. This is where ifixit bd comes in, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving errors in iPhone 13 Pro Max or any other iPhone device. ifixit bd is a prominent Apple gadget servicing center based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. We have service points in 4 different locations. We specialize in iPhone repairs and replacements of parts.

data.description:
The new iPhone 11 pro max comes with a generally better and more efficient better processor and battery than the iPhone X series. Although, the users have said that the phone tends to get hotter than the previous iPhones Apple has released. The new iPhone 11 pro max comes with a special thermal compound in the back area of the phone which helps to omit heat faster and more efficiently than the previous iPhones. It may make your iPhone seem a lot hotter than the previous iPhones.

However, that doesn’t make the iPhone 11 pro max so warm that the users find it difficult to hold it down with their hands. This is a clear indication of overheating in the iPhone 11 pro max. Some similar cases of overheating include

  • Phone gets way too hot while charging and takes a long time to be fully charged
  • Phone gets hot and the battery drains drastically
  • You might see a notification that will say “Temperature high”
  • The iPhone gets warm on standby mode for no apparent reason whatsoever

(Note: if your phone gets too hot while transferring data for the first time from a previous iPhone, chances are it’s a one-time issue and will not happen again.)

These are some of the most discussed problems in Apple’s user threads and community. However, there are some DIY (Do it Yourself) fixes that you may try which may help you to resolve your overheating issues.

  • Disable background app refresh.
  • Disable background app refresh from here: Settings > General > Background App Refresh
  • Turn off Bluetooth / Location services to reduce processes running in the background
  • Most of the users have reported they get the heating issue in the latest iOS version, In that case
  • try updating your iOS to later versions to check if it works for your phone.

If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get it looked at by professional technicians who specialize in resolving iPhone 11 pro max heating issues. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving your iPhone 11 pro max issues on your phone. ifixit bd is located in four different service points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Wifi Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone XR has a new wireless firmware that can support up to GHz of wireless bandwidth speed. This gives the users unmatched speed in comparison to most of the smartphones in the market. However, there have been issues regarding the Wi-Fi of the iPhone XR. And frankly, some users have taken issue with the phone, saying that the phone disconnects from the wireless network frequently and without any warning.

Other issues like high ping or latency have often been reported by the users of the phone. The most common reported iPhone XR Wi-Fi issues are…

  • Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone XR.
  • Wi-Fi stays connected, but there is no internet on the receiver.
  • 3. Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/non-metered connections on Wi-Fi.
  • High Latency/Ping on Wi-Fi Connections
  • iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi.
  • iPhone can’t discover your Wi-Fi connection.

These Wi-Fi issues found on the iPhone XR are pretty common issues found on other wireless-supported devices too! And does not necessarily indicate that there is something specifically wrong with your iPhone XR’s wireless hardware. There are some DIY (do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

  • Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issues have been resolved.
  • Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again.
  • Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection.
  • Restore the default network connection.

(Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > *Enter Passcode * > Confirm)

  • Update your iOS to the latest version available.

If none of the solutions mentioned above works to resolve your Wi-Fi issues on your iPhone XR, you may need to get it checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and professional technicians who specialize in repairing iPhone XR Wi-Fi and its related issues. ifixt bd has 4 service points located in prominent locations around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

The new iPhone 12 Pro comes with a generally better and more efficient better processor and battery than the iPhone X series. Phone gets way too hot while charging and takes a long time to be fully charged

Phone gets hot and the battery drains drastically

You might see a notification that will say “Temperature high”

The iPhone gets warm on standby mode for no apparent reason whatsoever

These are some of the most discussed problems in Apple’s user threads and community. However, there are some DIY (Do it Yourself) fixes that you may try which may help you to resolve your overheating issues.

Disable background app refresh.

Disable background app refresh from here: Settings > General > Background App Refresh

Turn off Bluetooth / Location services to reduce processes running in the background

Most of the users have reported they get the heating issue in the latest iOS version, In that case

try updating your iOS to later versions to check if it works for your phone.

If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get it looked at by professional technicians who specialize in resolving iPhone 12 Pro heating issues. data.description:
The new iPhone 7 Plus comes with a generally better and more efficient better processor and battery than the previous iPhone series. Although, the users have said that the phone tends to get hotter than the previous iPhones Apple has released. Sometimes the iPhone 7 plus is so warm that the users find it difficult to hold it down with their hands. This is a clear indication of overheating in the iPhone 7 plus. Some similar cases of overheating include.

  • Phone gets way too hot while charging.
  • Phone gets hot and the battery drains drastically.
  • The iPhone can perform simple tasks e.g., Making a phone call, watching a YouTube video, taking a photo without getting hot.
  • The iPhone gets warm on standby mode for no apparent reasons whatsoever.

(Note: if your phone gets too hot while transferring data for the first time from a previous iPhone, chances are it is a one-time issue and will not happen again.)

These are some of the most discussed problems in Apple’s user threads and community. However, there are some DIY (Do it Yourself) fixes that you may try which may help you to resolve your overheating issues.

  • Disable background app refresh.
  • Disable background app refresh from here: Settings > General > Background App Refresh
  • Turn off Bluetooth / Location services to reduce processes running in the background

Most of the users have reported they only get heating in older iOS, try updating your iOS to later versions to check if it works for your phone. If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get it looked at by professional technicians who specialize in resolving iPhone 7 plus heating issues. The Taptic Engine in an iPhone 8 is responsible for providing haptic feedback, such as vibrations for notifications and the "click" sensation for the home button (on supported models). You might need to replace the Taptic Engine in your iPhone if you experience any of the following issues:

Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:

  • If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.
  • The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.
  • The Taptic Engine produces grinding or buzzing noises that were not present before.
  • Error messages or diagnostics indicate an issue with the Taptic Engine.

Possible Causes of Failure:

  • Physical Damage: Dropping the phone or exposing it to water can damage internal components.
  • Software Bugs: Sometimes, a software issue may mimic hardware failure. Perform a factory reset or update the iPhone before deciding on hardware repair.
  • Wear and Tear: Over time, mechanical components can degrade and stop working properly.

data.title: Charge Draining Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone comes with a powerful battery. The battery is optimized perfectly for the phone. However, it may be for some manufacturer error or something about some faulty apps optimization, you may not get the smoothest output from your iPhone 8 plus battery.

Most users have reported that the iPhone’s battery starts draining after the system has updated. Several other issues may cause battery drain issues also. These issues include:

  • The battery of the iPhone 8 plus runs out too quickly after the update
  • The battery of the iPhone 8 plus runs out after installing an app/ update of an app.
  • The iPhone Battery drains after the phone heats up too quickly.

These are the most common problems regarding battery-draining found on the internet. Your issues may be one of them or not listed! However, we recommend trying some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may resolve your issue.

  • Turn off background iCloud/iTunes sync to save battery by a considerable amount.
  • When not in use turn off WiFi/Cellular Data/Location/Bluetooth service in your iPhone
  • Don’t overcharge/ Frequently charge your iPhone 8 plus. It may reduce battery health.
  • Adjust your brightness settings in iPhone 8 plus to auto-brightness.
  • Turn off Background app refresh From here: Settings > general > Background app refresh
  • Try running it on low power mode from here: Settings > Battery > Low power mode ON
  • Turn off “reduce motion” to turn off aesthetic animations in your phone to save battery life might help
  • Turn it off from here: Settings > General > Accessibility > Reduce Motion

If none of the aforementioned procedures work to resolve your battery draining issues, it may need to be looked at by a professional technician to get them resolved. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who have special expertise in repairing iPhones. Our experienced technicians are located in ifixit bd service points located in 4 different points in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: No Modem Firmware
data.description:
It is quite frustrating when you see there’s no network bar/ Wi-Fi signal strong enough near you. We use our phones mostly to stay connected with others most of the time, and problems like that keep us from staying connected.

You may face a similar kind of problem with your iPhone 13 mini. This usually happens after a faulty or incomplete update where you might see this:

There’s no network bar available at the top of the display. Restarting or reinstalling the SIM card doesn’t help. There is always “Searching” shown on the network bar.

There is no Cellular connection available for your phone. You can’t turn on, discover, or connect to available wireless Hotspot networks available near you through your iPhone 13 mini

You can’t connect to your Bluetooth devices like Apple Watch, Bluetooth headphones, and stereo speakers through your phone. It appears that you cannot connect to anything wireless through your iPhone 13 mini

If you are facing this issue go to Settings > General > About and see if you can find information regarding IMEI, Bluetooth location, Modem Firmware, etc. If there is nothing there then you are having an issue with the modem firmware

There are no DIY (Do It Yourself) fixes available for this issue. You are going to be needing to take your iPhone 13 mini to an expert repair technician to resolve the “No modem firmware” issue.

data.description:
The new iPhone 12 Pro Max offers one of the best displays consisting of a Super AMOLED retina display and a significantly high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both the back and front. However, not all damage in display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone 12 Pro Max have reported a sudden black screen without any prior damage history.

The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 12 Pro Max is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

The Phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus)

The phone has calls, notifications but doesn’t show anything on display

iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone. (Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen)

Connect the lightning cable, charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone

UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issue. It might be risky for any layman person.

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues, however, have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fixed attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector, make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.

Make sure you are facing the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID, instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked with face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts

If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all

If your iPhone 13 Pro Face ID problems can’t be categorized and sorted by the above-mentioned issues and fixes, you may just need to take it to an extremely diligent iPhone technician to deal with Face ID issues. data.description:
The new iPhone 8 offers a set of microphones to ensure your iPhone makes the best out of the audio inputs it receives. The iPhone offers the users a mono speaker and microphone to ensure the best listening experience for their users. However, it is often reported by iPhone 8 users that, they are getting trouble regarding the microphones in their phones.   • Low or unclear voice in Facetime, skype, or video recording.
  • Muffled or cracked sound while recording/calling using the mic.
  • Siri doesn’t work/ can’t hear me/ can’t pick up commands.

The iPhone 8 has at least 3 different microphones in different places for phones for different purposes...

  • The bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls
  • One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri
  • The one in the back of your in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video.

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any of the one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

  • Make sure if you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes.
  • Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there.
  • Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works
  • If the mic works in voice memo make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone 8 go to: Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone.

data.description:
MacBook Air 13 inch M1 trackpad issue in Bangladesh

MacBook Air 13 inch M1 trackpad issues are problems that stop the Force Touch trackpad on a MacBook Air A2337 from working correctly — including the cursor not moving, clicking not registering, dead zones appearing on the surface, or the trackpad behaving erratically. Many trackpad problems on the MacBook Air M1 are software-caused and can be fixed at home through a reset. Professional repair costs in Bangladesh range from 1,000–3,000 BDT for a software fix to 10,000–18,000 BDT for a trackpad-only replacement, while a full top case swap exceeds 50,000 BDT. ifixit BD provide diagnosis, trackpad-only hardware replacement, and a service warranty for every MacBook Air M1 trackpad service Bangladesh repair.

What is MacBook Air 13 inch M1 trackpad issue?

A MacBook Air 13 inch M1 trackpad issue is any problem that prevents the Force Touch trackpad on a MacBook Air A2337 from responding correctly to touch, clicks, or gestures — whether the issue is caused by software settings, a hardware fault, or physical damage to the trackpad unit itself.

The MacBook Air M1 (model A2337) uses a Force Touch trackpad powered by a Taptic Engine. Unlike older MacBook trackpads that physically pressed down, the Force Touch trackpad does not physically click — it stays fixed in place and uses haptic feedback from the Taptic Engine to simulate the feel of a click. This design means trackpad issues on the MacBook Air M1 can come from two completely different sources: software-level problems (macOS settings, driver faults, Bluetooth conflicts) or hardware-level problems (a damaged Taptic Engine, dead zones, trackpad flex cable failure, or physical damage). Because many MacBook Air M1 trackpad issues are software-caused, correct diagnosis is the critical first step — professional hardware repair is not always needed.

data.title: Audio Issue
data.description:
The iPhone 14 is one of the best phones on the market, considering its audio output quality. It has a dual stereo speaker with noise cancelation and spatial audio features. It has two speaker grills in the bottom part of the phone. Should keep in mind that, the left speaker grill is not a speaker but instead it is there to catch audio inputs for your voice calls and Siri. The audio-only comes out of the right speaker grill and is not a faulty feature. The two speakers of the iPhone 14 are located on the top and the bottom of the phone. The top speaker also serves its purpose as an ear speaker when in calls. However, some users have reported a lot of different audio issues.

The most common audio issues faced by iPhone 14 users are:

No sound on audio playback

No sound on voice calls

Distorted/Low sound on the speakers

Headphones not working

Audio not working or audio levels low after an update.

Phone stuck in Headphone mode

Ringer Switch not working/ Audio level increases or decreases automatically/ Physical audio level buttons not working.

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “Do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. They are:

Check the ringer switch to see if it is on sound mode

Restarting Your Phone

Disabling your Bluetooth on the iPhone 14

Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode

Check the sound notification settings and try turning noise cancelation off.

Try using headphones and check if the sounds come okay in headphones.

Try removing any protective cases

Clean speaker grills for dirt and debris

data.title: Temperature High Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 8 comes with a generally better and more efficient processor and battery than the previous iPhone series. Although the users have said that the phone tends to get hotter than the previous iPhones Apple has released. Sometimes the iPhone 8 is so warm that the users find it difficult to hold it down with their hands. This is a clear indication of overheating in the iPhone 8. Some similar cases of overheating include.

  • The phone gets way too hot while charging.
  • The phone gets hot, and the battery drains drastically.
  • The iPhone can perform simple tasks, e.g., making a phone call, watching a YouTube video, and taking a photo without getting hot.
  • The iPhone gets warm on standby mode for no apparent reason whatsoever.

(Note: if your phone gets too hot while transferring data for the first time from a previous iPhone, chances are it is a one-time issue and will not happen again.)

These are some of the most discussed problems in Apple’s user threads and community. However, there are some DIY (do it yourself) fixes that you may try that may help you to resolve your overheating issues...

  • Disable background app refresh.
  • Disable background app refresh from here: Settings > General > Background App Refresh
  • Turn off Bluetooth/location services to reduce processes running in the background.
  • Most of the users have reported they only get heating in older iOS. Try updating your iOS to later versions to check if it works for your phone.

data.description:
These power issues include:

  • The Phone does not turn on
  • The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked-out phone. Therefore you can not determine the problem.
  • iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.
  • iPhone doesn’t charge. It is stuck on the battery percentage you left it to charge on.
  • Can’t use the iPhone without keeping it on a constant power supply (eg: Connected to a wall adapter or power bank etc,)

These frustrating problems are however the most common issues found on iPhone 6s Plus. There are some widely renowned DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available on the internet which may help the issue on your device. Such as...

  • Force restarting your iPhone
  • Check Your Lightning cable and adapter and see if they are functioning properly.
  • Check if there is any debris on the iPhone 6s Plus charging porthole.
  • Limit background processes by stopping the background app refresh.
  • Try charging while keeping your phone switched off.
  • Sometimes excessive battery drain can be happening due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version.

If none of these methods work to resolve the issues on your smartphone, you might need to get it checked by professional technicians. data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone Xs comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature...

  • Face not recognized
  • Face ID is not available at the moment
  • Move the camera a bit lower/higher
  • Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID.

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

  • Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock.

Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

  • if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.
  • Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region.
  • Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy.
  • Update your iOS to the latest version.

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

  • User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone.
  • The user may have just restarted the device.
  • The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours.
  • The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days.
  • The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours.
  • The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space.
  • If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts.
  • If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all.

If your iPhone Xs Face ID problems can’t be categorized and sorted by the above-mentioned issues and fixes, you may just need to take it to an extremely diligent iPhone technician to deal with Face ID issues. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in issues regarding your iPhone Xs. ifixit bd is located in four different locations across Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Battery in critical condition — needs immediate replacement

Seven-plus years of charge cycles have severely degraded iPhone Xs batteries. Most units have dropped below 70% capacity and show iOS performance throttling, unexpected shutdowns, and very short on-time. Battery replacement at this device age is the repair we recommend before anything else. [→ iPhone Xs battery replacement]

Cracked OLED screen

The 5.8-inch Super Retina OLED panel produces permanent OLED damage — green lines, dead touch zones, and display bleed — when cracked. We replace the full assembly and verify Face ID sensor alignment post-repair. [→ iPhone Xs screen replacement]

Face ID failure

Face ID sensor failure on the iPhone Xs is common — TrueDepth sensors degrade with age and can be damaged by liquid ingress even on IP68-rated devices. A prior screen repair that broke sensor pairing is another frequent cause. [→ iPhone Xs Face ID repair]

Dual camera portrait mode blur or telephoto failure

The telephoto lens, OIS mechanism, and rear camera flex cable all wear over 7 years. Blur on the telephoto lens, Portrait Mode depth failure, and autofocus hunting are the common symptoms. [→ iPhone Xs camera repair]

Lightning port worn or charging slowly

Seven years of daily use compacts lint firmly and wears the Lightning port pins. Port cleaning and flex cable replacement are both available. [→ iPhone Xs charging issues]

data.description:
These common issues however can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 6s Plus. To resolve these Apple recommends its iPhone 6s Plus users some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

  • Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache.
  • Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. (requires a restart of the device)
  • Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.
  • To set up go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network

then:

  • Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier 
  • Insert Username (provided by your carrier)
  • Insert Password (provided by your carrier)
  • Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.
  • Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.
  • Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)
  • Restart your iPhone
  • Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to get checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving your network issues in your iPhone 6s Plus. ifixit bd has 4 service points which are located in points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Charge Draining Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone comes with a powerful battery. The battery is optimized perfectly for the phone.   • The battery of the iPhone 8 runs out after installing an app/ update of an app.
  • The iPhone Battery drains after the phone heats up too quickly.

  • Don’t overcharge/ Frequently charge your iPhone 8. It may reduce battery health.
  • Adjust your brightness settings in iPhone 8 to auto-brightness.
  • Turn off Background app refresh - From here: Settings > general > Background app refresh
  • Try running it on low power mode
  • from here: Settings > Battery > Low power mode ON
  • Turn off “reduce motion” to turn off aesthetic animations in your phone to save battery life might help
  • Turn it off from here: Settings > General > Accessibility > Reduce Motion

These are the most common issues found in the iPhone Xs proximity sensor. There are some DIY (do it yourself) fixes you may try that may solve issues regarding your proximity sensor if they are very minor. Apple recommends:
