data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 8 offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu.

This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

  • This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:
  • The iPhone has taken in some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)
  • Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss.
  • A third-party app may have access to vital permissions which can disrupt iPhones' productivity.
  • It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up.

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you...

  • Force Restart your iPhone 8
  • Update your iOS Software. 

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

  • Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from iStore.
  • Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work, for you. You might have an issue that needs the touch of a professional iPhone technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in fixing iPhones. ifixit bd is a prominent iPhone servicing center that is located in 4 locations around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

We offer service benefits for Apple logo issues for your iPhone 8. Not only will we provide the best available service for you, but you can also avail yourself.

  • Free Diagnostics to see what's wrong with your iPhone.
  • Quick service in applicable repair services
  • 30-days service warranty on applicable repairs
  • Money-back guarantee.

We understand how important your iPhone is to you, so to ensure top-notch quality we try to provide your servicing needs with original apple parts and accessories. We do not compromise with our quality.

data.title: Taptic Engine Issue
data.description:
The Taptic Engine in an iPhone Xs is responsible for providing haptic feedback, such as vibrations for notifications and the "click" sensation for the home button (on supported models). You might need to replace the Taptic Engine in your iPhone if you experience any of the following issues:

Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:

  • If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.
  • The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.
  • The Taptic Engine produces grinding or buzzing noises that were not present before.
  • Error messages or diagnostics indicate an issue with the Taptic Engine.

Possible Causes of Failure:

  • Physical Damage: Dropping the phone or exposing it to water can damage internal components.
  • Software Bugs: Sometimes, a software issue may mimic hardware failure. Perform a factory reset or update the iPhone before deciding on hardware repair.
  • Wear and Tear: Over time, mechanical components can degrade and stop working properly.

data.description:
The new iPhone Se 2022 offers a set of microphones to ensure your iPhone makes the best out of the audio inputs it receives. The iPhone offers the users a dual speaker and microphone to ensure the best listening experience for their users.

However, it is often reported by iPhone Se 2022 users that, they are getting trouble regarding the microphones in their phones. The most common issues reported in Apple’s user community forum and other blogs are:

Low or unclear voice in Facetime, skype, or video recording

Muffled or cracked sound while recording/calling using the mic

Siri doesn’t work/ can’t hear me/ can’t pick up commands

The iPhone Se 2022 has at least 3 different microphones in different places for the phone for different purposes

At the bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls

One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri

The one in the back of your in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any of the one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

Make sure if you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes

Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there

Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works

If the mic works in voice memo make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone Se 2022 go to: Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone XS MAX is a standard IP68 rated, dust and water-resistant phone. This means it can resist dust and water coming in up to a certain level. However, it is not completely immune to water getting inside the iPhone and damaging it. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water. However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY
  • If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.
  • If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers.

data.title: Mic Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone Xs Max offers a set of microphones to ensure your iPhone makes the best out of the audio inputs it receives. The iPhone offers the users a dual speaker and microphone to ensure the best listening experience for their users.

However, it is often reported by iPhone Xs Max users that, they are getting trouble regarding the microphones in their phones. The most common issues reported in Apple’s user community forum and other blogs are:

Low or unclear voice sound in voice calls/ voice memos.

Low or unclear voice in Facetime, skype, or video recording.

Muffled or cracked sound while recording/calling using the mic.

Siri doesn’t work/ can’t hear me/ can’t pick up commands.

The iPhone Xs Max has at least 3 different microphones in different places for phones for different purposes.

The bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls

One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri

The one in the back of your in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video.

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any of the one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

Make sure if you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes.

Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there.

Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works

If the mic works in voice memo make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone Xs Max

go to Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone.

If none of the fixes work for you, you may need it to be looked at by professional technicians. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving issues in your iPhone Xs Max. ifixit bd has multiple service points located in Dhaka, Bangladesh. We offer quick service for your ease of access. On top of that, we provide a 30-days service warranty for applicable services provided by us.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water. However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth

You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.

Never charge your phone until you have made sure it is completely dry

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth. If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers. data.title: Taptic Engine Issue

The Taptic Engine in an iPhone 11 Pro is responsible for providing haptic feedback, such as vibrations for notifications and the "click" sensation for the home button (on supported models). You might need to replace the Taptic Engine in your iPhone if you experience any of the following issues:

Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:

If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.

The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.

The Taptic Engine produces grinding or buzzing noises that were not present before.

Error messages or diagnostics indicate an issue with the Taptic Engine.

Possible Causes of Failure:

Physical Damage: Dropping the phone or exposing it to water can damage internal components.

Software Bugs: Sometimes, a software issue may mimic hardware failure. Perform a factory reset or update the iPhone before deciding on hardware repair.

Wear and Tear: Over time, mechanical components can degrade and stop working properly.

data.title: Temperature High Issue
data.description:

  • Phone gets hot and the battery drains drastically.
  • The iPhone can perform simple tasks e.g., Making a phone call, watching a YouTube video, taking a photo without getting hot.
  • The iPhone gets warm on standby mode for no apparent reasons whatsoever.

data.title: Audio Issue
data.description:
The iPhone 11 Pro is one of the best phones in the market, considering its audio output quality. It has a dual stereo speaker with noise cancellation and spatial audio features. It has two speaker grills in the bottom part of the phone. It should be kept in mind that, the left speaker grill is not a speaker but instead it is there to catch audio inputs for your voice calls and Siri. The audio-only comes out of the right speaker grill and it is not a faulty feature. The two speakers of the iPhone 11 pro are located on the top and the bottom of the phone. The top speaker also serves its purpose as an ear speaker when in calls.

However, some users have reported a lot of different audio issues. The most common audio issues faced by iPhone 11 pro users are:

  • No sound in audio playback
  • No sound in voice calls
  • Distorted sound/Low sound on the speakers
  • Headphones not working
  • Audio not working or audio levels low after an update
  • Phone stuck in Headphone mode
  • Ringer Switch not working/ Audio level increases or decreases automatically/ Physical audio level buttons not working

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “Do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. Those are:

  • Checking the ringer switch to see if it is on the sound mode
  • Restarting Your Phone
  • Disabling your Bluetooth in the iPhone 11 pro
  • Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode
  • Check sound notification settings and try turning noise cancellation off
  • Try using headphones and check if the sounds come okay in headphones
  • Try removing any protective cases
  • Clean the speaker grills for dirt and debris

if none of the fixes works for your phone you need to get it checked by professional technicians who specialize in repairing iPhone. data.title: Network Problem
data.description:
The iPhone 13 Mini comes with upgraded network connectivity compared to previous iPhone models and supports 5G network connectivity. Despite technological advancements from previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone 13 Mini network connectivity. Such as loss of the network, prompt disconnections, inability to find or locate the network.

The most common issues, however, are often discussed upon Apple’s user forum and the most common problems found regarding networks in iPhone 13 Mini are:

iPhone 13 Mini gets down to 0 network bars randomly

Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G

Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company

Network never reaches the full level

These common issues, however, can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 13 Mini. To resolve this, Apple recommends its iPhone 13 Mini users some DIY (do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache

Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. -requires a restart of the device

Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.

To set it up, go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network.

then:

Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier

Insert Username (provided by your carrier)

Insert Password (provided by your carrier)

Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.

Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.

Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)

Restart your iPhone

Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to be checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving your network issues with your iPhone 13 Mini. ifixit bd has 4 service points which are located in points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Taptic Engine Issue
data.description:
The Taptic Engine in an iPhone Se 2020 is responsible for providing haptic feedback, such as vibrations for notifications and the "click" sensation for the home button (on supported models). You might need to replace the Taptic Engine in your iPhone if you experience any of the following issues:

Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:

  • If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.
  • The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.

The iPhone 12 Pro Max comes with upgraded network connectivity than the previous iPhone models and supports 5G network connectivity. Despite these technological advancements from the previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone 12 Pro Max’s network connectivity. Such as loss in the network, prompt disconnections, inability to find or locate the network.

  • The most common issues however are often discussed upon Apple’s user forum and the most common problems found regarding network in iPhone 12 Pro Max are:

iPhone 12 Pro Max gets down to 0 network bars randomly

Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G

Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company

Network never reaches the full level

These common issues however can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 12 Pro Max. To resolve these Apple recommends its iPhone 12 Pro Max users some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache

Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. (requires a restart of the device)

Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.

To set up go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network

then:

Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier

Insert Username (provided by your carrier)

Insert Password (provided by your carrier)

Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.

Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.

Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)

Restart your iPhone

Soft reset your iPhone

data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 7 offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu.

  • This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.
  • This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:
  • The iPhone has taken in some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)
  • Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss.
  • A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity.

It is rare; however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up. These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

  • Force Restart your iPhone 7 (Press volume up (+) and then quickly press volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 7 power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software. (If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, you may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

  • Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM IN REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work, for you. You might have an issue that needs the touch of a professional iPhone technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in fixing iPhones. ifixit bd is a prominent iPhone servicing center that is located in 4 locations around Dhaka, Bangladesh. We understand how important your iPhone is to you, so to ensure top-notch quality we try to provide your servicing needs with original apple parts and accessories. We do not compromise with our quality. Battery completely depleted after years of use

Cracked LCD screen

The 4.7-inch LCD IPS Retina display cracks on drops. LCD-specific damage — white backlight bleed, colour banding, and unresponsive touch areas — require full assembly replacement. iPhone 7 screen replacement

Solid-state home button not responding

data.description:
It has two speaker grills in the bottom part of the phone. It should be kept in mind that the left speaker grill is not a speaker, but instead it is there to catch audio inputs for your voice calls and Siri. The audio only comes out of the right speaker grill, and it is not a faulty feature. The two speakers of the iPhone XS are located on the top and the bottom of the phone. The top speaker also serves its purpose as an ear speaker when in calls.

However, some users have reported a lot of different audio issues. The most common audio issues faced by iPhone XS users are

  • No sound in audio playback
  • No sound in voice calls
  • Distorted sound/low sound on the speakers
  • Headphones not working
  • Audio not working or audio levels low after an update.
  • Phone stuck in headphone mode
  • Ringer switch not working/audio level increases or decreases automatically/physical audio level buttons not working.

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. Those are

  • Checking the ringer switch to see if it is on the sound mode
  • Restarting Your Phone
  • Disabling your Bluetooth in the iPhone XS
  • Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode.
  • Check sound notification settings and try turning noise cancellation off.
  • Try using headphones and check if the sounds come through okay in headphones.
  • Try removing any protective cases.
  • Clean the speaker grills of dirt and debris.

If none of the fixes works for your phone, you need to get it checked by professional technicians who specialize in repairing iPhones. iPhone 6 repair service in Dhaka, Bangladesh

We repair every iPhone 6 fault — cracked Retina HD screens, dead batteries, charging port failures, liquid damage, and board-level logic board issues — using both A-grade and Original parts with full pricing transparency. Screen replacement starts from ৳1,800, battery replacement from ৳900, and every repair begins with a free written diagnosis. Most common repairs are completed same-day.

What are the common iPhone 6 problems we fix?

Battery draining fast or shutting down suddenly

Every iPhone 6 in use in 2026 is running a battery that is at minimum 10–12 years old. At that age, lithium-ion cells hold a fraction of their original capacity — you may see 15% drop to 0% with no warning, or the phone shut off at 30%. Battery replacement takes 30 minutes and is the single best-value repair for this device. We replace approximately iPhone 6 batteries every month across our Dhaka branches. [ iPhone 6 battery replacement]

Cracked or unresponsive screen

The iPhone 6's 4.7-inch Retina HD IPS LCD display is still a sharp, usable panel — worth replacing rather than tolerating cracks or dead touch zones. We fit a full display assembly (digitizer, LCD, and frame together) and run a post-repair touch calibration and colour check before handing the phone back. [ iPhone 6 screen replacement]

Not charging or charging only at an angle

The Lightning port on the iPhone 6 collects dust and pocket lint over years of use — often what feels like a charging fault is simply a blocked port. During every free diagnosis, our technicians clean the port first before recommending a flex cable replacement. If cleaning resolves it, you pay nothing. [→ iPhone 6 charging issues]

Home button not working or Touch ID failing

The physical home button on the iPhone 6 is a mechanical component that wears down over time — it can become stiff, stop clicking, or stop registering presses entirely. Touch ID fingerprint recognition can also stop working after the button degrades or following an unofficial repair elsewhere that broke the pairing between the button and the logic board. iFixit BD replaces the home button assembly and restores Touch ID function where the pairing is intact. [ iPhone 6 home button repair]

Liquid damage

The iPhone 6 has zero water resistance — there is no IP rating on this model. Liquid that enters the chassis reaches the A8 logic board within seconds and begins corroding metal traces immediately. If your iPhone 6 got wet, power it off and bring it to iFixit BD the same day. data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth

You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.

Never charge your phone until you have made sure it is completelty dry

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth. If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers. data.title: No Light On Display Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone XS MAX offers one of the best displays consisting of a Liquid Retina IPS LCD display and a significantly high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both back and front. However, not all damage in display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone XS MAX have reported a sudden black screen without any prior damage history. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone XS MAX is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

The Phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus)

The phone has calls, notifications but doesn’t show anything on display

iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display.

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone.

(Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen)

Connect the lightning cable, charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone.

UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issue. It might be risky for any layman person.

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving No light on display issues on your iPhone XS MAX. We are a service center that operates based on 4 different and convenient points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.description:
The new iPhone 14 Pro offers one of the best displays of high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both the back and the front. However, not all damage to the display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone 13 Pro Max have reported a sudden black screen with no prior damage history. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 14 Pro is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone is running okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. The phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

The phone's display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus) 

The phone has calls and notifications but doesn’t show anything on display

iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone. (Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen) 

Connect the lightning cable and charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone

UNCONVENTIONAL: Press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect to any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended, however, it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issues. It might be risky for any layman.

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. data.description:
The new iPhone 14 Pro offers a set of microphones to ensure your iPhone makes the best out of the audio inputs it receives. The iPhone offers the users a dual speaker and microphone to ensure the best listening experience for their users. However, it is often reported by iPhone 14 Pro users that, they are getting trouble regarding the microphones in their phones. The most common issues reported in Apple’s user community forum and other blogs are:

Low or unclear voice sound in voice calls/ voice memos

Low or unclear voice in Facetime, skype, or video recording

Muffled or cracked sound while recording/calling using the mic

Siri doesn’t work/ can’t hear me/ can’t pick up commands

The iPhone 14 Pro has at least 3 different microphones in different places for the phone for different purposes

At the bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls

One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri

The one in the back of your in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any of the one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

Make sure if you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes

Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there

Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works

If the mic works in voice memo make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone 14 Pro

go to: Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone. If none of the fixes work for you, you may need it to be looked at by professional technicians.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone 7 plus is not a standard IP68 rated, dust and water-resistant phone. Which means it can not resist dust and water coming in up to it. However, it can resist certain levels of water. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

  • If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:
  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY
  • If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.
  • If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers.

Force restarting your iPhone ( Press Volume up (+) and quickly press volume down (-) and then quickly press the power button to complete the restart process)

Check Your Lightning cable and adapter and see if they are functioning properly

Check if there is any debris on the iPhone 12 Pro charging porthole

Limit background processes by stopping the background app refresh

Try charging 20 minutes while keeping your phone switched off

Sometimes excessive battery drain can be happening due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version

data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro offers one of the best displays consisting of a Super AMOLED retina display and a significantly high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both back and front. However, not all damage in display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone 11 pro have reported a sudden black screen without any prior damage history. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 11 pro is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs.

But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls. The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

  • The Phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus)
  • The phone has calls, notifications but doesn’t show anything on display
  • iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display.

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone.

(Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen)

Connect the lightning cable, charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone.

UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issue. It might be risky for any layman person.

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 14 offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

The iPhone has taken some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss

A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity

It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 14

(Press volume up (+) and then quickly press the volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 14 power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work, for you. You might have an issue that needs the touch of a professional iPhone technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in fixing iPhones. ifixit bd is a prominent iPhone servicing center that is located in 4 locations around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Power Issue
data.description:
The iPhone 11 pro max comes with a 3969 MAh battery, which can support 18 Watt fast charging. To maintain the sleek and uniform design, Apple provided a power button at the side of the device. This correlation between the power button and the Battery is unavoidable for the perfect operation of the iPhone. The iPhone has been designed to maintain it. However, many users have complained about issues regarding issues in their power supply and other power-related errors in their iPhones.

These power issues include:

  • The Phone does not turn on
  • The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked-out phone. Therefore you can not determine the problem
  • iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.
  • iPhone doesn’t charge. It is stuck on the battery percentage you left it to charge on.
  • Can’t use the iPhone without keeping it on a constant power supply (eg: Connected to a wall adapter or power bank etc.

These frustrating problems are however the most common issues found on iPhone 11 pro max. There are some widely renowned DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available on the internet which may help the issue on your device. Such as...

  • Force restarting your iPhone ( Press Volume up (+) and quickly press volume down (-) and then quickly press the power button to complete the restart process)
  • Check Your Lightning cable and adapter and see if they are functioning properly
  • Check if there is any debris on the iPhone 11 pro max charging porthole
  • Limit background processes by stopping the background app refresh
  • Try charging 20 minutes while keeping your phone switched off
  • Sometimes excessive battery drain can be happening due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version

The new iPhone 15 has 3 physical buttons and 1 switch to ensure maximum accessibility to its users. The buttons and the switches are:

Volume Up (+) button

Volume down (-) button

Ringer Switch

Power Button

The buttons are stuck and can’t be pressed

data.title: Touch Issue
data.description:
The most common issues faced by the users that are reported in the iPhone 6s plus users community forum are as follows:

  • Too sensitive screen/screen response intermittently (means responses without the user having to input or auto touch)
  • Touchscreen in your iPhone does not respond at all
  • Ghost Touch / Delayed Touch issue
  • Touch doesn’t respond after dropping from hand. (Everything else seems to work fine)

There are some fixes you might try to see if any of them work for your phone. Those are the following listed below:

  • Make sure your touch screen protector doesn’t interfere with proper operation.
  • Make sure there’s no internal/external damage (cracking or shattering glass)
  • Disconnecting your USB-lightning port to check if it works. 
  • If your phone is above normal temperature wait for it to cool down and then try again.
  • Restart your device.

If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get your iPhone checked by professional technicians. iPhone 6 repair service in Dhaka, Bangladesh

With 18+ years of experience, 500,000+ devices repaired, and 70+ expert technicians across 4 dedicated branches in Dhaka, iFixit BD is one of Bangladesh's most established iPhone repair centres. We repair every iPhone 6 fault — cracked Retina HD screens, dead batteries, charging port failures, liquid damage, and board-level logic board issues — using both A-grade and Original parts with full pricing transparency. Screen replacement starts from ৳1,800, battery replacement from ৳900, and every repair begins with a free written diagnosis. Most common repairs are completed same-day.

What are the common iPhone 6 problems we fix?

Battery draining fast or shutting down suddenly

Every iPhone 6 in use in 2026 is running a battery that is at minimum 10–12 years old. At that age, lithium-ion cells hold a fraction of their original capacity — you may see 15% drop to 0% with no warning, or the phone shut off at 30%. Battery replacement takes 30 minutes and is the single best-value repair for this device. We replace approximately iPhone 6 batteries every month across our Dhaka branches. [ iPhone 6 battery replacement]

Cracked or unresponsive screen

The iPhone 6's 4.7-inch Retina HD IPS LCD display is still a sharp, usable panel — worth replacing rather than tolerating cracks or dead touch zones. We fit a full display assembly (digitizer, LCD, and frame together) and run a post-repair touch calibration and colour check before handing the phone back. [ iPhone 6 screen replacement]

Not charging or charging only at an angle

The Lightning port on the iPhone 6 collects dust and pocket lint over years of use — often what feels like a charging fault is simply a blocked port. During every free diagnosis, our technicians clean the port first before recommending a flex cable replacement. If cleaning resolves it, you pay nothing. [→ iPhone 6 charging issues]

Home button not working or Touch ID failing

The physical home button on the iPhone 6 is a mechanical component that wears down over time — it can become stiff, stop clicking, or stop registering presses entirely. Touch ID fingerprint recognition can also stop working after the button degrades or following an unofficial repair elsewhere that broke the pairing between the button and the logic board. iFixit BD replaces the home button assembly and restores Touch ID function where the pairing is intact. [ iPhone 6 home button repair]

Liquid damage

The iPhone 6 has zero water resistance — there is no IP rating on this model. Liquid that enters the chassis reaches the A8 logic board within seconds and begins corroding metal traces immediately. If your iPhone 6 got wet, power it off and bring it to iFixit BD the same day. We perform ultrasonic board cleaning using professional ultrasonic equipment and isopropyl alcohol (90%+) to remove corrosive mineral deposits before they cause permanent component failure. iPhone 6 liquid damage repair]

Won't turn on / boot loop / no service

If the iPhone 6 shows no response to the power button, restarts in a continuous loop, or shows no cellular service signal, the problem is at the board level. iFixit BD's micro-soldering lab diagnoses and repairs logic board faults — power management ICs, baseband chip failures, and boot-loop causes — that swap-only repair shops in Bangladesh cannot address. [ iPhone 6 software and boot issues]

How does our repair process work?

Step 1 — Free diagnosis. Bring your iPhone 6 to any iFixit BD branch. Our technician inspects the hardware and software, identifies the fault, and gives you a written quote at no cost.

Step 2 — Provide a report and a fixed price. You receive a clear fault report and a fixed price broken into parts and labour — A-grade and Original options shown side by side.

Step 3 — Confirm and repair. Once you approve, we begin. Most repairs are completed same day. Board-level repairs take 1–2 days.

Step 4 — Test together and collect with warranty. We test the repaired device with you present — screen response, battery charging, cellular signal, cameras — before you leave. Your [X]-month warranty starts from this moment.

iPhone 6 repair price list in ifixit BD?

data.title: Error Solution
data.description:
Sometimes when you update your iPhone, or when you try to run your phone you may see some sort of black screen with some sort of Error with a number on your iPhone’s screen out of nowhere. These messages with errors and numbers can be seen while booting up the phone or trying to upgrade the IPSW files from iTunes from a PC. These are Error Codes that indicate to the service technicians that a specific part of the iPhone is malfunctioning. These codes are used by professional repair technicians of iPhones to make their jobs easy. They do not need to diagnose the entire iPhone when they see the code. Therefore saves both the customer’s and the tech expert’s time and other resources.

Some of the common error codes seen on iPhones are as follows:

ERROR(9): This code shows when you are trying to upgrade your iOS through PC on iTunes, but the iTunes app shows an Error code-9. It is a relatable problem with iTunes error codes – 4013, 4014, and 4005.

Apple recommends:

To check if your iPhone is updated

If the update still fails try updating it from another pc

To check if the lightning cable works. (Error code 4013,4014 and 4015 usually indicate this issue)

Error 1015: This is an issue if you have a jailbroken device (iOS) and apple detects it.

Error 69: This is a common issue found in iPhone X and later devices. This issue suggests that there might be some sort of hardware error on your phone, which is repairable, to say the least.

Aside from these errors, there are a lot of errors that can occur on your iPhone. These are all listed on Apple’s error solution info page with possible DIY (Do it yourself) solutions. However, not all problems can be fixed only by DIY fixes. Some errors might require some handy work around the inner parts of the phone which should be done by a professional iPhone technician.This is where ifixit bd comes in, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving errors in iPhone Se 2022 or any other iPhone device. ifixit bd is a prominent Apple gadget servicing center based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. data.title: Network Problem
data.description:
The iPhone 11 comes with upgraded network connectivity than the previous iPhone models and supports 5G network connectivity. Despite these technological advancements from the previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone 11 network connectivity. Such as loss in the network, prompt disconnections, inability to find or locate the network.

The most common issues however are often discussed upon Apple’s user forum and the most common problems found regarding network in iPhone 11 are:

  • iPhone 11 gets down to 0 network bars randomly
  • Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G.
  • Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company.
  • Network never reaches the full level.

These common issues however can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 11. To resolve these Apple recommends its iPhone 11 users some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache.

Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. (requires a restart of the device)

Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.

To set up go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network

then:

Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier

Insert Username (provided by your carrier)

Insert Password (provided by your carrier)

Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.

Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.

Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)

Restart your iPhone

Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to get checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving your network issues in your iPhone 11. ifixit bd has 4 service points which are located in points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 12 Pro offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

The iPhone has taken in some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss

A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity

It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 12 Pro

(Press volume up (+) and then quickly press volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 12 Pro power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

4. Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

data.title: Taptic Engine Issue

The Taptic Engine in an iPhone X is responsible for providing haptic feedback, such as vibrations for notifications and the "click" sensation for the home button (on supported models). You might need to replace the Taptic Engine in your iPhone if you experience any of the following issues:

  • Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:
  • If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.
  • The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.
  • The Taptic Engine produces grinding or buzzing noises that were not present before.
  • Error messages or diagnostics indicate an issue with the Taptic Engine.

Possible Causes of Failure:

  • Physical Damage: Dropping the phone or exposing it to water can damage internal components.
  • Software Bugs: Sometimes, a software issue may mimic hardware failure. Perform a factory reset or update the iPhone before deciding on hardware repair.
  • Wear and Tear: Over time, mechanical components can degrade and stop working properly.

The proximity sensor is not working/ too sensitive. And turning the phone screen on and off during calls

The phone display doesn’t turn off during a phone call

The phone display doesn’t turn on automatically as it should after the phone call ends

These are the most common issues found in the iPhone 12 Pro proximity sensor. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes you may try which may solve issues regarding your proximity sensor if they are very minor. Apple recommends:

Try removing your screen protector which may block the proximity sensors' proper working

Restart your iPhone

Update your iOS

If you have already tried the above-mentioned fixes and none of the fixes work for you, you might need to get your phone checked by a professional technician. data.title: Audio Issue
data.description:
The iPhone 11 Pro Max is one of the best phones on the market, considering its audio output quality. It has a dual stereo speaker with noise cancellation and spatial audio features. It has two speaker grills in the bottom part of the phone. It should be kept in mind that the left speaker grill is not a speaker, but instead it is there to catch audio inputs for your voice calls and Siri. The audio only comes out of the right speaker grill, and it is not a faulty feature. The two speakers of the iPhone 11 Pro Max are located on the top and the bottom of the phone. The top speaker also serves its purpose as an ear speaker when in calls.

However, some users have reported a lot of different audio issues. The most common audio issues faced by iPhone 11 Pro Max users are

  • No sound in audio playback
  • No sound in voice calls
  • Distorted sound/low sound on the speakers
  • Headphones not working
  • Audio not working or audio levels low after an update.
  • Phone stuck in headphone mode
  • Ringer switch not working/audio level increases or decreases automatically/physical audio level buttons not working.

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “Do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. Those are:

  • Checking the ringer switch to see if it is on the sound mode
  • Restarting Your Phone
  • Disabling your Bluetooth in the iPhone 11 Pro Max
  • Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode.
  • Check sound notification settings and try turning noise cancellation off.
  • Try using headphones and check if the sounds come through okay in headphones.
  • Try removing any protective cases
  • Clean the speaker grills of dirt and debris.

If none of the fixes works for your phone, you need to get it checked by professional technicians who specialize in repairing iPhones. In iFixit BD, we have experienced technicians who specialize in repairing iPhone 11 Pro Max. Our service points are located at locations in Dhaka, Bangladesh. We also offer quick service for your ease of access, and on top of that, a 30-day warranty on applicable services you receive from ifixit bd. We do not compromise your phone’s well-being and use genuine Apple parts for the repair and replacement of your iPhone issues. Visit your nearest iFixit BD service point for fixing your iPhone 11 Pro Max audio or any other issues.

iPhone 17 Pro Max Original Display

This is a genuine Apple Super Retina XDR OLED display assembly for the iPhone 17 Pro Max, pulled from an original device — not an aftermarket or copy screen. The assembly includes the complete factory display stack: the LTPO OLED panel, the integrated touch layer, and the Ceramic Shield 2 front glass with Apple's anti-reflective coating. Every unit is function-tested before sale and comes with an 18-month warranty against display defects.

Display Technology and Specifications

The iPhone 17 Pro Max carries the largest and most advanced panel in the iPhone 17 lineup, and because this unit is pulled from a genuine device, every specification below is the factory specification.

Panel: 6.9-inch Super Retina XDR OLED with LTPO technology and a resolution of 2868×1320 pixels at 460 pixels per inch, with a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio and true blacks from self-emissive OLED pixels.

ProMotion adaptive refresh: The LTPO panel dynamically scales from 1Hz to 120Hz — full 120Hz smoothness for scrolling and gaming, dropping to 1Hz for static content, which is what enables the Always-On display without significant battery drain. Aftermarket panels are typically fixed at 60Hz and cannot support Always-On; this one behaves exactly like the factory screen because it is one.

Brightness: 1,000 nits typical maximum, 1,600 nits peak for HDR, and 3,000 nits peak outdoor brightness. Combined with the factory anti-reflective coating, the display stays fully readable in direct Dhaka sunlight, where lower-grade panels wash out.

Color and calibration: Full P3 wide color gamut with Apple's factory calibration, True Tone, and HDR support including Dolby Vision.

Front glass: Ceramic Shield 2 with approximately 3× the scratch resistance of the original Ceramic Shield, plus the anti-reflective, fingerprint-resistant coating.

Integrated components: Factory touch digitizer with 120Hz touch sampling, Haptic Touch, ambient light sensing, and the Dynamic Island cutout at correct tolerances for the TrueDepth system.

What "Pulled From a Genuine iPhone" Means?

This display is disassembled from a genuine iPhone 17 Pro Max, which means the panel was manufactured by Apple's display supplier and passed Apple's quality control. A pulled original panel is the closest thing to a factory display that can be purchased — the same OLED substrate, color calibration profile, and touch layer that shipped with the phone. Every unit is inspected and function-tested at our branch before sale.

How It Compares With Aftermarket and Copy Panels ?

The technical gap between grades is measurable. Aftermarket "original quality" panels typically run at a fixed 60Hz, lose Always-On support, reach noticeably lower peak brightness, and often lose True Tone. Copy panels (Incell/TFT) drop further — no ProMotion, washed-out color, weaker touch sampling, and short lifespans. The pulled original panel is the only grade that preserves the complete 17 Pro Max specification: LTPO 1–120Hz, 3,000-nit outdoor brightness, factory calibration, and Ceramic Shield 2. If you want a lower-cost 120Hz option, see our iPhone 17 Pro Max High Quality Display — we sell both grades openly so you can choose with full information.

Compatibility

This display fits the iPhone 17 Pro Max only. It is not compatible with the iPhone 17 Pro (6.3-inch, 2622×1206), iPhone 17, iPhone Air, or iPhone 17e — panel size, resolution, and connectors differ.

iPhone 17 Pro Max Original Display Price in Bangladesh

The original iPhone 17 Pro Max display costs Tk 58,000 at iFixit BD, including an 18-month warranty against display defects and per-unit testing before sale. As the largest and most advanced panel in the iPhone 17 lineup, this is the most premium display part we stock — the price reflects a genuine pulled Apple LTPO panel with the complete factory specification. If your budget calls for a lower price point with 120Hz preserved, our iPhone 17 Pro Max High Quality Display is the alternative, sold openly as an aftermarket grade.

Condition, Warranty, and Ordering

Every unit is a tested, fully functional pull in excellent condition, priced at Tk 58,000 and backed by an 18-month warranty against display defects plus a 30-day money-back guarantee (see our Refund Policy). Order on WhatsApp, call 01613338800, or visit any iFixit BD branch in Dhaka.

iPhone 17 Pro Max repair service in Dhaka, Bangladesh

With 18+ years of experience, 500,000+ devices repaired, and 70+ expert technicians across 4 dedicated branches in Dhaka, iFixit BD repairs every iPhone 17 Pro Max fault. Apple's 2025 flagship packs a 6.9-inch ProMotion OLED display, A19 Pro chip, titanium frame, and a triple-camera system with periscope telephoto. We fix cracked ProMotion displays, dead batteries, USB-C port faults, camera system failure, and board-level issues using both A-grade and Original parts. Screen replacement starts from ৳15,000, battery from ৳3,500, and every repair begins with a free written diagnosis.

What are the common iPhone 17 Pro Max problems we fix?

Battery draining faster than expected

The A19 Pro chip under ProMotion 120Hz and 5G connectivity draws significant power. After 12–18 months of heavy use, capacity drops and you notice the phone losing charge faster and shutting off before reaching 0%. Battery replacement restores full all-day performance and is a same-day repair. iPhone 17 Pro Max battery replacement

Cracked ProMotion OLED display

The 6.9-inch Super Retina XDR ProMotion display is the most expensive single component on this phone. Even a corner drop from moderate height can crack the glass or cause OLED bleed and dead zones. We replace the full assembly with A-grade or Original panels, verify ProMotion and TrueDepth alignment post-repair. iPhone 17 Pro Max screen replacement

Titanium frame damage creating gaps

The titanium frame is harder than steel but thin at the corners. Drops on a corner edge can bend the frame and break the IP68 dust and water seal, allowing moisture and dust to reach internal components. iFixit BD's housing repair service straightens frame deformation and replaces housing when required. iPhone 17 Pro Max housing repair

Triple camera malfunction — blur, lens switching failure, overheating

The three-lens camera system with periscope telephoto is precision hardware. Impact to the camera island, moisture in the lens module, or damaged flex cables can cause blur, failure to switch between lenses, or the camera app crashing during video. We diagnose each camera module independently and replace only what is confirmed faulty. iPhone 17 Pro Max camera repair

USB-C port failing or charging intermittently

Lint, moisture, or physical damage to the USB-C port causes intermittent power delivery, slow data transfer, or no connection. We clean the port during free diagnosis first — replacement is only recommended when the flex cable itself is confirmed damaged. iPhone 17 Pro Max charging issues

Face ID not working after drop or previous repair

The TrueDepth sensor cluster in the Dynamic Island controls Face ID. A drop to the front of the device, or a screen repair elsewhere that damaged the sensor pairing, can disable Face ID. iFixit BD protects TrueDepth function during screen replacements and can diagnose sensor damage independently. iPhone 17 Pro Max Face ID issues

data.title: Audio Issue
data.description:
The iPhone XR is one of the best phones on the market, considering its audio output quality. It has a dual stereo speaker with noise cancellation and spatial audio features. It has two speaker grills in the bottom part of the phone. It should be kept in mind that the left speaker grill is not a speaker, but instead it is there to catch audio inputs for your voice calls and Siri. The audio only comes out of the right speaker grill, and it is not a faulty feature. The two speakers of the iPhone XR are located on the top and the bottom of the phone. The top speaker also serves its purpose as an ear speaker when in calls.

However, some users have reported a lot of different audio issues. The most common audio issues faced by iPhone XR users are

  • No sound in audio playback
  • No sound in voice calls
  • Distorted sound/low sound on the speakers
  • Headphones not working
  • Audio not working or audio levels low after an update.
  • Phone stuck in headphone mode
  • Ringer switch not working/audio level increases or decreases automatically/physical audio level buttons not working.

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. Those are

  • Checking the ringer switch to see if it is on the sound mode
  • Restarting Your Phone
  • Disabling your Bluetooth in the iPhone XR
  • Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode.
  • Check sound notification settings and try turning noise cancellation off.
  • Try using headphones and check if the sounds come through okay in headphones.
  • Try removing any protective cases.
  • Clean the speaker grills of dirt and debris.

If none of the fixes works for your phone, you need to get it checked by professional technicians who specialize in repairing iPhones. In ifixit bd, we have experienced technicians who specialize in repairing iPhone XR. Our service points are located at locations in Dhaka, Bangladesh. We also offer quick service for your ease of access, and on top of that, a 30-day warranty on applicable services you receive from ifixit bd.

Battery not lasting through the day

The iPhone Xr's large battery was a standout feature in 2018. After 7+ years, capacity has dropped significantly — most units today need charging by midday. Battery replacement restores the excellent battery life the Xr is known for. [→ iPhone Xr battery replacement]

The 6.1-inch LCD IPS display cracks and shows LCD-specific damage — white spots, expanding dark bleed patches, and inverted corner colours. Unlike OLED, LCD damage can appear localised at first but spreads over time if left unrepaired. [→ iPhone Xr screen replacement]

The single 12MP wide camera lacks OIS. Drops that impact the rear glass crack the camera lens or misalign the module. Blur, autofocus failure, and camera app crashes are the visible results. [→ iPhone Xr camera repair]

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water. However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth

You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.

NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.

If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers. The new iPhone XR offers its users a dual-front camera for an enhanced photography experience. Some users have reported specific issues where they are not getting the desired type of photographs from the front camera of the iPhone XR. These complaints are mostly about the quality of the photograph itself and not about specific hardware or software problems regarding the front camera.

However, there have been issues regarding the front camera, which can be labeled as faulty camera issues. Complaints like that are

  • No display/black screen in the camera.
  • Blurry Photos
  • Face ID not working properly
  • The camera is not working after an iOS update.
  • Degraded Photo Quality (Photos looked good before, but they look bad now.)

These are some of the most common issues found in an iPhone XR smartphone. There are some quick fixes available for you to do at home to fix yourself. Some good initiatives include

  • Remove any protective case that may be metallic or have magnets. Sometimes it gets in the way of a camera’s proper functioning.
  • Clean your lens with a microfiber cloth. Make sure not to scratch it.
  • Try closing your voiceover settings. Available in Settings > General > Accessibility > Turn off VoiceOver. Some users have reported that turning off voice-over helps to fix some front camera issues.

If none of the methods work, you may try to reset your phone. Back up all of your personal data before doing so. If resetting your phone doesn’t resolve your iPhone XR front camera issues, you may need to get it looked at by professional technicians. Now you can repair your faulty touch mechanism of the iPhone Se 2022 without having to change the entire display! Since the launch of the new iPhone X models, Apple has introduced a technology that separates the touch mechanism and upper glasses from the entire display. Signs that indicate a faulty touch mechanism in iPhone Se 2022 are...

Doesn’t work or No response / Program doesn’t open or respond after touching the icon

Delayed response or wrong response (Clicking on one place but the phone registers the touch elsewhere and opens an unrelated app)

Takes multiple touch attempts to open an app or perform an action on the phone.

If you see any of the signs on your phone you can safely assume that the touch mechanism is faulty and should be replaced. Because Apple uses Haptic touch on iPhone Se 2022 and haptic touch ensures that there’s no struggle to operate the phone by touching it.

So, if you are facing any of the issues listed above, visit your nearest ifixit bd service point. We have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in iPhone Se 2022 services. Battery draining quickly on a small capacity cell

The 4.7-inch iPhone SE 2022 has a physically small battery — smaller than any other current iPhone. Combined with 5G connectivity and A15 performance demands, battery life was already limited from day one. After regular use, capacity drops further and the phone needs charging multiple times daily. Cracked small 4.7-inch LCD screen

A corner drop on the small body transfers more energy to the glass. Cracked screens and unresponsive touch are common results. iPhone SE 2022 screen replacement

Touch ID home button failing or not reading fingerprints

Normal mechanical wear, accidental liquid exposure, and prior repairs at non-specialist shops can all cause Touch ID to fail or the button to stop clicking. iFixit BD replaces the button assembly and restores Touch ID where the board-level pairing is intact. iPhone SE 2022 Touch ID / home button repair

Some of the common error codes seen in the iPhones are as follows: ERROR(9): This code shows when you are trying to upgrade your iOS through PC on iTunes, but the iTunes app shows an Error code-9. It is a relatable problem with iTunes error code – 4013, 4014, and 4005.

Apple recommends:

  • To check if your iPhone is updated
  • To check if the lightning cable works. (Error code 4013,4014 and 4015 usually indicate this issue)
  • If the update still fails try updating from another pc.
  • Error 1015: This is an issue if you have a jailbroken device (iOS) and apple detects it.
  • Error 69: This is a common issue found in iPhone X and later devices. This issue suggests that there might be some sort of hardware error on your phone, which is repairable, to say the least.

Aside from these errors, there are a lot of errors that can occur on your iPhone. These are all listed on Apple’s error solution info pages with possible DIY (Do it yourself) solutions. data.description:
Most users have reported that the iPhone’s battery starts draining after the system has updated. Several other issues may cause battery drain issues also. These issues include:

  • The battery of the iPhone 7 runs out too quickly after the update
  • The battery of the iPhone 7 runs out after installing an app/ update of an app.
  • The iPhone Battery drains after the phone heats up too quickly.

These are the most common problems regarding battery-draining found on the internet. Your issues may be one of them or not listed! However, we recommend trying some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may resolve your issue.

  • Turn off background iCloud/itunes sync to save battery by a considerable amount.
  • When not in use turn off WiFi/Cellular Data/Location/Bluetooth service in your iPhone
  • Don’t overcharge/ Frequently charge your iPhone 7. It may reduce battery health.
  • Adjust your brightness settings in iPhone 7 to auto-brightness.
  • Turn off Background app refresh
  • From here: Settings > general > Background app refresh
  • Try running it on low power mode from here: Settings > Battery > Low power mode ON
  • Turn off “reduce motion” to turn off aesthetic animations in your phone to save battery life might help
  • Turn it off from here: Settings > General > Accessibility > Reduce Motion

If none of the aforementioned procedures work to resolve your battery draining issues, it may need to be looked at by a professional technician to get them resolved. data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone 12 is a standard IP68 rated, dust and water-resistant phone. This means it can resist dust and water coming in up to a certain level. However, it is not completely immune to water getting inside the iPhone and damaging it. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth

You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there

NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth

If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers.

Introduction

Liquid damage on iPhone 17e causes short circuits, display malfunction, and sudden power failure within minutes of exposure. Water or any conductive liquid directly affects the Apple motherboard and interrupts core iOS system stability.

The iPhone internal structure uses tightly packed components like the charging IC, power IC, Face ID module, and OLED connectors. When liquid enters the device, these circuits oxidize and lose electrical conductivity.

Even small exposure from rain, spills, or humidity in Dhaka, Bangladesh leads to delayed failures. The device may work temporarily, then show random shutdowns, no charging, or distorted display behavior.

iFixit BD performs structured liquid damage diagnostics using board-level inspection and cleaning. Each device is tested to identify whether recovery is possible through component restoration or full module replacement using original and high-quality parts.

data.title: Audio Issue
data.description:
The iPhone 13 Pro is one of the best phones on the market, considering its audio output quality. It has a dual stereo speaker with noise cancelation and spatial audio features. It has two speaker grills in the bottom part of the phone. Should keep in mind that, the left speaker grill is not a speaker but instead it is there to catch audio inputs for your voice calls and Siri. The audio-only comes out of the right speaker grill and is not a faulty feature. The two speakers of the iPhone 13 Pro are located on the top and the bottom of the phone. The top speaker also serves its purpose as an ear speaker when in calls. However, some users have reported a lot of different audio issues.

The most common audio issues faced by iPhone 13 Pro users are:

No sound on audio playback

No sound on voice calls

Distorted/Low sound on the speakers

Headphones not working

Audio not working or audio levels low after an update.

Phone stuck in Headphone mode

Ringer Switch not working/ Audio level increases or decreases automatically/ Physical audio level buttons not working.

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “Do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. They are:

Check the ringer switch to see if it is on sound mode

Restarting Your Phone

Disabling your Bluetooth on the iPhone 13 Pro

Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode

Check the sound notification settings and try turning noise cancelation off.

Try using headphones and check if the sounds come okay in headphones.

Try removing any protective cases

Clean speaker grills for dirt and debris

if none of the fixes work for your phone, you need to get it checked by professional technicians who specialize in repairing iPhones.
