data.title: Network Problem
data.description:
The iPhone X comes with upgraded network connectivity than the previous iPhone models and supports 5G network connectivity. Despite these technological advancements from the previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone X network connectivity. Such as loss in the network, prompt disconnections, inability to find or locate the network.

The most common issues however are often discussed upon Apple’s user forum and the most common problems found regarding network in iPhone X are:

  • iPhone X gets down to 0 network bars randomly
  • Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G.
  • Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company.
  • Network never reaches the full level.

These common issues however can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone X. To resolve these Apple recommends its iPhone X users some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

  • Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache.
  • Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. (requires a restart of the device)
  • Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.
  • To set up go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network

then:

  • Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier
  • Insert Username (provided by your carrier)
  • Insert Password (provided by your carrier)
  • Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.
  • Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.
  • Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)
  • Restart your iPhone
  • Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to get checked by a professional technician. data.title: Charging Issues
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro Max has a beautiful battery that is optimized for using it for a reasonable amount of time. However, most of the users have complained the iPhone 11 Pro Max charges very slowly in comparison to other smartphones on the market with almost the same range. The Apple company recommends that you use an Apple 18-W USB Type-C charging brick if you face a slow charging issue. Which is the default charger with the iPhone 11 Pro Max? Apple claims this charging brick can shoot your charging time up to 50% in 30 minutes only!

However, even with an 18 W charger, some users face issues while charging their iPhone 11 Pro Max. The most common issues are as follows:

  • The iPhone 11 Pro Max charges slowly or not at all.
  • The iPhone is not charging beyond 80%.
  • An alert that shows that the accessory you are using to charge the iPhone is not certified or supported

These are the most reported issues for an iPhone 11 Pro Max with faulty charging. You may try some home fixes that may resolve the issues.

  • Try changing the wall adapter or cable.
  • Check if there is no debris or dirt in both the charging dock and the charging adapter.
  • Make sure the USB is connected firmly on both ends.
  • Check the charging adapter or the Lightning cable for visible signs of damage. Example: bent pin, loose cable, etc.
  • If you have iOS 14 or above, make sure you uncheck the “optimized battery charging” option to make sure it charges beyond 80 %.
  • To disable it go to Settings > Battery > Battery Health > Optimized Battery Charging.
  • Make sure you have no damage in your charging dock if an unsupported device warning shows.

If none of the fixes seem to work for resolving your iPhone 11 Pro Max charging issues,. You may need to get it looked at by professionals. data.title: Boot Loop
data.description:
The iPhone 14 pro max offers the users a new iOS version (iOS 13 upgradable to iOS 14) and updates it forward. Users need to update iOS regularly to maintain the stable and smooth operation of the iPhone. However, sometimes a user may face some unforeseen problems. This issue happens mostly when there is a failed or interrupted software update happens on your phone. Also, other issues may cause your phone to boot loop such as:

Hardware Damage.

Physical Damage (Dropping the phone from your hand, etc.)

The battery connector may have gotten loose or have gone bad.

Improper or failed update that is missing necessary files to get the phone started.

If you think one of the above issues is causing the boot looping error on your phone, you may just try these fixes listed below and see if they work to resolve your issue.

Force Restart Your iPhone 14 pro max

(press the volume up button (+) then release the button. And then quickly press and release the volume down (-) and then hold the power button again until your screen turns black and shows the apple logo)

Check if your iPhone is fully charged or is charging properly.

Connect your iPhone to your computer and try restoring or updating the software through the iTunes application.

If your phone still doesn’t recover from boot looing after trying these fixes, something may have gone wrong which can only be fixed by a professional iPhone technician. This is where ifixit bd comes in, ifixit bd is a prominent iPhone servicing center that has 4 different service points ranging in Dhaka, Bangladesh. MacBook Air 13 inch M1 motherboard repair in Bangladesh

MacBook Air 13 inch M1 motherboard repair is the process of finding and fixing the broken part on the main circuit board (called the logic board) of a MacBook Air A2337, or replacing the full board when the damage is too severe. Logic board failure in the MacBook Air M1 shows up as the laptop not turning on, crashing repeatedly, or the charging port stopping working. In Bangladesh, MacBook Air M1 repair costs range from 8,000 BDT to 70,000 BDT depending on whether a small chip repair or a full board replacement is needed.ifixit BD specializes in chip-level MacBook logic board repair in Bangladesh, using micro-soldering tools to fix the broken part without losing your saved data.

What is MacBook Air 13 inch M1 motherboard repair?

MacBook Air 13 inch M1 motherboard repair is the process of diagnosing and fixing a broken part on the logic board of the MacBook Air A2337, or replacing the full logic board when the damage cannot be repaired at the component level. The logic board is the main circuit board inside the MacBook Air M1 — it is the most important part of the laptop because it holds the Apple M1 chip, the RAM, the storage (SSD), and all the controllers that run the ports and screen.

The MacBook Air M1 (model A2337) is different from older Intel MacBooks in one important way: Apple placed the M1 chip, RAM, and SSD all on one single logic board through Apple M1 chip integration and a unified memory architecture design. The SSD storage is soldered MacBook directly to this board, meaning the storage and data cannot be moved to a different board. This makes MacBook Air A2337 motherboard component repair skill very important — a wrong repair move can cause permanent data loss.

If you have dirt, dust, or debris on your iPhone it may get in the way of your phone's functionality, for example:

  • Dirt can get in your charging dock and can cause interruptions in charging

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service restores your damaged handset to full working order through diagnostics, component replacement, and function testing. The service covers screen repair, battery replacement, charging port repair, back glass replacement, camera repair, Face ID repair, speaker and microphone repair, water damage repair, logic board repair, and software fault repair.

Repair costs sit in three tiers. Entry-level jobs like a charging port cleanup cost the least, mid-level jobs like a battery replacement land in the middle, and premium jobs like an OLED display swap cost the most. Screen replacement pricing follows the same three tiers.

Turnaround times vary by repair type. A battery swap wraps up same day, while logic board and water damage work takes longer because part availability drives the schedule.

You pick the replacement part grade before work starts. New genuine parts, used genuine parts, OEM-grade parts, and certified after-market parts each carry a different price and a different effect on parts and service history reporting. Every repair ships with a parts and labor warranty.

Booking takes six steps, starting with a free diagnostic and ending when you collect a function-tested device. Walk in or reserve your slot ahead — booking ahead locks in the part you need.

What is an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair service is a technical service that diagnoses faults in an Apple iPhone 16 Pro Max, replaces the failed component, and verifies device function before handover. The service addresses display faults, power faults, camera faults, audio faults, liquid damage, and board-level faults. Every repair starts with a free diagnostic check that identifies the failed component before you approve any cost. Each completed repair passes a function test that confirms the repaired component and the surrounding systems operate correctly.

The iPhone 16 Pro Max repairs covered by this service are listed below.

  • iPhone 16 Pro Max screen repair — Replaces the cracked or unresponsive 6.9-inch LTPO OLED display assembly and calibrates True Tone, brightness, and touch response after fitting.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max battery replacement — Installs a new battery when battery health drops below 80 percent, then calibrates the cell so battery health reporting reads accurately.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max charging port repair — Restores the USB-C connector when the device charges intermittently, rejects accessories, or stops recognizing a cable.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max back glass replacement — Replaces the cracked rear glass panel and reseals the housing so the device retains its water resistance rating.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max camera repair — Replaces the rear camera module, front camera assembly, LiDAR sensor, or camera lens when images blur, shake, or fail to focus.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max facial recognition repair — Restores the TrueDepth camera and dot projector so Face ID authenticates, unlocks the device, and authorizes Apple Pay.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max speaker repair — Replaces the loudspeaker or earpiece when call audio distorts, media playback crackles, or one channel goes silent.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max microphone repair — Replaces the microphone assembly when callers hear you faintly, voice memos record silence, or Siri stops responding.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max water damage repair — Removes corrosion from the board with ultrasonic cleaning, replaces oxidized components, and restores the affected circuits.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max logic board repair — Repairs the failed integrated circuit at chip level when the device shows a boot loop, no power, or no display output.
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max software fault repair — Recovers iOS when the device sticks on the Apple logo, restarts repeatedly, or fails a firmware update.

How much does an iPhone 16 Pro Max repair cost?

An iPhone 16 Pro Max repair costs between BDT 2,500 and BDT 55,000, depending on the failed component and the replacement part grade you select. The component determines the base cost, and the part grade adjusts it. You receive a written quotation after the free diagnostic, and that figure holds through the repair.

Entry-level repairs cost between BDT 2,500 and BDT 6,000. This tier covers charging port cleaning, speaker replacement, microphone replacement, button repair, and software fault recovery. These repairs use inexpensive components and finish quickly.

Mid-level repairs cost between BDT 7,000 and BDT 18,000. This tier covers battery replacement, charging port replacement, rear camera replacement, front camera replacement, and back glass replacement. These repairs use moderately priced modules and require housing disassembly.

Premium repairs cost between BDT 20,000 and BDT 55,000. This tier covers OLED display replacement, Face ID and TrueDepth camera repair, water damage restoration, and logic board repair. Display assemblies and board-level work carry the highest component and labor cost on the iPhone 16 Pro Max.

You confirm the exact figure for your device during the free diagnostic, since the same symptom sometimes traces to different components.

How much does an iPhone 16 Pro Max screen replacement cost?

data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 13 mini offers its users better optimization and balance in software than previous iPhone models. However, no matter how hard they try, there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning.The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it gets stuck on the boot menu. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

This Stuck on the Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

The iPhone has caused some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

Update disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss

A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity

It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up

These issues, however, can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps to see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 13 mini

(Press the volume up (+) and then quickly press the volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 13 mini power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS app to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

So, visit your nearest ifixit bd service point to avail the best iPhone servicing available to you for your iPhone 13 mini “Stuck on apple logo” issue or any other iPhone issue for that matter.

data.title: Charging Dock Replacement
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 comes with a lightning port which is one of the most important parts of the smartphone. It can be charged with a lightning cable and charges at a whopping 18 Watt (fast charging). This can charge your phone to 50 percent in 30 minutes. And it can also be used as a USB 2.0 port. However, after using the phone for a long time or by an accident; your charging dock of the phone may get faulty or damaged, and you might need to get it replaced.

The most common issues of the iPhone 11 charging dock are:

  • The battery charges very slowly
  • iPhone 11 not charging beyond 80 %.
  • Charging Not available or Liquid has been detected in the charging port error.
  • The charging dock can’t be connected to a USB supported device through the lightning cable

If your phone has any one of these issues or something not mentioned in the list of the common issues. You will still like to check out these DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may solve the problem regarding the charging dock in your iPhone 11.

  • Make sure you don’t have any debris or dirt on your charging dock. This may prevent charging.
  • Make sure your power outlet isn’t faulty.
  • Make sure you do not have the “optimized battery charging” option checked on your iPhone 11. if you do have it make sure to disable it to charge your phone past 80%.
  • Disable optimized Charging in here: Settings > Battery > Battery Health.
  • Note: This option is only available on iOS 13 or later updates.

If your phone is wet, wait until it is dry to charge your phone. If none of the fixes cut it for you, you may need to get your phone looked at by professionals. data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone xr comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature...

  • Face not recognized
  • Face ID is not available at the moment
  • Move the camera a bit lower/higher
  • Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID.

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

  • Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode
  • if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.
  • Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region.
  • Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy.
  • Update your iOS to the latest version.

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompts with a passcode. The reasons may be:

  • User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone.
  • The user may have just restarted the device.
  • The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours.
  • The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days.
  • The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours.
  • The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space.
  • If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts.
  • If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all.

If your iPhone xr Face ID problems can’t be categorized and sorted by the above-mentioned issues and fixes, you may just need to take it to an extremely diligent iPhone technician to deal with Face ID issues. data.title: Mic Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro max offers a set of microphones to ensure your iPhone makes the best out of the audio inputs it receives. The iPhone offers the users a dual speaker and microphone to ensure the best listening experience for their users. However, it is often reported by iPhone 11 pro max users that, they are getting trouble regarding the microphones in their phones. The most common issues reported in Apple’s user community forum and other blogs are:

  • Low or unclear voice sound in voice calls/ voice memos
  • Low or unclear voice in Facetime, skype, or video recording
  • Muffled or cracked sound while recording/calling using the mic
  • Siri doesn’t work/ can’t hear me/ can’t pick up commands

The iPhone 11 pro max has at least 3 different microphones in different places for the phone for different purposes.

  • The bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls
  • One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri
  • The one in the back of your in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video.

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any of the one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY(Do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

  • Make sure if you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes
  • Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there
  • Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works

If the mic works in voice memo make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone 11 pro max go to Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone.

If none of the fixes work for you, you may need it to be looked at by professional technicians. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving issues in your iPhone 11 pro max.

data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 16 Pro comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

The face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way

Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts

If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all

If your iPhone 16 Pro Face ID problems can’t be categorized and sorted by the above-mentioned issues and fixes, you may just need to take it to an extremely diligent iPhone technician to deal with Face ID issues. data.title: Wifi Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 14 has new wireless firmware that can support up to 7GHz of wireless bandwidth speed. This gives the users unmatched speed in comparison to most of the smartphones in the market. However, there have been issues regarding the Wi-Fi of the iPhone 14. And frankly, some users have taken issue with the phone saying that the phone disconnects from the wireless network frequently and without any warning. Other issues like high ping or latency have often been reported by the users of the phone. The most commonly reported iPhone 14 Wi-Fi issues are…

  • Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone 14
  • Wi-Fi stays connected but there is no internet on the receiver
  • Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/ non-metered connections on Wi-Fi
  • High Latency/Ping on Wi-Fi connections
  • iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi
  • iPhone can’t discover your Wi-Fi connection

These Wi-Fi issues found on iPhone 14 are pretty common issues found on other wireless-supported devices too! It also does not necessarily indicate that there is anything specifically wrong with your iPhone 14 wireless hardware. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

  • Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issue has been resolved
  • Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again
  • Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection
  • Restore the default network connection

(Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > * Enter Passcode * > Confirm)

  • Update your iOS to the latest version available

If none of the solutions mentioned above work to resolve your Wi-Fi issue on your iPhone 14, you may need to get it checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and professional technicians who specialize in repairing iPhone 14 Wi-Fi and its related issues. iFixit bd has 4 service points located in prominent locations around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Charging Issues
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro has a beautiful battery that is optimized for using it for a reasonable amount of time. However, most of the users have complained the iPhone 11 Pro charges very slowly in comparison to other smartphones on the market with almost the same range. However, even with an 18-W charger, some users face issues while charging their iPhone 11 Pro. The most common issues are as follows.

  • The iPhone 11 Pro charges slowly or not at all.
  • The iPhone is not charging beyond 80 %.
  • An alert that shows that the accessory you are using to charge the iPhone is not certified or supported

These are the most reported issues for an iPhone 11 Pro with faulty charging. You may try some home fixes that may resolve the issues.

Try changing the wall adapter or cable.

Check if there is no debris or dirt in both the charging dock and the charging adapter.

Make sure the USB is connected firmly on both ends.

Check the charging adapter or the Lightning cable for visible signs of damage. Example: bent pin, loose cable, etc.

If you have iOS 14 or above, make sure you uncheck the “optimized battery charging” option to make sure it charges beyond 80 %.

To disable it, go to Settings > Battery > Battery Health > Optimized Battery Charging.

Make sure you have no damage in your charging dock if an unsupported device warning shows.

If none of the fixes seem to work for resolving your iPhone 11 Pro charging issues. You may need to get it looked at by professionals. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who have expertise in resolving issues regarding iPhones. What are the common iPhone 6 problems we fix?

Battery draining fast or shutting down suddenly

Every iPhone 6 in use in 2026 is running a battery that is at minimum 10–12 years old. Battery replacement takes 30 minutes and is the single best-value repair for this device. We replace approximately iPhone 6 batteries every month across our Dhaka branches. Cracked or unresponsive screen

The iPhone 6's 4.7-inch Retina HD IPS LCD display is still a sharp, usable panel — worth replacing rather than tolerating cracks or dead touch zones. We fit a full display assembly (digitizer, LCD, and frame together) and run a post-repair touch calibration and colour check before handing the phone back. [ iPhone 6 screen replacement]

Not charging or charging only at an angle

The Lightning port on the iPhone 6 collects dust and pocket lint over years of use — often what feels like a charging fault is simply a blocked port. During every free diagnosis, our technicians clean the port first before recommending a flex cable replacement. If cleaning resolves it, you pay nothing. [→ iPhone 6 charging issues]

Home button not working or Touch ID failing

The physical home button on the iPhone 6 is a mechanical component that wears down over time — it can become stiff, stop clicking, or stop registering presses entirely. Touch ID fingerprint recognition can also stop working after the button degrades or following an unofficial repair elsewhere that broke the pairing between the button and the logic board. iFixit BD replaces the home button assembly and restores Touch ID function where the pairing is intact. Liquid damage

The iPhone 6 has zero water resistance — there is no IP rating on this model. Liquid that enters the chassis reaches the A8 logic board within seconds and begins corroding metal traces immediately. If your iPhone 6 got wet, power it off and bring it to iFixit BD the same day. We perform ultrasonic board cleaning using professional ultrasonic equipment and isopropyl alcohol (90%+) to remove corrosive mineral deposits before they cause permanent component failure. iPhone 6 liquid damage repair]

data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 12 offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

The iPhone has taken in some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss

A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity

It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try these following steps and see if it works for you

Force Restart your iPhone 12

(Press volume up (+) and then quickly press volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 12 power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work, for you. You might have an issue that needs the touch of a professional iPhone technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in fixing iPhones. ifixit bd is a prominent iPhone servicing center that is located in 4 locations around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

We offer service benefits for Apple logo issues for your iPhone 12. Not only will we provide the best available service for you, but you can also avail yourself.

Free Diagnostics to see what's wrong with your iPhone

We understand how important your iPhone is to you, so to ensure top-notch quality we try to provide your servicing needs with original apple parts and accessories. We do not compromise with our quality. So, visit your nearest ifixit bd service point to avail the best iPhone servicing available to you for your iPhone 12 “Stuck on apple logo” issue or any other iPhone issues for that matter.

Battery draining fast or shutting down suddenly

During every free diagnosis, our technicians clean the port first before recommending a flex cable replacement. If cleaning resolves it, you pay nothing. [→ iPhone 6 charging issues]

Home button not working or Touch ID failing

The physical home button on the iPhone 6 is a mechanical component that wears down over time — it can become stiff, stop clicking, or stop registering presses entirely. Touch ID fingerprint recognition can also stop working after the button degrades or following an unofficial repair elsewhere that broke the pairing between the button and the logic board. iFixit BD replaces the home button assembly and restores Touch ID function where the pairing is intact.   • Make sure you do not have the “optimized battery charging” option checked on your iPhone X. if you do have it make sure to disable it to charge your phone past 80%.
  • Disable optimized Charging in here: Settings > Battery > Battery Health.

Note: This option is only available on iOS 13 or later updates.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water. However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth

Never charge your phone untill you have made sure it is completely dry

You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth. If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers. data.title: Power Issue
data.description:
This correlation between the power button and the battery is unavoidable for the perfect operation of the iPhone. The iPhone has been designed to maintain it. However, many users have complained about issues regarding issues in their power supply and other power-related errors in their iPhones.

These power issues include:

Phone does not turn on

The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked-out phone. Therefore you can not determine the problem

iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.

iPhone doesn’t charge. It is stuck on the battery percentage you left it to charge on.

Can’t use the iPhone without keeping it on a constant power supply (eg: Connected to a wall adapter or power bank etc.

These frustrating problems are however the most common issues found on iPhone 14. There are some widely renowned DIY (Do It Yourself) fixes available on the internet which may help with the issue on your device. Such as...

Force restart your iPhone ( Press Volume up (+) and quickly press volume down (-) and then quickly press the power button to complete the restart process)

Check your Lightning cable and adapter to see if they are functioning properly

Check if there is any debris on the iPhone 14 charging porthole

Limit background processes by stopping background app refresh

Try charging for 20 minutes while keeping your phone switched off

Sometimes excessive battery drain can happen due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version

If none of these methods work to resolve the issue on your smartphone, you might need to get it checked by professional technicians. ifixit bd is an iPhone servicing center located around 4 different service points around Dhaka, Bangladesh. data.title: Mic Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 13 Pro Max offers a set of microphones to ensure your iPhone makes the best out of the audio inputs it receives. The iPhone offers the users a dual speaker and microphone to ensure the best listening experience for their users. However, it is often reported by iPhone 13 Pro Max users that, they are getting trouble regarding the microphones in their phones. The most common issues reported in Apple’s user community forum and other blogs are:

Low or unclear voice sound in voice calls/ voice memos.

Low or unclear voice in Facetime, skype, or video recording.

Muffled or cracked sound while recording/calling using the mic.

Siri doesn’t work/ can’t hear me/ can’t pick up commands.

The iPhone 13 Pro Max has at least 3 different microphones in different places for the phone for different purposes

The bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls

One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri

The one in the back of your in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video.

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any of the one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

Make sure if you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes.

Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there.

Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works

If the mic works in voice memo make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone 13 Pro Max go to Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone. If none of the fixes work for you, you may need it to be looked at by professional technicians. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving issues in your iPhone 13 Pro Max. ifixit bd has multiple service points located in Dhaka, Bangladesh. We offer quick service for your ease of access. On top of that, we provide a 30-days service warranty for applicable services provided by us.

Screen cracking more easily due to the ultra-thin chassis

  • Checking the ringer switch to see if it is on the sound mode
  • Restarting Your Phone
  • Disabling your Bluetooth in the iPhone 8 plus
  • Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode
  • Check sound notification settings and try turning noise cancellation off.
  • Try using headphones and check if the sounds come okay in headphones.

data.title: Touch Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 12 offers a haptic touch system instead of a 3D touch system that was available in the previous versions of the iPhones. The new haptic touch does not require assessing the strength of users like it needed to in the 3D touch system. Instead, it measures the area of your fingertips to decide the strength and length of the touch input provided by the user. This haptic touch is also a way to ensure your touch works for a long time. However, you just might face an issue anytime soon on your iPhone 12 regarding your phone’s touch.

The most common issues faced by the users that are reported in the iPhone 12 users community forum are as follows:

Too sensitive screen/screen response intermittently (means responses without the user having to input or auto touch)

Touchscreen in your iPhone does not respond at all

Delayed Touch issue

Touch doesn’t respond after dropping from hand. (Everything else seems to work fine)

There are some fixes you might try to see if any of them work for your phone. Those are the following listed below:

Make sure your touch screen protector doesn’t interfere with the proper operation

Make sure there’s no internal/external damage (cracking or shattering glass)

Disconnecting your USB-lightning port to check if it works

If your phone is above normal temperature wait for it to cool down and then try again

Restart your device

If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get your iPhone checked by professional technicians. data.description:
The new iPhone 14 Pro Max offers one of the best displays of high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both the back and the front. However, not all damage to the display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone 13 Pro Max have reported a sudden black screen with no prior damage history. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 14 Pro Max is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone is running okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. The phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

The phone's display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus) 

The phone has calls and notifications but doesn’t show anything on display

iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone. (Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen) 

Connect the lightning cable and charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone

UNCONVENTIONAL: Press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect to any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended, however, it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issues. It might be risky for any layman.

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving no light-on-display issues on your iPhone 14 Pro Max. We are a service center that operates based on 4 different and convenient points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

What are the common iPhone 14 Pro Max problems we fix?

Battery capacity declining — Always-On Display drains it faster

The Always-On Display on the iPhone 14 Pro Max runs the screen at a low refresh rate continuously — a useful feature that adds constant background battery drain. Combined with natural cell degradation over two years of use, battery replacement is the most common repair we see on this model. iPhone 14 Pro Max battery replacement

Cracked ProMotion OLED with Always-On Display failure

The 6.7-inch ProMotion panel supports always-on functionality via a low-power LTPO state. A screen crack or OLED damage that disables the always-on feature in addition to normal display function is common after a significant drop. We replace the full assembly and verify ProMotion and always-on operation after every repair. iPhone 14 Pro Max screen replacement

The Dynamic Island replaced the notch on the iPhone 14 Pro Max — and houses the TrueDepth sensor cluster. A drop to the front top edge of the phone can damage the sensors around the island cutout, disabling Face ID. iPhone 14 Pro Max Dynamic Island / Face ID repair

48MP main camera blur or focus issues

The 48MP wide camera introduced on the 14 Pro Max produces significantly larger files and higher detail — and is a more complex mechanical system. Drops, OIS misalignment, and flex cable damage all cause blur, autofocus hunting, and camera app instability. iPhone 14 Pro Max camera repair

Lightning port charging slowly or loosely

The iPhone 14 Pro Max uses Lightning — one of the last iPhone Pro Max models with this connector. Lint compaction and physical cable wear cause loose connections and slow or failed charging. We clean first — replacement only when cable is confirmed damaged. iPhone 14 Pro Max charging issues

data.title: Ear Speaker Replacement
data.description:
The earpiece or the top speaker of the iPhone 16 Pro is the most. Because it is used as both an audio playback speaker and the earpiece of your phone while making phone calls. This high level of usage can be a reason to create wear and tear on that speaker very quickly and may cause it to cease functioning properly. If the earpiece/ ear speaker of your iPhone 16 Pro stops working or produces sounds on lower levels you should check some of the factors that might be the reason behind it. Which are:

  • Check if your volume levels are in an optimum range
  • Check if you have a noise-canceling feature on your iPhone turned on. Try turning it off and see if it returns your phone to normal audio levels. Check the settings at Settings > Accessibility > Audio/Visual > Phone Noise Cancelation.
  • Sometimes the speaker may have debris or dirt in it. Causing it to cease properly functioning properly. Cleaning it may also resolve the issue.

If none of the procedures resolve the issue regarding your ear speaker issue, you may need to get it looked at by professionals. Here at Ifixit BD, we have experienced repairmen who specialize in repairing and resolving issues regarding your iPhone 16 Pro. We have service points located in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Boot Loop
data.description:
The iPhone 12 Pro offers the users a new iOS version (iOS 13 upgradable to iOS 14) and updates it forward. Users need to update iOS regularly to maintain the stable and smooth operation of the iPhone. However, sometimes a user may face some unforeseen problems. Like the Boot loop in this instance, where the phone starts and shows the Apple logo. Then goes black and again shows only the apple logo on the screen, the phone can show nothing beyond that.

This issue happens mostly when there is a failed or interrupted software update happens on your phone. Also, other issues may cause your phone to boot loop such as:

Physical Damage (Dropping the phone from your hand, etc.)

The battery connector may have gotten loose or have gone bad.

Hardware Damage.

Improper or failed update that is missing necessary files to get the phone started.

If you think one of the above issues is causing the boot looping error on your phone, you may just try these fixes listed below and see if they work to resolve your issue.

Force Restart Your iPhone 12 Pro

(press the volume up button (+) then release the button. And then quickly press and release the volume down (-) and then hold the power button again until your screen turns black and shows the apple logo)

Check if your iPhone is fully charged or is charging properly.

Connect your iPhone to your computer and try restoring or updating the software through the iTunes application.

If your phone still doesn’t recover from boot looing after trying these fixes, something may have gone wrong which can only be fixed by a professional iPhone technician. This is where ifixit bd comes in, ifixit bd is a prominent iPhone servicing center that has 4 different service points ranging in Dhaka, Bangladesh. We have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing iPhones.

data.title: Mic Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone XS offers a set of microphones to ensure your iPhone makes the best out of the audio inputs it receives. The iPhone offers the users a dual speaker and microphone to ensure the best listening experience for their users. However, it is often reported by iPhone XS users that they are having trouble regarding the microphones in their phones. The most common issues reported in Apple’s user community forum and other blogs are...

  • Low or unclear voice sound in voice calls/voice memos.
  • Low or unclear voice in FaceTime, Skype, or video recording.
  • Muffled or cracked sound while recording/calling using the mic.
  • Siri doesn’t work/can’t hear me/can’t pick up commands.

The iPhone XS has at least 3 different microphones in different places for phones for different purposes.

  • At the bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls.
  • One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri
  • The one in the back of you is in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video.

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY (do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

  • Make sure you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes.
  • Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there.
  • Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works.
  • If the mic works in voice memo, make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone XS.
  • Go to Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone.

If none of the fixes work for you, you may need it to be looked at by professional technicians. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving issues in your iPhone XS.

data.description:
The iPhone 7 Plus offers the users a new iOS version and updates it forward. Users need to update iOS regularly to maintain the stable and smooth operation of the iPhone. However, sometimes a user may face some unforeseen problems. Like the Boot loop in this instance, where the phone starts and shows the apple logo. Then goes black and again shows only the apple logo on the screen, the phone can show nothing beyond that. This issue happens mostly when there is a failed or interrupted software update happens on your phone. Also, other issues may cause your phone to boot loop such as:

  • Physical Damage (Dropping the phone from your hand, etc.)
  • Battery connector may have gotten loose or have gone bad.
  • Hardware Damage.
  • Your Phone is boot looping after a recent screen replacement.
  • Improper or failed update that is missing necessary files to get the phone started.

If you think one of the above issues is causing the boot looping error on your phone, you may just try these fixes listed below and see if they work to resolve your issue.

  • Force Restart Your iPhone 7 plus
  • Check if your iPhone is fully charged or is charging properly.
  • Connect your iPhone to your computer and try restoring or updating the software through the iTunes application.

If your phone still doesn’t recover from boot looing after trying these fixes, something may have gone wrong which can only be fixed by a professional iPhone technician. data.description:
These common issues however can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 6s. To resolve these Apple recommends its iPhone 6s users some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

  • Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache.
  • Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. (requires a restart of the device)
  • Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time. To set up go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network

then:

  • Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier 
  • Insert Username (provided by your carrier)
  • Insert Password (provided by your carrier)
  • Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.
  • Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.
  • Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)
  • Restart your iPhone
  • Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to get checked by a professional technician. data.title: Error Solution
data.description:
Sometimes when you update your iPhone, or when you try to run your phone you may see some sort of black screen with some sort of Error with a number on your iPhone’s screen out of nowhere. These messages with errors and numbers can be seen while booting up the phone or trying to upgrade the ipsw files from iTunes from a pc. These are Error Codes that indicate to the service technicians that a specific part of the iPhone is malfunctioning. These codes are used between professional repair technicians of iPhones to make their jobs easy. They do not need to diagnose the entire iPhone when they see the code. Therefore saves both the customer’s and the tech expert’s time and other resources.

Some of the common error codes seen in the iPhones are as follows:

ERROR(9): This code shows when you are trying to upgrade your iOS through PC on iTunes, but the iTunes app shows an Error code-9. It is a relatable problem with iTunes error code – 4013, 4014, and 4005.

Apple recommends:

  • To check if your iPhone is updated
  • To check if the lightning cable works. (Error code 4013,4014 and 4015 usually indicate this issue)
  • If the update still fails try updating from another pc.
  • Error 1015: This is an issue if you have a jailbroken device (iOS) and apple detects it.
  • Error 69: This is a common issue found in iPhone X and later devices. This issue suggests that there might be some sort of hardware error on your phone, which is repairable, to say the least.
  • Aside from these errors, there are a lot of errors that can occur on your iPhone. These are all listed on Apple’s error solution info pages with possible DIY (Do it yourself) solutions.
  • The whole error code list: https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT201444

However, not all problems can be fixed only by DIY fixes. Some errors might require some handy work around the inner parts of the phone which should be done by a professional iPhone technician. That is where ifixit bd comes in, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving errors in iPhone 8 Plus or any other iPhone devices. ifixit bd is a prominent Apple gadget servicing center based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the SIM tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the SIM tray by putting the ejector pin into the SIM tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the SIM tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the SIM tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver, then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water. However, if your LCI turns red, you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water, here are some basic things you should do:

  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth.
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY.
  • If anything spills on your phone (like oil, etc.), just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.
  • If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your battery or charging port or give you muffled speakers.

Here at ifixit bd, we have professional and dedicated technicians who specialize in fixing the problems in your iPhones. ifixit bd is located in service points across Dhaka, Bangladesh. We at ifixit bd offer our customers quick repair service for their ease of access.

data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone Se 2022 offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

The iPhone has taken some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss

A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity

It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone Se 2022 (Press volume up (+) and then quickly press the volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone Se 2022 power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software. (If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work, for you. You might have an issue that needs the touch of a professional iPhone technician. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

  • Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issue has been resolved
  • Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again
  • Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection
  • Restore the default network connection

(Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > * Enter Passcode * > Confirm)

  • Update your iOS to the latest version available

data.description:
The most common issues with the iPhone 16 charging dock are:

  • The battery charges very slowly
  • iPhone 16 is not charging beyond 80%

  • Make sure your power outlet isn’t faulty
  • If your phone is wet, wait until it is dry to charge your phone
  • Make sure you do not have the “optimized battery charging” option checked on your iPhone 16. if you do have it, make sure to disable it to charge your phone past 80%
  • Disable optimized Charging here: Settings > Battery > Battery Health. Note: This option is only available on iOS 13 or later updates.

data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 14 Plus offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update. This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

The iPhone has taken some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss

A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity

It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 14 Plus

(Press volume up (+) and then quickly press the volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 14 Plus power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work, for you. You might have an issue that needs the touch of a professional iPhone technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in fixing iPhones. ifixit bd is a prominent iPhone servicing center that is located in 4 locations around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.description:
MacBook Air 13 inch M1 battery replacement in Bangladesh

MacBook Air 13 inch M1 battery replacement is the process of taking out the old, worn-down battery from a MacBook Air A2337 (Late 2020) and fitting a new MacBook Air 13 Inch M1 Battery in its place. Signs that the battery needs replacing include macOS showing "Service Recommended," the laptop dying faster than normal, and the battery swelling up inside the body. In Bangladesh, the total repair cost ranges from 8,000 BDT to 14,000 BDT depending on the battery quality and the repair center. iFixit BD one of the top repair centers in Dhaka— finish the battery swap in 30 minutes to 2 hours and give a warranty of 3 months to 12 months.

What is MacBook Air 13 inch M1 battery replacement?

MacBook Air 13 inch M1 battery replacement is the repair process of removing the old built-in battery from a MacBook Air A2337 (Late 2020) and installing a new A2389 battery in its place. The MacBook Air M1 uses a built-in A2389 battery — this battery is glued firmly inside the laptop body and cannot be taken out by the user. A trained technician uses special tools to safely remove the old battery and fit a new one.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone 12 Pro Max is a standard IP68 rated, dust and water-resistant phone. This means it can resist dust and water coming in up to a certain level. However, it is not completely immune to water getting inside the iPhone and damaging it. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth

You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there

NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth

If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers.

data.description:
The iPhone 12 Pro Max offers the users a new iOS version (iOS 13 upgradable to iOS 14) and updates it forward. Users need to update iOS regularly to maintain the stable and smooth operation of the iPhone. However, sometimes a user may face some unforeseen problems. Like the Boot loop in this instance, where the phone starts and shows the Apple logo. Then goes black and again shows only the apple logo on the screen, the phone can show nothing beyond that.

This issue happens mostly when there is a failed or interrupted software update happens on your phone. Also, other issues may cause your phone to boot loop such as:

Physical Damage (Dropping the phone from your hand, etc.)

The battery connector may have gotten loose or have gone bad.

Hardware Damage.

Improper or failed update that is missing necessary files to get the phone started.

If you think one of the above issues is causing the boot looping error on your phone, you may just try these fixes listed below and see if they work to resolve your issue.

Force Restart Your iPhone 12 Pro Max

(press the volume up button (+) then release the button. And then quickly press and release the volume down (-) and then hold the power button again until your screen turns black and shows the apple logo)

Check if your iPhone is fully charged or is charging properly.

Connect your iPhone to your computer and try restoring or updating the software through the iTunes application.

If your phone still doesn’t recover from boot looing after trying these fixes, something may have gone wrong which can only be fixed by a professional iPhone technician. This is where ifixit bd comes in, ifixit bd is a prominent iPhone servicing center that has 4 different service points ranging in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The new iPhone Se 2022 has a beautiful battery that is optimized for using it for a reasonable amount of time. However, most of the users have complained the iPhone Se 2022 charges very slowly in comparison to other smartphones on the market with almost the same range. The Apple company, recommends that you use an Apple 18-W USB Type-C charging brick if you face a slow charging issue. Which is the default charger with iPhone Se 2022. However, even with an 18-W charger, some users face issues while charging their iPhone Se 2022. The most common issues are as follows:

The iPhone Se 2022 charges slowly or not at all

The iPhone is not charging beyond 80 %

An alert that shows that the accessory you are using to charge the iPhone is not certified or supported

These are the most reported issues for an iPhone Se 2022 with faulty charging. You may try some home fixes that may resolve the issues.

Try changing the wall adapter or cable

Check if there is no debris or dirt in both the charging dock and the charging adapter

Make sure the USB is connected firmly on both ends

Check the charging adapter or the lightning cable for visible signs of damage. Example: Bent pin, loose cable, etc.

if you have iOS 14 or above make sure you uncheck the “optimized battery charging” option to make sure it charges beyond 80 %.To disable it go to: Settings > Battery > Battery Health > Optimized Battery Charging

Make sure you have no damage in your charging dock if unsupported device warning shows.

data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 15 Plus comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

The face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way

Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts

If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all

If your iPhone 15 Plus Face ID problems can’t be categorized and sorted by the above-mentioned issues and fixes, you may just need to take it to an extremely diligent iPhone technician to deal with Face ID issues. data.description:
The iPhone 13 Pro comes with upgraded network connectivity compared to previous iPhone models and supports 5G network connectivity. Despite technological advancements from previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone 13 Pro network connectivity. iPhone 13 Pro gets down to 0 network bars randomly

Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G

Network never reaches the full level

Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company

These common issues, however, can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 13 Pro. To resolve this, Apple recommends its iPhone 13 users some DIY (do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache

Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. -requires a restart of the device

Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.

To set it up, go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network.

then:

Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier

Insert Username (provided by your carrier)

Insert Password (provided by your carrier)

Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.

Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.

Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)

Restart your iPhone

Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to be checked by a professional technician. However, most of the users have complained the iPhone 13 Pro charges very slowly in comparison to other smartphones on the market with almost the same range. An alert that shows that the accessory you are using to charge the iPhone is not certified or supported

Try changing the wall adapter or cable

Check if there is no debris or dirt in both the charging dock and the charging adapter

Make sure the USB is connected firmly on both ends

Check the charging adapter or the lightning cable for visible signs of damage. Example: Bent pin, loose cable, etc.

if you have iOS 14 or above make sure you uncheck the “optimized battery charging” option to make sure it charges beyond 80 %.

To disable it go to: Settings > Battery > Battery Health > Optimized Battery Charging

iPhone 6 repair service in Dhaka, Bangladesh

With 18+ years of experience, 500,000+ devices repaired, and 70+ expert technicians across 4 dedicated branches in Dhaka, iFixit BD is one of Bangladesh's most established iPhone repair centres. We repair every iPhone 6 fault — cracked Retina HD screens, dead batteries, charging port failures, liquid damage, and board-level logic board issues — using both A-grade and Original parts with full pricing transparency. Screen replacement starts from ৳1,800, battery replacement from ৳900, and every repair begins with a free written diagnosis. Most common repairs are completed same-day.

What are the common iPhone 6 problems we fix?

Battery draining fast or shutting down suddenly

Every iPhone 6 in use in 2026 is running a battery that is at minimum 10–12 years old. At that age, lithium-ion cells hold a fraction of their original capacity — you may see 15% drop to 0% with no warning, or the phone shut off at 30%. Battery replacement takes 30 minutes and is the single best-value repair for this device. We replace approximately iPhone 6 batteries every month across our Dhaka branches. [ iPhone 6 battery replacement]

Cracked or unresponsive screen

The iPhone 6's 4.7-inch Retina HD IPS LCD display is still a sharp, usable panel — worth replacing rather than tolerating cracks or dead touch zones. We fit a full display assembly (digitizer, LCD, and frame together) and run a post-repair touch calibration and colour check before handing the phone back. [ iPhone 6 screen replacement]

Not charging or charging only at an angle

The Lightning port on the iPhone 6 collects dust and pocket lint over years of use — often what feels like a charging fault is simply a blocked port. During every free diagnosis, our technicians clean the port first before recommending a flex cable replacement. If cleaning resolves it, you pay nothing. [→ iPhone 6 charging issues]

Home button not working or Touch ID failing

The physical home button on the iPhone 6 is a mechanical component that wears down over time — it can become stiff, stop clicking, or stop registering presses entirely. Touch ID fingerprint recognition can also stop working after the button degrades or following an unofficial repair elsewhere that broke the pairing between the button and the logic board. iFixit BD replaces the home button assembly and restores Touch ID function where the pairing is intact. [ iPhone 6 home button repair]

Liquid damage

The iPhone 6 has zero water resistance — there is no IP rating on this model. Liquid that enters the chassis reaches the A8 logic board within seconds and begins corroding metal traces immediately. If your iPhone 6 got wet, power it off and bring it to iFixit BD the same day. We perform ultrasonic board cleaning using professional ultrasonic equipment and isopropyl alcohol (90%+) to remove corrosive mineral deposits before they cause permanent component failure. iPhone 6 liquid damage repair]

Won't turn on / boot loop / no service

If the iPhone 6 shows no response to the power button, restarts in a continuous loop, or shows no cellular service signal, the problem is at the board level. iFixit BD's micro-soldering lab diagnoses and repairs logic board faults — power management ICs, baseband chip failures, and boot-loop causes — that swap-only repair shops in Bangladesh cannot address. [ iPhone 6 software and boot issues]

You decide — no pressure, no surprise charges after the fact. Board-level micro-soldering lab. Is the iPhone 6 still worth repairing in 2026?

It depends on what the issue is, and iFixit BD will tell you honestly before you spend anything.

Yes, repair is worth it for the most common issues. A battery replacement at ৳900–1,800 costs a fraction of any replacement phone available in Bangladesh today and adds 1–2 years of reliable daily use. The iOS ceiling is a real factor. The iPhone 6 is capped at iOS 12 — Apple no longer issues security updates for this version, and an increasing number of apps have dropped iOS 12 support. For users who rely on banking apps or newer social media features, this is worth knowing before investing in a repair. For users who want a reliable everyday phone for calls, messages, and basic apps, iOS 12 is still functional.

Board-level damage needs an honest conversation. If the A8 logic board has severe liquid corrosion or multiple chip failures, repair costs can approach the resale value of the device. At iFixit BD, we give you a clear cost-vs-value assessment at the diagnosis stage — if repair is not the right answer for your specific situation, we say so.

data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 13 Pro offers its users better optimization and balance in software than previous iPhone models. However, no matter how hard they try, there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning.The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it gets stuck on the boot menu. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

This Stuck on the Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

The iPhone has caused some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

Update disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss

A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity

It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up

These issues, however, can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps to see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 13 Pro

(Press the volume up (+) and then quickly press the volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 13 Pro power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS app to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work for you. You might have an issue that requires the touch of a professional iPhone technician. So, visit your nearest ifixit bd service point to avail the best iPhone servicing available to you for your iPhone 13 Pro “Stuck on apple logo” issue or any other iPhone issue for that matter.

The Lightning port on the iPhone 6 collects dust and pocket lint over years of use — often what feels like a charging fault is simply a blocked port. Home button not working or Touch ID failing

The physical home button on the iPhone 6 is a mechanical component that wears down over time — it can become stiff, stop clicking, or stop registering presses entirely.
